score.method:
Per name:
    mu_ens = m + tilt + a   (tilt = EPS-revision tilt from conviction.py, 2026-10-08)
    m  = options-market part: conviction.py mu_market (T-bill + beta x ERP on the options-implied distribution).
    a  = research alpha = multiplier x w_llm x (r_research - m), where
         r_research = average of the agents' 12M mean return (supervisor ladder) and the reconciled fair value's return,
         w_llm      = the research weight in combine.py (33%),
         multiplier = conviction.py's shrink, clip(t / median t, 0.5, 1) (upper clip 2 until Kilian's 2026-10-20 card 'Cap at 1x'), t = |agents vs market| / sqrt(disp^2 + 10%^2).
    Open supervisor flags halve a; a thesis-break or fact-check flag blocks the name (score shown, no buy).
    score = gain in book Sharpe at the name's best share count (0..cap, exhaustive) against the live book at cost plus the
            committed buys (portfolio.json sharpe_combo), every name at mu_ens, riskcal correlations, same Sharpe formula as
            allocate.py (invested dollars, cash left out). Caps: stop budget, cash after committed
            buys. Would buy = score > 0 and a free name slot (cap 10).

portfolio.method:
Since 2026-09-29 (Kilian: "solve as one portfolio against the factor model") all candidates are sized together:
    maximize sum_i w_i (mu_i - rf) - (gamma/2) w' Sigma w,   gamma = 4 (quarter Kelly),
with w the share of total wealth (current account + new cash), mu_i the conviction-adjusted 1Y expected return
(conviction.py; the options market's part at quarter Kelly, the research part scaled 0.5x-2x), and
Sigma_ij = rho_ij s_i s_j: s_i the s.d. of the name's final blended 1Y distribution (result.json, the same one that sets
target, TP and SL), rho_ij from the Risk Prism factor model recalibrated to the option market (riskcal.py), else 2Y
realized correlation shrunk toward the pool average. Constraints per name, the smallest binding:
  - Gate: no buy unless the NTM target (blended median) is above the last price ('target_above_last').
  - Stop budget: a stop-out at the SL may cost at most stop_budget_share_of_wealth of total wealth (data/review_settings.json;
    5% since Kilian 2026-09-29, was 2%): w <= budget / ((spot - SL) / spot).
  - The supervisor's sizing.max_weight_pct, if given, and a 20% single-name ceiling.
  - Index fund (review_settings index_fund, SPY since Kilian 2026-09-29): an S&P 500 fund is always a candidate, expected
    to earn the risk-free rate plus the measured 7.69% equity premium with its option-implied vol; no stop, supervisor or conviction caps, only
    its own max_weight. It soaks up cash the stock picks leave idle, sized against them in the same solve.
  - Kelly split (Kilian 2026-09-29): the options-implied part of each expected return is sized at market_kelly_fraction
    (half Kelly), the research part at quarter Kelly; done by solving with mu_solve = rf + MKF*gamma*(m - rf) + alpha.
    Reported expected returns are the true mu, not mu_solve.
  - Conviction rubric: removed 2026-11-09 (Kilian "get rid of conviction rubric"; its gate was off since 2026-10-21).
    No conviction label, no book dP, no conviction gate; the Sharpe tests and the gates below decide buys.
  - Driver model (Kilian 2026-11-02 "im not buying anything without one + a memo", 2026-11-04): no buy and no staged
    new-name tranche unless the research round behind the target has a driver-led set (gate 'no_driver_model').
  - Research after the print (2026-11-04): no buy unless the research is dated on or after the name's last earnings print
    (last_print.py: earnings_miss.json dates, a passed next-report date, the newest SEC 8-K Item 2.02); unknown = no buy
    (gate 'research_before_print').
  - Big-miss block (Kilian 2026-10-19 card 'Add flag'): no buy, and a staged new name's buy pauses, for 6 months after a
    big earnings miss (earnings_miss.py -> data/earnings_miss.json; gate 'big_miss_block').
  - Held names (Kilian 2026-10-19 15:21Z, SIZING = 'max_sharpe'): review.py sizes them to Sharpe-optimal (tangency)
    targets on mu_eff, scaled to the total this rule would hold; here they stay fixed and a new name must still raise
    the book's Sharpe (Sharpe test below).
  - AI cap (Kilian 2026-11-05 cards 'Named list plus a rule' and '50% of stocks, buys only'; ai_cap.py): AI names (named
    list, watchlist semis, semis_ai loading >= 0.3 or AI/DC revenue >= 25%) at most 50% of the money in stocks, held at
    market value plus today's buys. One linear group constraint in the joint solve, sum_AI w <= 0.5 sum w, through its
    Lagrange multiplier (ai_cap.solve_capped); the whole-share and Sharpe-test steps keep it. Freed weight goes to the
    next-best non-AI name or cash. If the held book is already over, new AI names get no buy; nothing is trimmed (gate 'ai_cap').
Across the book: total buys <= cash. An optional industry limit (max_industry_risk_share; null = off, Kilian removed
the 40% limit 2026-09-29) caps any one Risk Prism industry's share of the book's variance. Held names (holdings mode) stay fixed at
their current weight; review.py decides trims and adds for those. Whole shares: rounded down, then single shares added
back while they raise the objective and fit the cash and limits. The rest stays in cash.
runs/DATE/portfolio.json carries the book's expected return, volatility (recalibrated model, plus the raw model and the
option market's own view), Sharpe, beta, factor and industry risk shares.
portfolio.calibration_method:
LIVE since 2026-11-02 (Kilian's pick, after the out-of-sample test in risk/model_study/report.md and the GICS
sub-industry comparison in risk/finer_model/report.md). Sizing takes only rho_ij from here; each name's vol comes from its
own 1Y distribution. Correlations come from:
  1. Risk Prism exposures and factor returns, with the factor covariance re-estimated from weekly factor returns
     (exponentially weighted, half-life 26 weeks; no scale-up to implied vol).
  2. Two extra semis factors, each the equal-weight average residual of a basket: AI chips and chip equipment, and analog
     chips. Each name's loadings come from a ridge regression of its weekly residual on the basket factors (half-life 52 weeks,
     prior worth 26 weeks at loading 0, the name left out of its own basket).
  3. Specific risk from each name's own weekly residuals (half-life 26 weeks; no top-up to implied or realized vol).
     Names with under 26 weeks of residuals use Risk Prism's specific x 1.2 (our weekly residual vols run ~1.2x theirs).
  4. The sample correlation of weekly returns blended in: rho = d x model + (1 - d) x sample, with d from the Ledoit-Wolf
     fixed-target rule (sampling noise / distance). 104 weeks where both names have them, else 52, else the model alone.
Replaced (backup riskcal.py.bak-v2_1102): Risk Prism with each name's specific risk topped up to its 1Y implied vol.
Usage: M = riskcal.load(DATE, syms)  -> riskcalc.Model subclass; M.corr/M.cov use the blend,
M.risk/M.beta_spy keep the factor structure (reporting only). M.calib records the market's implied vol for reference.

tax_assumptions._tax_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: taxable account; ~$20,000 internship wages in 2026 plus realized gains; claimed as a dependent by a parent living in CA; full-time student under 24 living in CT. Assumed (not confirmed): domicile stays CA (a student living away at school keeps the parents' domicile, FTB Pub 1031), CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode so CT does not tax investment income; kiddie tax applies (earned income not more than half of his support). tax_assumptions._other_unearned_note: Dividends etc. this year (rough: GOOGL + META dividends). Counts toward the kiddie-tax threshold.
tax_assumptions._kiddie_note: Unearned income above $2,700 (2 x $1,350, Rev. Proc. 2025-32) is taxed at the parent's rate, federal (Form 8615) and CA (FTB 3800). Applies to a full-time student 19-23 whose earned income is not more than half of his own support.
tax_assumptions._parent_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: parent in NYC, 37% federal bracket. Parent's NY/NYC rates do not apply to Kilian's gains (no NY kiddie tax under Form 8615).
tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. Net losses offset gains; up to $3,000 deducts at the own short-term rate. Bracket mode (mode 'brackets') still holds the CA schedule and is not updated.
tax_assumptions._short_term_all_note: Kilian 2026-10-28 card 'Assume short-term on all' (thread 'Fix AMAT target vs sell mismatch'): every holding is assumed sold within the year at the short-term rate, so a trim only pays the same tax H years sooner; band per year = q tau (1 - (1+d)^-H) / H + spread / T. Overrides lot_aware_horizon; false restores it.
tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. Long-term lots keep the T-year rule (years_until_you_would_otherwise_sell, future_rate_on_deferred_gains, Claude defaults 2026-09-28). false restores the T-year rule for every lot.

industrials.theme: LTL freight volume inflection after a 3-year freight recession
industrials.evidence: Saia Q2 2026 (Jul 30): tonnage/workday +8.4%, shipments +4.4%, contract renewals +10.7%, EPS +31%, yet stock -12% on a Q3 margin guide; Saia July and August 2026 volumes above 2025 (Simply Wall St, Sep 16). XPO August tonnage/day +3.7% YoY (8-K, Sep 3). FedEx Freight 10-K (Aug 5) still guides to industrial softness through CY2026, so consensus is not yet positioned for recovery. ISM manufacturing 54.5 in Sep, new orders 55.3 (First Trust, Oct 1).

industrials.theme: Commercial aerospace production ramp and engine aftermarket (LEAP shop visits)
industrials.evidence: Boeing moving 737 from 42 to 47/month with FAA concurrence and opened a fourth line in July 2026 (10-Q Q2 2026; CEO May 27). Airbus at 475 deliveries Jan-Aug vs 434, targeting 870 for 2026. Metalworking machinery orders +31.9% YTD, driven largely by aerospace (May 2026). Aftermarket names derated anyway: SARO -41% from its high despite a beat-and-raise.

industrials.theme: Data center power equipment (gensets, power pods, switchgear, fiber)
industrials.evidence: Leaders (VRT, GEV, ETN, PWR) are on the watchlist and heavily owned. But second-derivative names are de-rating while their 2027 backlog builds: Generac's data center backlog is $1.6B, $1.35B of it for 2027 delivery, against ~$450M of 2026 data center revenue. Regal Rexnord has ~$735M of E-Pod orders shipping from early 2027. Dycom's backlog is $12.2B (+53%). Several AI-infrastructure names are well below their 2026 highs (Nasdaq, Sep 4).

industrials.theme: Fiber build-out: BEAD broadband plus hyperscaler long-haul and middle-mile
industrials.evidence: Dycom: BEAD construction starts 'in earnest' in calendar 2027. It has over $1B of contracted long-haul/middle-mile backlog and expects 'marked acceleration' of industry activity in CY2027 (Q2 FY27 call, Aug 26, 2026). The stock fell 52% from its high on a soft Q3 guide and a $150M wireless deferral.

industrials.theme: IEEPA tariff refunds and input-cost inflation
industrials.evidence: Refunds of IEEPA tariffs are flowing into 2026 earnings: RRX guide includes $0.57/sh, GNRC EBITDA margin +~150bp. The market strips these out as one-offs, which flatters 2026 multiples. ISM prices paid jumped to 77.9 in September (First Trust, Oct 1), and supplier deliveries are stretched by AI demand for electrical parts and by Middle East shipping disruption.

CNH Q2 2026 (Aug 3): management says this is the trough (dealer inventory normalised, fleets ageing) but sees no evidence yet of a sustained recovery. NA tractors -16/-17% in Q2. 2026 EPS guide is $0.41-0.46, so estimates are not yet rising. Deere is already +46% off its low. Too early to pick: no estimate support.

industrials.theme: Residential HVAC, pool and housing weakness
industrials.evidence: RRX's PES segment fell 6.6% organically on residential HVAC and pool (Aug 5). Generac residential sales -2% in Q2. This is a known drag and is in the price of mixed names.

tech.theme: Hyperscaler AI capex still rising into 2027
tech.evidence: A July 2026 report has the largest cloud operators' combined 2026 capex up ~89% y/y to ~$710B (prior +72%); BofA (Arya) sees global cloud/AI infrastructure capex approaching $1.5T by 2027; TSMC lifted 2026 capex to $60-64B (Jul 2026). The GPU/custom-silicon leaders already price this in (MRVL at ~65x FY1/38x FY2 EPS, +287% off its 52w low; CIEN ~38x FY27). Sources: finance.yahoo.com semis $1.3T article (2026); news.ainauten.com chip-capex-doubt story (Jul 2026).

tech.theme: Value migrating to rack-scale integration and data-center power (EMS/ODM)
tech.evidence: Flex's Cloud and Power Infrastructure unit is guided to grow 65-75% in FY27 (Jul 29, 2026 call) and Flex sold $2.0B of preferred in it (Axiom) at a $37.5B EV on 2026-10-05, vs Flex's own EV of ~$46.6B. Sanmina's ZT Systems (bought from AMD Oct 2025) runs at a $5-6B annual rate, and management says FY27 revenue will exceed $16B. Both stocks sit 25-30% below their June 2026 highs even though guidance went up, so the market has not yet repriced them for this growth.

tech.theme: Advanced packaging, HBM and silicon photonics/optical interconnect
tech.evidence: Onto raised its 2026 advanced-packaging growth outlook to ~80% from 50%, has a >$1B backlog and won a >$200M Dragonfly order from one OSAT for 2027 delivery (Aug 6, 2026). Amkor expects advanced-packaging revenue to triple in 2026. GlobalFoundries' photonics-led data-center segment grew 62% y/y and is targeted to double in 2026, with a $1B run-rate exiting 2028. Semtech guides Q3 FY27 revenue +20% q/q on data-center ACC/LPO.

Gartner projects 2026 DRAM/NAND prices +125%/+234%, with relief not until late 2027. UBS sees DRAM undersupplied until at least 2Q28 (streetinsider, 2026). SNDK is +1183% on 12-1 momentum and WDC/MU have already re-rated. The second-order effect is negative for phone and PC demand: GFS guides its mobile segment down low-teens in 2026 and Qualcomm's China OEM demand is weak.

tech.theme: Semis volatility: AI-capex durability doubts and China equipment
tech.evidence: In late July 2026 the SOX fell into a bear market on AI-spend durability doubts and reports of Chinese state-backed tool production. KLAC fell >6% despite a beat (Jul 28-29, 2026; quiverquant, sentisense), GFS fell 34% from Jun 22 to Jul 21 (tickeron) and ONTO fell ~44% from its June high to its July low. Estimates kept rising through that selloff, which is where today's entry points come from.

tech.theme: Software: AI-agent seat-compression scare, then rebound to usage-priced names
tech.evidence: IGV fell ~30% in early 2026 on the 'SaaSpocalypse' (seat-based pricing fears), then rose ~42% from its April low by Jun 3 (Reuters via finance.yahoo.com, 2026-06-03). Security, observability and communications names have since run hard (OKTA +264%, CRWD +189%, TWLO +148%, NET +117% over 6 months) and now mostly trade above their average analyst targets, so I took no software picks. ideas.summary: Materials research is paused this week, so only the industrials and tech scouts were ranked. The themes were 2027 data-center power and rack-integration backlogs being valued at compressed multiples (GNRC, RRX, FLEX, SANM), a de-rated fiber/BEAD build (DY), the LTL freight inflection (SAIA) and AI packaging/photonics (ONTO, GFS, SMTC). The picks for a screen are GNRC (industrials, 26): consensus 2027 EPS +34% and revenue +32%, estimates up sharply since Q2 while the stock sits 24% below its high at ~17x 2027. FLEX (tech, 25) has a third-party $37.5B Axiom mark, EPS +43%/+50%, and spin and investor-day catalysts within six months. Both lean on data-center power, so they overlap VST and each other. DY (25, the cheapest at ~13x FY28) was the close alternative but lost on the one-per-sector rule, and SARO passed the defense check (military 17.8% of revenue) but has slower growth.

ideas.name: Generac Holdings Inc.
ideas.thesis: Data-center generators turn Generac from a residential-standby cyclical into a growth story: about $1.35B of its ~$1.6B data-center backlog ships in 2027, against about $450M of data-center revenue in 2026. A second hyperscale agreement, which management expects to be at least as large as the first, is not yet in backlog. Consensus now has revenue +32% and EPS +34% in 2027, yet the stock trades at ~17x 2027 EPS.
ideas.why_now: Q2 2026 (Jul 29): sales +11%, about $1B of new data-center orders in ~90 days, and the C&I and margin guides were raised. Estimates have moved up a lot since then: FY26 EPS went from ~$8.43 before Q2 to $9.69, and FY27 from ~$10.11 to $12.97. The stock is 24% below its high at $224.6, so the multiple has compressed while the numbers rose.

tax_assumptions._ignore_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: ignore taxes for now (he has money set aside for the liability). Set false to use the tax facts below.
tax_assumptions._future_note: Combined rate you'd expect on today's embedded gains when you'd otherwise sell (15% federal + ~6% state once working). Drives the sell cost and the gain-harvest suggestion.
tax_assumptions._tax_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: taxable account; ~$20,000 internship wages in 2026 plus realized gains; claimed as a dependent by a parent living in CA; full-time student under 24 living in CT. Assumed (not confirmed): domicile stays CA (a student living away at school keeps the parents' domicile, FTB Pub 1031), CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode so CT does not tax investment income; kiddie tax applies (earned income not more than half of his support). Federal 2026 figures from IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32; CA brackets are 2025 (FTB Tax News Oct 2025), 2026's not published yet.
tax_assumptions._other_unearned_note: Dividends etc. this year (rough: GOOGL + META dividends). Counts toward the kiddie-tax threshold.
tax_assumptions._kiddie_note: Unearned income above $2,700 (2 x $1,350, Rev. Proc. 2025-32) is taxed at the parent's rate, federal (Form 8615) and CA (FTB 3800). Applies to a full-time student 19-23 whose earned income is not more than half of his own support.
tax_assumptions._parent_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: parent in NYC, 37% federal bracket. Parent's NY/NYC rates do not apply to Kilian's gains (no NY kiddie tax under Form 8615).
tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. Net losses offset gains; up to $3,000 deducts at the own short-term rate. Bracket mode (mode 'brackets') still holds the CA schedule and is not updated.
tax_assumptions._short_term_all_note: Kilian 2026-10-28 card 'Assume short-term on all' (thread 'Fix AMAT target vs sell mismatch'): every holding is assumed sold within the year at the short-term rate, so a trim only pays the same tax H years sooner; band per year = q tau (1 - (1+d)^-H) / H + spread / T. Overrides lot_aware_horizon; false restores it.
tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. Long-term lots keep the T-year rule (years_until_you_would_otherwise_sell, future_rate_on_deferred_gains, Claude defaults 2026-09-28). false restores the T-year rule for every lot.

agents.reasoning: Round 2 keeps the round-1 primary-document build and fixes what the supervisor established: (1) the DOJ/40-state False Claims Act settlement is final ($348.7M + $35.5M, CA AG 2026-09-21) -> p=1, -$345M after tax; (2) the 2026-08-20 8-K says ~12,700 infants remain AFTER the deal (round 1 subtracted 2,000 wrongly) -> NEC remaining -$875M; (3) the 2026-10-21 Nutrition separation (8-K: tax-free, by end-2027) -> -$320M one-time cash and a 10% ladder branch where the distribution precedes 2027-10-20 and the quote falls ~$10 (Abbott's AbbVie spin, announced Oct-2011, completed 2013-01-01, finished at the end of its target year); (4) CMS CGM competitive bidding (awards 2027) priced into FY28 Diabetes growth and the multiple; (5) P/E re-based on the 11-peer median 18.8x ex-ISRG, set at 17.5x (supervisor 17.0x: I keep a smaller discount because ABT's ~9.3% EPS growth equals the peer median and the spin removes the lowest-multiple segment); (6) SOTP weight cut to 0.20 (kept, not zero, because the spin makes the parts' separate pricing concrete). From the call transcript: diabetes low-to-mid single digit for several quarters (Diabetes FY27/28 5.0/5.5% vs 7.5/7.5%), EP ~20% in Q4 (Other MD FY27 7.0%), Cancer Dx already at a high-teens margin (17/19% vs 14/17%), 2027 sales growth 'pretty similar' (~5.9% pro forma organic in the build). EPS FY27 $5.99 / FY28 $6.55 (consensus $6.08/$6.74, -1.5%/-2.8%). Fair value $110.82 (from $116.93), +13% vs ~$98.4. Ladder: 60% scenario mix (bear $79 / base $111 / bull $133, 25/55/20, within-scenario sigma 0.16) + 40% lognormal around ~$102 (start $98.4 plus drift, sigma 0.27), then 10% spin branch scaled by 0.91: median ~$102.5, P(>= $102) ~0.51, P(>= $138) ~0.11, P(< $82) ~0.21. No option data used; research limited to ~8 follow-ups.

CEO on the Q3 call: diabetes low-to-mid single digit for the next several quarters, so FY2027 Diabetes +4% (was +5%); EP +15% (Volt PFA from ~1% US share per Qsight, Q4 EP ~20% per call); other +6%. FY2028: Diabetes +3.5% (Libre Duo and payer formulary wins less ~2pt from Medicare competitive-bid pricing effective by 2028-01-01, CMS/DLA Piper), EP +13%, other +6%: (9.05x3.5% + 3.91x13% + 11.87x6%) / 24.85 = (0.317 + 0.508 + 0.712) / 24.85 = 6.2%. Margin 34.8% / 35.1% (round 1: 35.0% / 35.3%) as slower CGM, the highest-margin franchise, gives less operating leverage.

memo.title: ABT: Long, hold 16 sh and size the add on tonight's re-mark. Q3 cut the growth guide but kept EPS; research target (12m) $107.79 at 17x, target $110.95
memo.call_reason: The published target ($110.95) and the research target (12m) of $107.79 are above the $102.45 pre-print close, with P(gain) 0.6116 and sizing confidence medium. The edge is modest: the supervisor's confidence is low and it claims no directional edge.
memo.one_liner: Q3 held the earnings line: adj. EPS $1.42 and the FY2026 $5.50-5.55 midpoint reaffirmed. It cut the growth line: comparable growth ~6.0%, diabetes low-to-mid single digit, and a Nutrition spin by end-2027. At 17.0x a below-consensus ~$6.43 NTM EPS, net of ~$2.7B of litigation and separation cash, ABT is worth $107.79 (+9.6% vs the $98.36 post-print quote, derived: 107.79 / 98.36 - 1), so we keep the 16 sh @ $102.80 and stage the second tranche, which tonight's post-print re-mark sizes (+18 sh on the pre-print plan).

thesis.point: The print cut growth, not earnings, and our EPS already sits below the street.
thesis.evidence: Q3 adj. EPS $1.42 (+9.2%) on $13,013M sales (+7.0% comparable). The FY2026 adj. EPS midpoint was reaffirmed and the range narrowed to $5.50-5.55, and Q4 is guided to $1.62-1.67. The comparable-growth guide fell to ~6.0% (prior memo: 6.5-7.5%). Our horizon NTM adj. EPS of ~$6.43 (supervisor build) comes from that guide: FY2027 ~$6.06 and FY2028 ~$6.52, 0.3% and 3.2% under the pre-print Zacks consensus of $6.08 / $6.74 (supervisor figures on unrounded EPS; derived on the rounded figures: 6.06 / 6.08 - 1 = -0.3%, 6.52 / 6.74 - 1 = -3.3%), and 2.7% under a horizon-NTM consensus of ~$6.61 (derived: ~0.2 x $6.08 + ~0.8 x $6.74 = $6.61; 6.43 / 6.61 - 1 = -2.7%). Street cuts after the guide change should mostly converge toward our numbers, not below them.

thesis.point: The valuation needs no re-rating. We price 17.0x, which keeps a ~7% discount to peers and is only ~3% above today's multiple (derived: 17.0 / 18.2 - 1 = -6.6%; 17.0 / 16.5 - 1 = +3.0%).
thesis.evidence: On one calendar NTM window (2026-10-21 to 2027-10-20), ABT trades at 16.5x against an 18.2x median for 11 peers (supervisor rebase, derived: ABT $98.36 / (0.197 x $5.53 + 0.803 x $6.08 = $5.97) = 16.5x). The P/E leg uses 17.0x and the EV/EBITDA leg 13.3x, which is ABT's own multiple today (derived: EV ~$198.6B / ~$14.88B NTM adj. EBITDA in the build = 13.35x). The discount persists through the horizon for three reasons: Nutrition plus EPD are ~22% of FY2027 segment operating earnings in the reconciled build (derived: (1,621 + 1,481) / 14,277 = 21.7%; FY2025 10-K actual (1,558 + 1,290) / 11,800 = 24.1%) at staples/generics multiples until a spin that most likely lands after 2027-10-20, CGM growth is slower and Medicare bidding pricing starts ~2028, and ~12,700 NEC infants are still pending. The 17.0x / 13.3x multiple was chosen on the 2026-10-21 decision card over the 18.2x / 14.0x peer median, which would give $115.00 (supervisor).

thesis.point: The known liabilities are now sized and deducted. The Nutrition separation is value-neutral, and any re-rating it brings is upside we do not count.
thesis.evidence: The research target (12m) deducts ~$2.67B after tax (derived: 520 + 350 + 750 + 150 + 600 + 300 = $2,670M): the ~$670M NEC deal (-$520M), the $384.2M DOJ/states settlement (-$350M), the ~12,700 remaining NEC infants (-$750M, supervisor estimate; derived: ~$970M pre-tax / ~12,700 = ~$76k per infant, ~2x the August deal's ~$35k = (~$670M - ~$600M Gill) / ~2,000), Libre 3 recall claims (-$300M x 0.5), specified-items cash (-$600M) and separation costs (-$300M). The 8-K describes a distribution of a ~$8.5B-sales Nutrition company, intended to qualify as tax-free, completion expected by end-2027, with a combined dividend equal to Abbott's. We carry a 10% chance that it distributes before 2027-10-20, which moves only the quote (~$9 lower on a distribution of equal value; derived by the supervisor as the mean of two agent estimates, ($10.7 + $7.35) / 2 = ~$9.0).

memo.variant_view: The variant view is small, and it points the other way from the street. Our $110.95 target and $107.79 research target (12m) sit well below the sell-side: mean $120.72, median $120, 28 analysts, Strong Buy, as of 2026-10-16 before the print, given zero weight. We think the street is stale. Pre-print FY2027/FY2028 consensus of $6.08 / $6.74 predates the cut to ~6.0% comparable growth, diabetes at low-to-mid single digit 'for the next few quarters', and EP guided to ~20% in Q4, and our build is already 0.3% / 3.2% below it. Against the options market we are only slightly more constructive: the market-only distribution has a $107.35 median and P(gain) 0.5633, against the published $110.95 and 0.6116. The research leg alone gives $110.78 / 0.6191. The supervisor's reconciled value ($107.79) sits on the five forecasters' mean ($107.67), and the supervisor claims no directional edge. Read this as a fairly priced, defensive compounder bought slightly below value, not a mispricing the market is missing. (Sources 1, 3, 9, 23, 24, 25.)

valuation.methods: The research target (12m) is $107.79, the model engine's base horizon value (2027-10-20) on the supervisor's reconciled inputs. It weights 0.6 x P/E (17.0x NTM adj. EPS of ~$6.43) and 0.4 x EV/EBITDA (13.3x NTM adj. EBITDA); both legs come to $107.79. It is net of ~$2.67B after-tax litigation, settlement, separation and specified-items cash, on 2026-06-30 net debt of $27,005M (derived: 3,005 + 29,603 - 5,104 - 499, 10-Q). Scenarios: bear $78.79 / base $107.79 / bull $132.55. The five agents' research targets (12m) run $104.53-$110.82 (median $107.96; mean $107.67, derived: (110.82 + 108.80 + 104.53 + 107.96 + 106.26) / 5). The multiple decision card gave three values: 17.0x / 13.3x at $107.79 (chosen), the 18.2x / 14.0x peer median at $115.00 ($114.92 before the citation-gate fixes), and today's 16.5x / 13.0x at $104.75. There is no DCF leg this round; the prior memo blended 0.4 DCF. The $110.95 target is the median of the published 12-month distribution, which weights the options market 0.67 and research 0.33 with a calibration shift (expected value $115.03). It is not the research target (12m). Upside from the $102.45 pre-print close is +8.30% to target and +5.21% to the research target (12m) (derived: 110.95 / 102.45 - 1; 107.79 / 102.45 - 1). From the $98.36 post-print quote it is +12.8% and +9.6% (derived: 110.95 / 98.36 - 1; 107.79 / 98.36 - 1). Changes vs the 2026-10-14 memo: target $110.01 to $110.95 (+$0.94), research target (12m) $114.08 to $107.79 (derived: -$6.29, -5.5%), TP $130.57 to $133.60, stop $82.51 to $82.70, thesis break $80 to $78. The research target (12m) fell on 17.5x to 17.0x, dropping the DCF leg, slower Libre and EP after the call, and a fuller litigation/separation deduction. All levels are from the pre-print 2026-10-20 close and are re-marked tonight on the post-print close. (Sources 6, 7, 11, 24, 25, 30, 31, 36.)

It holds 34 sh at $102.45 and 36 sh at $97.33 with no news check, and 38 sh at $92.20 and 42 sh at $81.96 only after a news check. what_changes_our_mind: Tonight's re-mark on the post-print close. If the re-run target falls below the price, or the add fails the Sharpe test, we skip the second tranche and stay at 16 sh. If it holds above the price, we add up to the re-sized amount from 2026-10-22.

The January 2027 guide. FY2027 adj. EPS at or above ~$6.0 with organic growth accelerating from ~6% confirms the build, and we build toward 34 sh. A guide well below $6.0, or diabetes still decelerating in Q4, breaks the earnings leg of the thesis, and we cut and re-run.

Litigation and Libre quality. An NEC settlement batch above ~2x our ~$76k per infant, or a Libre consent decree or second recall, means our deductions are too small and we cut. A CMS non-insulin type 2 coverage decision or a warning-letter close-out is upside not in the numbers, and we would add on weakness.

tax_assumptions._kiddie_note: Unearned income above $2,700 (2 x $1,350, Rev. Proc. 2025-32) is taxed at the parent's rate, federal (Form 8615) and CA (FTB 3800). Applies to a full-time student 19-23 whose earned income is not more than half of his own support.
tax_assumptions._parent_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: parent in NYC, 37% federal bracket. Parent's NY/NYC rates do not apply to Kilian's gains (no NY kiddie tax under Form 8615).
tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM GAAP EPS at horizon from the build (~FY2028 ~$20.5) x 19.3x (peer median 24.95x shrunk k=0.8 toward own 18.6x, less China haircut)

inputs_detail.derivation: CY25 = 155 / 1.37 = 113 (Hill: SS +40%+ in CY26 'slightly above WFE growth' -> WFE ~+37%; Archer CY26 mid-$150B). CY26 155, CY27 200 (Archer '>$200B'; Dickerson '>30%' -> >201; below Goldman 218), CY28 220 (+10%: conservative vs Goldman 281/+29%; AMAT doubling output by 2028 says customers want more), CY29 226 (+3%: mid-cycle flattening year, rule 0c conservative). FY window: FY26 = 113x2/12+155x10/12 = 147.6; FY27 = 155x2/12+200x10/12 = 192.5; FY28 = 200x2/12+220x10/12 = 216.7; FY29 = 220x2/12+226x10/12 = 225.0.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Goldman 2026-08-23 path (CY27 218, CY28 281) puts FY28 window at ~270 (+25%): research target (12m) ~ +20%; a CY28 digestion year (-15%) ~ -20%.

inputs_detail.derivation: base 26.142 / 147.6 = 0.1771. +0.3pt FY27 (Hill expects to outgrow WFE again; DRAM and advanced packaging fastest, AMAT >50% of HBM packaging steps per Cantor), +0.2pt FY28, +0.1pt FY29: ~0.6pt by FY29, below the pace of the 2pt-by-2030 target (haircut: share targets are management statements). Cross-check: FY27 SS = 192.5 x 0.180 x 53/52 = $35.3B vs Q1 guide $8.7B (14 wk) rising every quarter (8.7+8.5+8.9+9.3 = 35.4).
inputs_detail.variant_view: Hold at FY26 0.177 (no share gain): ~ -3%.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 39.5% = Q4 run-rate 38.8% + ~0.7pt leverage on +35% revenue, net of capacity-ramp hiring; FY28 40.0% at peak volume; FY29 38.5% as WFE flattens and the doubled capacity is underabsorbed (mid-cycle). Alternative: hold at Q4 38.8% all years (~-2% value); 2030-target path to 42% (+~4%).
inputs_detail.variant_view: Mid-cycle at FY26 35.5%: ~ -9%.

inputs_detail.derivation: Peer median NTM P/E (LRCX 23.1, KLAC 26.8, ONTO 20.1, NVMI 31.5) = 24.95x; own NTM 349.23 / 18.75 (consensus FY27, TIKR 2026-11-13) = 18.6x; shrink k = 0.8: 24.95 x (18.6/24.95)^0.8 = 19.7x; less ~0.4 turn for China export-rule risk (long_dated_risks) = 19.3x.

memo.title: AMAT: staged Long after a 17.6% sell-off with no AMAT 8-K left it 14.6% below its $523 research target (12m)
memo.call_reason: The published 12-month target of $494.60 is 10.7% above the $446.63 close, conviction is medium and the Sharpe gate passed, so the book takes 5 shares, staged around the October prints and FQ4.
memo.one_liner: AMAT fell from $542.28 (Oct 5) to $446.63 (Oct 14) with no AMAT 8-K filing; since Sept 29 Micron, ASML and TSMC have all printed strong, and SEMI's 2028 WFE forecast is now $220B, which supports the $23.85 FY28 consensus. We buy 5 shares in tranches for a $494.60 target (research target (12m) $523), with a $328.23 stop just under the $335 thesis break.

thesis.point: The equipment upcycle runs through 2028, and it is being raised, not cut.
thesis.evidence: SEMI has WFE +21.8% in 2027 and raised its 2028 forecast to $220B from ~$200B on Sept 1, which supports consensus FY28 EPS of $23.85 on $55.9B of sales. Since our Sept 29 research, Micron printed record FQ4 revenue of $54.23B and guided FQ1 FY27 to $61.5B +/- $1.5B. ASML guided Q4 to EUR 14.2-15.2B and says planned 2027-28 supply will not fully meet customer demand. TSMC guided Q4 revenue to US$52.3-54.3B.

thesis.point: The market has already done much of the de-rating our research target (12m) assumes.
thesis.evidence: The close fell from $512.01 on Sept 29 to $446.63 on Oct 14, including -6.7% on Oct 13 (from $497.53) and -3.8% on Oct 14. AMAT filed no 8-K between Aug 27 and Oct 15. At $446.63 the stock is ~24.2x FY27 consensus EPS of $18.43, against ~27.8x at research ($512.01; derived). The research target (12m), derived, is NTM EPS of ~$22.8 (FY28 consensus less 4.5%) x 22.5x + $10.03 net cash = ~$522.5, rounded to $523, so the gap to the research target (12m) has widened from ~2% to 17.1%.

thesis.point: The next two quarters of earnings are visible, and the balance sheet is net cash.
thesis.evidence: The Q4 FY26 guide is revenue of $10.25B +/- $0.5B and non-GAAP EPS of $4.02 +/- $0.20. FY26 sales come to ~$34.3B (derived: 9M $24.04B + the $10.25B guide midpoint), and FY27 consensus is $46.3B (+35%, derived). Net cash is $7,957M ($10.03/share; derived from the 10-Q balance sheet). FQ3 converted 83% of non-GAAP net income to FCF (derived: $2,330M / $2,795M), against 51% over 9M (derived: $5,568M operating cash flow less $1,988M capex = $3,580M, over $6,980M), so the AR build reversing would add cash.

memo.variant_view: There is no strong variant view against the Street. We are well below it: the StockAnalysis median target is $645.50 (40 analysts, Strong Buy, range $358-900) [10], and our recency-weighted median of the individual targets is $654.18 (result.json), while our $494.60 target and $523 research target (12m) assume the multiple compresses to ~22.5x NTM as the cycle ages. Morgan Stanley's cut to $563 from $642 (Sep 28) shows that compression starting [11]. Against the options market we are modestly more constructive: its distribution (result.json market_only) has a median of $442.00 and P(gain) 0.49, against our blended P(gain) of 0.57. Our research-only view is a median of $608.71. The edge is narrow. The options market prices the stock as if the cycle peaks soon, while customer prints since Sept 29 (Micron, ASML, TSMC) point the other way [12, 13, 14].

valuation.methods: [2, 3] Supervisor research target (12m) $523 (derived): Sep-2027 NTM EPS of ~$22.8 (FY28 consensus $23.85 less ~4.5%) x 22.5x = ~$512.5, plus $10.03/share net cash from the Q3 FY26 10-Q ($14,501M cash and investments less $6,544M debt = $7,957M, on 793.6M shares) = ~$522.5. Excluding the $2.42B of equity investments ($3.05/share) it would be ~$519.5. The five agents are at $507.03-517.03 (lead $515.03), using ~$8/share net cash. All blend forward P/E (21-23.5x on NTM/FY28 EPS of $21.5-23.85, i.e. 0-10% haircuts to consensus; one agent adds a 25x FY27 leg) and, for four agents, FCF yield (3.0-3.4% on NTM/FY28 FCF). The standard model's DCF leg gets 0 weight: its DCF check (runs/2026-09-29/AMAT/model_engine.json) flags it at ~$147-172, 67-72% below the other legs, because its 13.6% WACC is far above the ~5% that the multiples imply. The published target of $494.60 is the 12-month median of a blend that is 67% the options market and 33% the research view, so it sits below the research target (12m). Thesis break is $335 (~18x FY27 consensus).

catalysts.event: TSMC Q3 2026 earnings conference (results released; call 14:00 Taiwan time)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Taiwan was 22% of AMAT's FQ3 revenue, and TSMC's capex drives leading-edge foundry/logic tool demand. Q3 revenue (NT$1,494.24B) and the Q4 guide (US$52.3-54.3B) are out. Capex comments come on the call.
catalysts.watch: Whether the 2026 capex range of $60-64B is raised, and any first 2027 capex figure. Flat or 'disciplined' 2027 language would hurt.

catalysts.event: Lam Research September-quarter financial conference call (2:00 p.m. PDT)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Lam is the closest peer, with the same customers and the same WFE cycle. Its December guide and its 2027 WFE view are the market's first read on AMAT's FQ4 and FQ1.
catalysts.watch: The 2027 WFE growth figure, the memory share of the guide, China as % of revenue, and any comment on the Nov 10 Affiliates Rule date.

catalysts.date: 2026-10-28 (09:00 Seoul; evening of Oct 27 US time)
catalysts.event: SK hynix Q3 2026 earnings conference call
catalysts.why_it_moves: DRAM is ~26-29% of AMAT's Semiconductor Systems revenue, and HBM/DRAM capex plans drive the 2027 memory tool budget.
catalysts.watch: 2027 capex level and any talk of slowing DRAM expansion to avoid overcapacity.

catalysts.event: KLA September-quarter results
catalysts.why_it_moves: A peer read on 2027 WFE and on process-control intensity at the leading edge, reported in the same week as the memory prints.
catalysts.watch: The December-quarter guide and the 2027 WFE framing.

catalysts.event: Hyperscaler quarterly reports and 2027 capex guides (Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon; they reported Oct 29-30 last year)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Doubts about AI spending, not AMAT news, drove the Aug 19 semicap sell-off, and hyperscaler 2027 capital plans are the most direct offset [19]. These capex guides set AI-capex sentiment for the group.
catalysts.watch: Whether 2027 capex guides rise again, or ROI and funding worries surface.

catalysts.event: BIS Affiliates (50%) Rule re-added to the EAR (suspension stayed until Nov 9, 2026, absent a future extension)
catalysts.why_it_moves: China is 28% of AMAT's FQ3 revenue. Reimposition would put Entity List controls on 50%-owned affiliates of listed Chinese customers. Treasury Secretary Bessent said the US-China truce is extended to Jan 10, 2027, but no extension of this rule had appeared in the Federal Register as of Oct 14.
catalysts.watch: A Federal Register/BIS notice extending the stay, possibly to Jan 10, 2027. Without one by early November, expect the risk to be priced into the FQ4 guide.

catalysts.event: AMAT FQ4 FY26 results and FQ1 FY27 guide (the company has not announced the date; FQ4 FY25 was reported Nov 13, 2025)
catalysts.why_it_moves: This is the first company read on FY27 against a consensus of $46.3B revenue and $18.43 EPS (+35% revenue), plus the China impact of the Affiliates Rule.
catalysts.watch: FQ4 against the $10.25B / $4.02 guide, the FQ1 guide, management's 2027 WFE framing, China % of revenue, FCF conversion (51% over 9M) and the AR build.

catalysts.event: SEMI year-end total equipment forecast (SEMI's forecast is bi-annual, with a year-end edition)
catalysts.why_it_moves: This updates the 2027 and 2028 WFE path that underpins FY28 consensus. It was last raised to $220B for 2028 in September.
catalysts.watch: 2028 WFE above or below $220B, and 2027 growth against +21.8%.

catalysts.event: Micron FQ1 FY27 results (FQ1 FY26 was reported Dec 17, 2025)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Micron is the biggest DRAM capex swing factor. It guided FQ1 revenue to $61.5B +/- $1.5B and says it is increasing manufacturing investment.
catalysts.watch: The FY27 capex figure and how much of it is tools rather than cleanroom construction.

catalysts.event: US-China trade truce deadline (extension announced by Treasury Secretary Bessent)
catalysts.why_it_moves: This is a binary China-policy event. A lapse could bring back the tariffs the truce holds off, and the Affiliates Rule if its stay is extended only to this date.
catalysts.watch: Talks on a further extension in December. A lapse with no deal is negative for the 28% of revenue from China.

catalysts.event: TSMC Q4 2026 results and any first 2027 capex guide (Q4 2025 results were released Jan 15, 2026)
catalysts.why_it_moves: The single most important 2027 tool-budget number for leading-edge logic, against 2026 capex of $60-64B.
catalysts.watch: A 2027 capex guide above the 2026 range supports the thesis. Flat or lower would point to a 2027-28 digestion.

catalysts.event: AMAT FQ1 FY27 results and FQ2 guide
catalysts.why_it_moves: This confirms or breaks the +35% FY27 revenue consensus at the start of calendar 2027, after the China policy dates.
catalysts.watch: FQ2 guide run-rate against ~$11.6B/quarter of FY27 consensus (derived: $46.3B / 4), China revenue after Nov 10 / Jan 10, and gross margin.

risks.risk: AI or memory capex digestion: customers pause 2027-28 tool spending after the current build, and FY28 consensus ($23.85) gets cut the way out-year numbers are at cycle turns.
risks.signpost: TSMC's January 2027 capex guide at or below the 2026 $60-64B range, Lam's December guide down, or SK hynix/Micron talking about slower DRAM expansion. SEMI cutting 2028 below $220B in its year-end update.

risks.risk: China: the Affiliates Rule returns on Nov 10, 2026 (or after a Jan 10, 2027 truce lapse), hitting a region that is 28% of revenue. A suspended BIS denial order from the $252.5M settlement also remains.
risks.signpost: No Federal Register extension notice by early November. AMAT's FQ1 guide citing China, or China share falling well below 28%.

risks.risk: Multiple compression on sentiment: the stock fell 42.5% from $723.00 (Jun 30) to $415.38 (Sep 16), a stretch that included the record FQ3 and raised outlook (Aug 13), and 17.6% from $542.28 to $446.63 (Oct 5-14) with no AMAT 8-K filing.
risks.signpost: A close below the $415.38 September low with no fundamental cause. Below $335 (~18x FY27) the market is pricing a real downturn, which is the thesis break.

risks.risk: Cash conversion stays weak: 9M FCF was 51% of non-GAAP net income (derived) because of the AR build and facilities capex, against 83% in FQ3 (derived).
risks.signpost: FQ4 FCF conversion below ~70% or DSO rising again in the mid-November report.

trade.position: 5 sh (~$2,233, 9.3% of the $23,933 book; 10.6% of cash to deploy). The book-level Sharpe test sets the size; the supervisor's per-name 8% cap no longer applies, since the book dropped per-name caps on 2026-10-07. The loss at the stop is ~$592. AMAT would be ~54% of account risk, with 0.66 correlation to NVDA and 0.61 to AVGO already held.
trade.entry: The supervisor's 3-tranche plan over ~6 weeks. Its first triggers (Micron Sep 30, ASML Oct 14) are past and positive. Buy 2 sh after the TSMC call (Oct 15), 2 sh after Lam (Oct 21) if the 2027 WFE view holds, and the last 1 sh after AMAT FQ4 (mid-November, estimated).
trade.exit_or_add: Exit at the $328.23 stop (a noise floor of 2x one-month implied vol, just below the $335 thesis break), or on a close below $335 on fundamental news: customer capex cuts, an AMAT guide-down, or the Affiliates Rule reimposed with a quantified China loss. Take profit at $704.94. Reassess near the $523 research target (12m). No adds beyond 5 sh: the Sharpe test sets the size and AMAT would already be ~54% of account risk. Only a research refresh that raises the target, for example TSMC's 2027 capex above 2026 plus a strong FQ1 guide, would justify new sizing. [Updated 2026-11-24: the one upside exit is now $487.19, where the 12-month expected value no longer beats the 4% cash sleeve and the model sells every share; any other take-profit figure in this memo is superseded.]
trade.take_profit_note: expected value: the price where the 12-month expected return (research fixed in dollars, options leg moving with the price) falls to the 4% cash rate (full exit) (as of 2026-11-24)

what_changes_our_mind: TSMC's 2027 capex guide (mid-Jan) at or below the 2026 $60-64B range, or Lam/AMAT guiding the December/January quarter down: that means the 2027-28 WFE path behind the $23.85 FY28 consensus is breaking.
The Affiliates Rule takes effect on Nov 10 with no Federal Register extension, and AMAT's FQ1 guide shows a China revenue hit well beyond today's 28% mix trend.

A close below the $415.38 September low that comes with estimate cuts rather than sentiment. Conversely, a fast move to the $523 research target (12m) without higher estimates would remove the edge and argue for trimming.

results.supervisor_summary: Research target (12m) $47.66 (update 2026-11-10, was $50.13) vs the 11-10 close $45.24, after the Q3 FY2026 beat and raise: sales 38.1 (+110%), non-GAAP GM 48.7%, EPS -0.05 vs Street -0.16; Q4 guide 43.5-44.5. The set books FY26-29 revenue 141.4 / 188.8 / 218.8 / 242.9, rebuilt from the Q4 carry-in, end-market units, Apollo5 ASP mix and management's non-wearables mix; FY28 revenue is lower than the old carried +28.9% path, so the target falls 4.9%. Base round: Research target (12m) $50.13 (P10 $27.10, P90 $88.90) vs the 11-03 close $44.68, after the citation gate rebuilt every driver year on cited evidence or a labeled trend: FY26 sits on the company's ~$135M sales and ~$85M opex guides, FY27 total revenue on consensus 178.43, and FY28-29 revenue extends the last evidenced growth (+28.9%) because no FY28 guide or free consensus exists (the set's slower +20% path would give $47.85). Valued at 5.02x EV / NTM sales from four comparable peers all on EV / NTM consensus revenue (median 4.785x), plus ~$343M of net cash and interest at the horizon. Concentration (top-3 = 78% of sales) and the Q3 print in November keep this a small, staged position.

agents.reasoning: Lane: primary documents (filings, releases, call transcripts, IR decks, Form 144/EDGAR index, proxy). I started from the thread quarterly driver set and checked each driver against the company's own words. Revenue: FY26 guide ~$135M [18]; 4/4 quarterly beats (median +8.4%) but H2 explicitly supply-constrained and orders unmet [20,17]; purchase commitments 7.6 -> 27.7 -> 32.2 [27,6] support demand; so I keep us/cn/row and the FY26 138.5 (+2.6% vs guide). Opex: I differ from the set (+14/11/10% vs +22/14/12%) because management framed breakeven at ~$47M/qtr in 2H27-early 2028 [20] and opex landed at/below guide twice [4,5]; recurring IP purchases (7-10M/yr, ~2M in Q3) [17] keep it from being flat. In the EV/sales leg this matters only ~$0.3/sh, so the value is driven by revenue and the multiple. Loss-making through FY28, so P/E and EV/EBITDA cannot carry it; Round 2: the supervisor showed my round-1 multiple was on the wrong basis (own 3.98x on basic shares and CY27 consensus; peers on CY27 rather than NTM). Rebuilt on one basis: 5 genuine peers on EV / Nov-26..Oct-27 sales (median 4.39x, range 3.57-10.71x), own 4.87x on 27.97M fully diluted shares, k = 0.8 -> 4.77x; plus $16.2M interest on net cash that the engine omits. I keep my opex path (only $0.28/sh) and the thread revenue/GM drivers, which the supervisor also kept; agent_3's sell-in concern (inventories 16.9 -> 29.4, receivables 7.3 -> 17.5 [6]) was already in my downside. ASP pressure; supply relief, design wins, mix) and the multiple to ~2.62x / ~7.32x: P10 $25.28, P90 $73.29. New primary findings beyond the recaps: top-3 concentration rose to 78% from 71%; inventories +73% in six months; the October slide followed the end of the 60-day follow-on lock-up and 16 Form 144s; bonuses are discretionary; FY26 opex guide includes IP purchases while the cash-flow statement also capitalises intangibles (possible double count, flagged). agents.reasoning: Rerun on current data (the earlier file used Oct 5-6 consensus and predated the Q3 print). Primary lane: the Q3 2026 release and 10-Q, the Q4 2025, Q1 and Q2 2026 releases (segment and ad tables, quarterly guides), XBRL quarterly capex/D&A/interest, and call excerpts with speakers. Key facts: Q3 revenue $201.9B (+12%), AWS $46.0B (+39%, 38.7% margin), ads $19.6B (+11%), operating income $28.1B (a record 13.9% margin). Q4 guide: $240-247B revenue and $28.5-33.5B operating income, ads 'high teens'. AWS backlog $578B (6.1-year life, +$82B q/q). TTM FCF -$42.4B on $215B TTM capex. 2026 capex ~$220B, 'meaningfully more' in 2027 (CEO). Anthropic carried at $238.7B and OpenAI at $35B in the 10-Q. Model: AWS grows +39.5% in FY2027 and +33% in FY2028 (sequential adds capped by capacity; 3.5 points under UBS's 43%) at a 37.5% margin, below 2026 as D&A climbs. Ads grow +17%/+15%, retail ex-ads +8.5%/+8%, and the retail margin rises +0.7/+0.6 points on the ads mix. Capex follows the project's Big-4 path at Amazon's 2026 share ($303.5B and $392.5B). The result: FY2027 revenue $962B (consensus $960B), EBIT $147B (consensus $147B), and FY2028 EBIT $187B (5% under consensus) with EPS $12.33 vs $14.58. Valuation: P/E with the 0.8 shrink, and a SOTP; stakes added after tax and illiquidity. Research target (12m) $322.8 (+24%). It sits close to the sell-side mean ($326.5) for a different reason: below-consensus EPS on a higher multiple of core earnings once the $18/share of stakes is taken out of today's multiple. Scenarios: P10 $209 (AWS -12% revenue and -3pt margin, multiple -5 turns, SOTP multiples -20%, stakes -40%) and P90 $419 (AWS +10% revenue and +2.5pt margin, multiple +3, SOTP multiples +12%, stakes +40%). The left tail is fatter, matching the AI capex digestion risk and the stock's 34% realized volatility. Decart: reported near a ~$7-7.5B deal but not signed; left out as value-neutral.

Case: Big-4 capex rises 34.5% in 2027 and 29.3% in 2028 (NVDA model path) after ~+83% in 2026; capacity bought in 2026 lands in 2027 revenue, so growth stays above capex growth in 2027 and converges to it in 2028. memo.title: AMZN: Long. Hold 1 sh into the Oct 29 print and add toward ~11 sh after it. Target $280.84 (+12.2%), research target (12m) $278.28 on 23x driver-built EPS plus an AWS-led sum of parts
memo.call_reason: The published target ($280.84) and research target (12m) ($278.28) are both above the $250.38 close, and P(gain) is 0.6279. The edge is modest: the supervisor's confidence is low (its ladder is not used), and conviction scales the expected return from 18.3% to 17.5% (multiplier 0.72).
memo.one_liner: AWS is adding capacity faster than ever: AWS net PP&E reached $263.8B at mid-2026 against a ~$496B backlog. Our driver build turns that into AWS sales of $234.6B in 2027 (+35%) and lets ads carry retail profits. The Anthropic and OpenAI stakes add ~$21/share, which the street's EPS does not count. We price 23x on NTM EPS of $11.32, 13% below consensus; the gap is EBITDA, not D&A (2028: $297.9B vs consensus $355.3B), so the $278.28 research target (12m) and $280.84 target are not stretch numbers; we hold 1 sh and stage the add after the Oct 29 print.

thesis.point: AWS growth is capacity-led and largely pre-sold, so revenue follows the capex.
thesis.evidence: Q2-26 AWS sales were $42.2B (+37%) with $16.6B OI. The backlog is ~$496B with a 6.4-year weighted life, and management says power capacity doubles by end-2027 vs 2025 and 2027 capacity is largely reserved. The driver build rolls AWS net PP&E from $150.4B (FY25 average) to $266.2B / $426.3B / $590.8B averages in 2026-28. Capacity turnover falls from 0.86x to 0.65x / 0.55x / 0.50x. That gives AWS sales of $173.8B / $234.6B / $293.7B, which is +35.0% in 2027 and +25.2% in 2028 (derived: 234.6 / 173.8 - 1; 293.7 / 234.6 - 1). AWS EBITDA margin goes from 57.1% in H1-26 (ex the ~$0.6B energy gain) to 58.5% / 60.0%. The external backdrop is supportive: the cloud market grew +43% y/y in Q2 with Amazon at 28% share, and AWS raised Capacity Block GPU prices ~15% on Oct 7 (P6-B300 now $16.146 per accelerator-hour; the prior $14.04 is from the research).

thesis.point: Ads, not the stores, carry North America + International profit, and that profit compounds even with flat retail margins.
thesis.evidence: Advertising was $68.6B in FY25 and grew +25.1% in H1-26 (Q2 +26.2%). The driver path is $85.4B / $102.5B / $121.0B for 2026-28 (+24% / +20% / +18%). At an assumed 50% ads margin, which is our estimate and not disclosed, stores run at ~0.16% margin held flat. Segment OI still rises from $43.7B in 2026 to $52.3B in 2027 and $61.6B in 2028 (engine rows). The SOTP values this at 22x NTM after-tax OI of $46.9B = $1,032B.

thesis.point: The AI-lab stakes are real equity value that consensus EPS excludes. We count them once, after tax, lock-up and an overlay.
thesis.evidence: The 10-Q carries Anthropic at $190.4B, and Amazon committed $50B to OpenAI's Series C. We value Anthropic at a $1.5T IPO, which is 17.60% after the Public Benefit Fund and primary dilution, less 24% tax and a 10.37% lock-up discount, for $183.7B. OpenAI is at cost, $50.0B. Together that is ~$21.19/share on 11.03B horizon shares (derived: (183.7 + 50.0) / 11.03). After the Leo and Zoox loss add-backs (+$72.7B) and their own scenario values (+$22.0B), other investments (+$4.6B), Globalstar (-$10.9B), probability-weighted legal (-$34.5B) and a 10% conglomerate overlay (-$26.0B), the net equity-level items are +$23.72/share (derived: $261.6B / 11.03B) on both legs. The stakes cut both ways: an Anthropic IPO at ~$1.0T takes ~$6.95/share off, and ~$1.92T adds ~$5.53.

memo.variant_view: We sit below the street and slightly above the options market. StockAnalysis shows a median target of $329.50 (average $331.46, Strong Buy); our recency-weighted median of 56 individual analyst targets is $326.23, +30.3% from $250.38. Our $280.84 target is 13.9% below it (derived: 280.84 / 326.23 - 1), and analysts get zero weight in the published target (ex-analyst target $276.13). The gap is earnings, not the multiple. Our driver-built NTM EPS at the Oct-2027 horizon is $11.32, against ~$13.03 on consensus (derived: 0.237 x $10.51 + 0.763 x $13.81), so we are 13.1% below. Driver-built 2028 EBIT is $155.1B vs MarketScreener's $182.7B (-15.1%). The difference is not D&A. We depreciate AWS PP&E at 14% a year on a capex roll that uses consensus 2027-28 capex ($277.4B / $296.9B), yet the build's 2028 D&A of $142.7B is below the $172.6B implied by consensus EBITDA less EBIT (derived: 355.3 - 182.7). The gap is EBITDA: $297.9B vs $355.3B in 2028 (-16.2%, derived), with the stores margin held at ~0.16% (H1-26 0.76%) and ads at an assumed 50% margin. The street's ~$326 implies ~31x FY27 EPS (derived: 326.23 / 10.51 = 31.0x), against a 23.5x CY2027 peer median. Against the options market, the market-only median is $265.01 with P(gain) 0.5615. Our published $280.84 is 6.0% higher (derived: 280.84 / 265.01 - 1) and our P(gain) of 0.6279 is 6.6 points higher. The gap comes from the research leg (weight 0.33, with its calibration shift), whose value includes the ~$21/share of AI-lab stakes. This is a real but small variant: a below-consensus earnings path, with sum-of-parts value the street's P/E does not capture.

valuation.methods: The research target (12m) of $278.28 is the model engine's base horizon value (2027-10-06) on the driver-led set: 0.5 x P/E leg + 0.5 x SOTP leg. P/E leg $284.09: 23x (a 2.3% discount to the 23.5x CY2027 11-peer median; cloud subgroup 22.5x) x driver-built NTM EPS $11.32 = $260.36, plus $23.72/share of equity-level items. SOTP leg $272.47: AWS NTM after-tax OI $70.9B x 25 = $1,772.5B, plus North America + International $46.9B x 22 = $1,032.0B, less a $3.2B venture basis correction = EV $2,801.4B. From that we deduct horizon net debt of $58.4B (incl. finance leases) and add the same equity items, over 11.03B horizon shares (0.9%/yr dilution). The DCF is a diagnostic only, at weight 0 ($182 at a 10.44% WACC with a mid-capex-cycle terminal year). Scenarios are bear $183.10 (p 0.25: AWS turnover -8%, EBITDA margin -2 pts, ads -4%, 17.5x, Anthropic ~$1.0T), base $278.28 (p 0.5) and bull $343.83 (p 0.25: AWS turnover +6%, +1.5 pts, ads +3%, 25.5x, Anthropic ~$1.92T). The model median is $270.60. The driver gate (2026-10-22) moved the research target (12m) $277.36 -> $278.28 by fixing the EPS/EBIT ratio. The three agents' research targets (12m) were $290 / $278 / $267. The $280.84 target is the median of the published 12-month distribution, which weights the options market 0.67 and research 0.33 with a calibration shift (expected value $296.27). Upside from $250.38 is +12.17% to target and +11.14% to the research target (12m) (derived: 280.84 / 250.38 - 1; 278.28 / 250.38 - 1).

catalysts.why_it_moves: It is the largest legal item: p(liability) 0.35 on a 3-10% remedy hit to the retail + ads value, -$15.9B in the build. Liability is tried first and remedies later, so a remedy ruling inside the horizon is unlikely. Headlines can still move the stock.
catalysts.watch: Pretrial rulings, settlement talk, and whether the FTC/22-state ad-surcharge suit (filed Aug 31, 2026) is consolidated or survives a motion to dismiss.

risks.risk: AI-capex digestion: AWS growth slides to the low-to-mid 20s while D&A from the capex roll keeps rising. This is the bear case at $183.10 (AWS turnover -8%, AWS EBITDA margin -2 pts, 17.5x).

risks.risk: AI-lab concentration: OpenAI and Anthropic are large parts of the ~$496B backlog and large equity marks. Anthropic also signed multi-gigawatt TPU capacity with Google and Broadcom from 2027.
risks.signpost: Backlog (RPO) flat or down in the 10-Q, a renegotiated lab commitment, Anthropic workloads shifting to TPU, or an Anthropic IPO priced below $1.5T (at ~$1.0T, -$6.95/share).

risks.signpost: The 10-year back above 5.3% after a hawkish Oct 28 or Dec 9 FOMC, peer CY2027 P/Es compressing toward the 22.5x cloud subgroup or lower, and a close below the $193.10 stop.

risks.signpost: Adverse pretrial rulings before the Mar 29, 2027 trial, the ad-surcharge suit surviving dismissal (it is -$14.1B in the build: -$4.0B damages, -$10.1B forward pricing), or an injunction in California.

Add per the decider ladder above after the print, if AWS growth holds at or above ~30% and 2027 capex framing is not above ~$300B without AWS acceleration. what_changes_our_mind: Q3 (Oct 29) shows AWS growth below ~30% (vs +37% in Q2) together with 2027 capex framed above ~$300B. The driver path, and with it the $278.28 research target (12m), would be too high, so we stop adding and re-run.

A close below the $188 thesis break while FY27 consensus EPS is still being revised up (4 up / 0 down in 30 days at the last check). That would mean the market is pricing a structural break (backlog quality or a margin reset), not noise. We exit.

On the upside: AWS holding 35%+ with margins at or above 60%, or an Anthropic IPO at or above ~$1.92T. Both move us toward the $343.83 bull case, and we would re-test the $350.53 full exit rather than sell into it.

thesis_triggers.event: Reviewed 2026-11-04, unchanged at $185: Q3 confirmed growth (+55.5%) and margins (84.3%); $185 is well below our downside (P10) case. Net debt is now 342.4 (9-30) and the buyback authorization $3.6B after October's $3.2B raise (src 46, 47). Earlier review (2026-10-30, figures as of then): Reviewed 2026-10-30, unchanged at $185: the -10.4% on Oct 30 had no company news (sector AI selloff, src 25) and the close of $228.50 is still ~24% above it; $185 is ~9.2x our FY2027 model EPS and sits just above our downside (P10) case of ~$174. At about $185 the stock trades at about 9.4x FY27 Zacks consensus EPS ($19.63, 11-04 snapshot), about 7-8x EBITDA and a 10%+ FCF yield, with about $0.46B of net debt and $1.8B of buyback authorization left at 6-30. A sustained trade there would mean the market expects earnings to fall, not just growth to slow. Likely causes: a Q4 guide implying flat or negative q/q revenue, visible MAX/Axon share or spread loss to Unity Vector (now growing about 16% q/q), a loss in the Unity dispute that exposes MAX auction data, an Apple/Google platform action, or a damaging litigation development. The agents' mean is $185 (range $180-195); it sits about one 12-month sigma below spot.

memo.title: AppLovin: cheap at about 14x FY27 EPS but conviction is low. The model says no position; a 1-share post-print starter would be an exception to the conviction rule.
memo.call_reason: Conviction is below medium: the supervisor rated it low, so the allocator sized it at 0 shares (binding: conviction_below_min). The target of $292.84 is above the $268.22 price, so the target is not what blocks the trade; low conviction is.
memo.one_liner: APP trades at about 14x FY27 EPS with a 6% FCF yield, $0.46B net debt and $1.8B of buyback left. Our $292.84 target (+9%) and $322 research target (12m) (+20%) are well below the Street's $512 median, and the model takes no position because conviction is low. The only trade on the table is a proposal awaiting your yes: 1 share (about $268) after the Q3 print and Q4 guide, expected around Wed Nov 4 but not yet announced. It is an explicit exception to the medium-conviction rule, justified by its effect on the book's Sharpe, not by a stronger view on the stock.

thesis.point: The business is still growing fast and is very profitable. The de-rating comes from slower growth, not shrinking earnings.
thesis.evidence: Q2 2026 revenue was $1,924M (+53% y/y), adjusted EBITDA $1,614M (84% margin), diluted EPS $3.76 and free cash flow $863.3M. The Q3 2026 guide is revenue of $2,055-2,085M (about +7.6% q/q at the midpoint) and adjusted EBITDA of $1,710-1,740M (83% margin).

thesis.point: Valuation and the balance sheet give a floor. Further downside needs earnings estimates to fall, not just the multiple.
thesis.evidence: At $268 the stock is about 14x FY27 consensus EPS of $20.00 and about a 6% FCF yield (supervisor). At Jun 30 2026: cash $3,053M against long-term debt $3,515M, so net debt is about $0.46B. Shares outstanding were 335.3M. The company bought back 3.28M shares for $1.5B in H1 2026, and $1.8B of authorization remains. The thesis break of $185 equals about 9x FY27 EPS and a 10%+ FCF yield.

thesis.point: The upside needs the estimate cuts to stop, and the Q4 guide is the first chance for that. This is why we would enter after the print, not before.
thesis.evidence: FY27 consensus EPS fell from $21.16 to $20.00 in 60 days (19 cuts, 5 raises; vendor data). Edgewater expects Q4 at +8-9% q/q (about $2.25B), against a consensus of about $2.27-2.28B. Wells Fargo's traffic-weighted pixel data (about 85% of new sites show no traffic) suggests e-commerce is a 2027 story. A Q4 guide at or above consensus would stop the cuts. A guide below about $2.25B would extend them.

memo.variant_view: Our variant view is against the sell side, not against the options market. Our blended 12-month target is $292.84 (P(gain) 0.55). The 24 analysts' weighted mean is $511 (median $512, range $325-790, rating Buy). We think those targets are stale: they assume a re-rating that falling revisions do not support. In the last two months BofA moved to $400 and Piper to $325, and Wells Fargo is at $325. The options market alone implies $252 (P(gain) 0.46). We sit modestly above it because valuation support (14x, 6% FCF yield, buybacks) has not yet broken. That edge over the options market is small, about +$41 in the median, and at about 68% implied vol it is not a strong variant view. The supervisor said plainly that no verified fact shows a clear edge per unit of risk. [sources 20, 23, 24, 25, 18, 22]

valuation.methods: Supervisor research target (12m) $322, against the agents' range of $310-348 (mean $326). Three methods, blended: (1) P/E: FY27 EPS of about $19.2 (consensus $20.00 less about 4%), rolled to an NTM EPS of about $22 at Oct 2027, at about 15x = about $330. (2) FCF yield: FY27E FCF of about $6.4B / about 328M shares at a 6-6.3% yield = about $310-325. (3) EV/EBITDA: 11-12x on about $8.1B, less $0.46B net debt = about $290-320. Share base: 335.3M at Jun 30 2026 (10-Q), falling to about 326-330M with buybacks. The 12-month target ($292.84) is the calibrated median of a 67% options-market / 33% agent blend. Scenario range across agents: bear $170-190 (22-30%), base $310-325 (45-53%), bull $475-500 (25-27%). Model take-profit $453.69 (q75); stop $180.70 (2x 1M IV noise floor). [sources 2, 20, 22]

trade.position: Proposed: 1 sh (about $268 at the $268.22 close, about 2.7% of the $9,976 book). This is an explicit EXCEPTION to the medium-conviction rule. The model allocation is 0 shares because the supervisor rated conviction low (binding: conviction_below_min). The case for the exception is the portfolio effect: 1 APP share, alongside 1 AMZN share, raises the book's Sharpe on invested money from about 0.60 to about 0.68. 1 share is slightly above the supervisor's 2.5% cap (about $249), and a single share cannot be split into the supervisor's two tranches.
trade.entry: Do not buy before the print. Buy 1 share after the Q3 2026 report and Q4 guide (expected around Wed Nov 4 2026; the company has not announced the date as of Oct 3), and only if all three hold: (a) the Q4 revenue guide midpoint is at or above about $2.25B (Edgewater's bar); (b) the stock is above the $185 thesis break; (c) nothing new turns up in litigation or the Unity dispute. This adapts the supervisor's two-tranche plan (half after Q3, half after Q4 in Feb 2027) to a 1-share size. If the guide misses, there is no trade.
trade.exit_or_add: Exit if: the stock closes below the $180.70 stop or holds below the $185 thesis break (loss at stop about $88, about 0.9% of the book); the Q4 2026 report (around mid-Feb 2027) misses its own guide, or the Q1 2027 guide implies flat or negative q/q; FY27 consensus EPS falls below about $18; or AppLovin loses the Unity dispute in a way that exposes MAX auction data. Take profit at $453.69. Add a 2nd share only after the Q4 2026 report, if the guide held, FY27 revisions have stopped falling, and the supervisor's conviction rating rises to medium. Until then the position stays at 1 share as an exception.

what_changes_our_mind: Bullish: a Q4 guide at or above about $2.28B, with management quantifying e-commerce, and FY27 consensus EPS turning up from $20.00. This would justify medium conviction and a normal-sized position.
Bearish: a Q4 guide implying less than about +5% q/q, or a sustained trade below $185. Either would mean the market expects earnings to fall; we would drop the idea and not buy the exception share.

Competitive: Unity Q3 Strategic Grow beats $385M and guides Q4 to another mid-teens q/q while AppLovin decelerates, or the TRO is denied and Unity keeps collecting MAX auction data. Either would move weight to the bear case ($170-190).

tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. Net losses offset gains; up to $3,000 deducts at the own short-term rate. Bracket mode (mode 'brackets') still holds the CA schedule and is not updated.
tax_assumptions._short_term_all_note: Kilian 2026-10-28 card 'Assume short-term on all' (thread 'Fix AMAT target vs sell mismatch'): every holding is assumed sold within the year at the short-term rate, so a trim only pays the same tax H years sooner; band per year = q tau (1 - (1+d)^-H) / H + spread / T. Overrides lot_aware_horizon; false restores it.
tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. Long-term lots keep the T-year rule (years_until_you_would_otherwise_sell, future_rate_on_deferred_gains, Claude defaults 2026-09-28). false restores the T-year rule for every lot.

Anchors: (a) purchase commitments rise from $52,674M (FY27) to $72,952M (FY28), +38.5% [4]; scaling the $115B FY27 guide by that ratio gives 115 x 72,952/52,674 = $159B, a floor because later-year commitments are still filling in; (b) house capex base 2028 $2,255B [16]: $115B/$1,841B = 6.2% in 2027; $180B = 8.0% of 2028 (+1.8pt share gain, backed by Anthropic +10 GW and OpenAI >5 GW line of sight [6]); $230B would need 10.2%. $180B sits between the commitment floor and management's figure.

agents.reasoning: Round 2 follows the supervisor's findings, each re-checked at the primary source. (1) FY28 AI revenue: I cut my $195B to $180B. Three of my own cross-checks bracket it: scaling the 10-Q purchase commitments (FY27 $52.7B, FY28 $73.0B [4]) gives $179B on total revenue and $166B on semis only; an 8.2% share of house 2028 base capex gives $185B [11]. The FY28 commitment bucket did not grow between the Q2 and Q3 10-Qs [4][5]. (2) I dropped the 'FY27 consensus x 21x' leg: at an Oct-2027 horizon the market prices FY28, and stalled earnings belong in the bear scenario, not at a full multiple. A DCF (30% weight) replaces it, at the verified 10-yr of 5.31% [12] and Q3 FCF conversion of 0.835 [1]. (3) The P/E build is now pinned to reported Q3 lines: interest $778M less other income $98M [1], margin slope from Q3 to the Q4 guide [1][2]; the build reproduces Q3 non-GAAP NI within 0.4%. (4) Peers: 11 names on one CY2027 basis from Finviz, with three off-cycle names calendarized [7-10]; the median is 26.0x, not my old 30.6x (mixed NTM) nor the supervisor's 23.7x (which kept CSCO/COHR/CRDO on mid-2028 fiscal years). I use 20x, inside the range, for the persistent reasons in comps_summary. (5) Removed from every number: the Anthropic S-1 figures, press-reported $60B bank financing, and Marvell's targets (context only [15][16]); the $42B is now cited from Broadcom's 10-Q [3]. I did not use the MS SPCX digest's AVGO EV/EBIT/growth bar-chart value (marked unverified). Industry read: Broadcom's Q3 AI revenue $16.7B [1] vs NVIDIA Data Center $89.0B [17] means ~16% of the pair. TSMC calls packaging the binding constraint [13]. Result: FY28 EPS $23.60, P/E leg $472, DCF $318, fair value $426. Scenarios: bear $237 (25%), base $426 (50%), bull $550 (25%), weighted mean $410. The ladder is a mixture of three lognormals centred on the scenario prices (sigmas 0.36/0.30/0.33, giving overall log-sd ~0.45 vs 47% realized). Its median is ~$408 (P(>=415) 0.48), its mean ~$432, and P(>=377) = 0.57. The fair value of $426 sits between the ladder median and mean; the median is below it because the bear case is further from base than the bull is. I trimmed the right tail (P(>=943) 0.044 -> 0.015). Analyst targets were not used as anchors.
