memo.title: AVGO: long a de-rated AI compounder at ~13.5x FY28 consensus; target $390, research target (12m) $407, stop $261
memo.call_reason: The published 12-month target ($390.49) is above the $349.57 price, conviction is medium, and there is no special situation; the supervisor's 8% cap limits size and the book gets 2 shares.
memo.one_liner: Broadcom has fallen ~30% from its June high while earnings rose ~43%. It trades at ~13.5x LSEG FY28 EPS of $25.86, against management's $115B FY27 / $230B FY28 AI roadmap. We underwrite consensus EPS, not management's >$30, and still get a $407 research target (12m) (+16%) and a $390 target (+12%, P(gain) 60%), with the Q4 print on ~Dec 10 as the first test.

thesis.point: Earnings are compounding faster than the stock is falling: the de-rating is multiple, not fundamentals.
thesis.evidence: Q3 FY26 revenue $29.6B (+86% y/y), AI semis $16.7B (+221%), non-GAAP EPS $3.32, FCF $13.7B. The Q4 guide is $34.8B with $21.7B AI. Yet the stock is back at its end-2025 level with EPS ~43% higher and ~30% below the June high, at ~18x FY27 consensus ($19.38) and ~13.5x FY28 ($25.86).

thesis.point: We do not need management's numbers: consensus EPS at a below-peer multiple gets to ~$407.
thesis.evidence: Management guides $115B FY27 and $230B FY28 AI revenue and >$30 FY28 EPS; LSEG consensus is $25.86. All five agents value on NTM EPS of $24.7-26.5 at 16.5-17x, i.e. at or below consensus. Every $1 of FY28 EPS the market underwrites is worth ~$16-17/share, so each beat on the path toward >$30 is upside to the target.

thesis.point: The XPV financing scare is smaller than the headline: expected loss ~$0.5/share.
thesis.evidence: The 10-Q (Note 10) shows a Backstop of one customer's 5-year lease obligations: 85% of lease balance owed less rack resale value, max ~$29B, fair value not material, nothing paid, plus a facility under which the customer may issue Broadcom up to $42B of convertible notes (none issued). BofA's $370B is a hypothetical 20 GW build-out; its loss case on the existing tranche is ~$2.9B. We deduct ~$2-2.5B (~$0.5/share).

memo.variant_view: The variant view is modest, and it cuts both ways. Against the options market we are more constructive: its implied 12-month median is ~$364 with P(gain) 54%, while our blended target is $390 with P(gain) 60%, because the agents give credit for ~2x EPS growth at a compressed ~16-17x NTM multiple that the market is not paying for today. Against the sell side we are far more cautious: 38 analysts rate it Strong Buy with a median target of $525.5 (mean $517), which in effect capitalizes management's >$30 FY28 EPS at ~18-20x. We underwrite LSEG's $25.86 and a discount for six-customer concentration, Google's move toward MediaTek and the XPV overhang. So this is not a contrarian call. It is a 'consensus earnings, de-rated multiple' call that is roughly half-way between options pricing and the Street.

valuation.methods: The research target (12m) of $407 is the mean of five independent agents ($391-425), valued as of Sep 2027. Legs: (1) P/E on NTM (mostly FY28) EPS of $24.7-26.5 at 16.5-17x = $420-439 (40-60% weight); (2) FCF yield of 5-5.5% on ~$97-122B NTM/FY28 FCF = $388-441; (3) DCF at 10% WACC, 3% terminal growth = $311-373 (agents 1 and 5); (4) SOTP with AI at 16x after-tax earnings = $333-388 (agents 2 and 3). EV-based legs deduct $35.4B net debt ($59.419B debt less $23.975B cash) and ~$2-2.5B expected XPV loss; all use 4.94B non-GAAP diluted shares. $407 is ~16x NTM EPS of ~$25.5, dividends (~$2.60/yr) excluded. The published $390.49 target is the median of the blended distribution (67% options market, 33% agents after calibration), below the research target (12m) because of the 44-58% volatility and the fat left tail. Expected value is $435; quartiles $291 / $522.

catalysts.event: Micron fiscal Q4 FY26 results (after close)
catalysts.why_it_moves: HBM pricing and supply read-through: memory-heavy XPUs are the main reason Broadcom's gross margin is guided down to ~73%, and HBM/substrate tightness can shift XPU revenue across quarters.
catalysts.watch: HBM4 pricing for 2027, sold-out commentary and capacity adds; higher HBM prices are bullish for AI demand but negative for AVGO gross margin.

catalysts.event: Anthropic public S-1 / institutional roadshow / possible IPO pricing
catalysts.why_it_moves: Anthropic is expected to be Broadcom's largest XPU customer in 2027 and the tenant behind the XPV lease Backstop (max ~$29B) and the $42B convertible-note facility. A funded, well-received IPO de-risks both the 5 GW TPU ramp and the credit overhang; a delay or weak pricing does the opposite. The S-1 will also disclose the size and terms of the compute commitments.
catalysts.watch: Public S-1 filing; disclosed compute commitments to Google/Broadcom and the Fluidstack/XPV leases; pricing versus the $965B Series H mark; any delay announcement.

catalysts.event: Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft and Amazon Q3 results and first 2027 capex guides
catalysts.why_it_moves: Google TPU and Meta MTIA spending is Broadcom revenue. 2027 capex growth is expected to slow from ~79% to ~35%; a weaker guide would hit the multiple, a stronger one would support the $115B FY27 plan.
catalysts.watch: 2027 capex ranges, Alphabet TPU commentary (Broadcom vs MediaTek), Meta MTIA scale-up, any mention of data-center power/shell delays.

catalysts.event: China SASAC decision on Broadcom switches in state-backed data centres
catalysts.why_it_moves: The survey found Broadcom switches in up to ~90% of state-owned data centres and is also examining bundling. Informal 'domestic chips' guidance would cut China networking sales and add an antitrust-style overhang.
catalysts.watch: Reports of informal procurement guidance favouring Huawei/H3C/Ruijie, any SAMR bundling probe, and management quantifying China switch exposure.

catalysts.event: XPV follow-on debt deal (~$70-80B, reported) for Anthropic/OpenAI compute
catalysts.why_it_moves: Pricing and demand for the next tranche is the market's cleanest read on XPV credit risk; a new tranche also enlarges Broadcom's contingent exposure.
catalysts.watch: Deal size, spread, Broadcom's Backstop terms on the new tranche, rating-agency and credit-strategist commentary.

catalysts.event: Nvidia Q3 FY27 results
catalysts.why_it_moves: Sector sentiment on AI capex; AVGO has traded with the group since the September 'pace the frontier' sell-off.
catalysts.watch: Data-center guide versus the $108B revenue outlook; comments on customer ASIC competition and power constraints.

catalysts.event: Broadcom Q4 FY26 results, FY27 outlook and annual dividend increase (after close; date from aggregators, not yet announced by Broadcom)
catalysts.why_it_moves: The first hard checkpoint on the $115B FY27 AI plan. The Q3 print fell despite a beat because the Q4 guide was light; this print sets the Q1 FY27 guide and the tone for the $230B FY28 target.
catalysts.watch: Q4 AI revenue vs $21.7B guide and total vs $34.8B; Q1 FY27 AI guide (needs a run-rate consistent with ~$29B/quarter average for $115B); explicit reaffirmation of $115B/$230B and >$30 FY28 EPS; gross margin vs ~73%; XPV Backstop balance and any convertible notes issued; Google share comments; dividend raise.

catalysts.event: Hyperscaler Q4 results and finalized 2027 capex budgets
catalysts.why_it_moves: Locks in the capex envelope that funds FY27 XPU and networking shipments.
catalysts.watch: Year-over-year 2027 capex growth versus the ~35% expectation; Google TPU generation vendor split.

catalysts.event: Broadcom Q1 FY27 results
catalysts.why_it_moves: First quarter of the FY27 ramp: shows whether the Anthropic TPU 8i (5 GW) and OpenAI (1.3 GW) deployments start on schedule.
catalysts.watch: AI revenue run-rate versus the $115B path, gross margin trend, 10-Q update on XPV Backstop and note-facility draws.

risks.risk: Frontier-lab deployment or funding slip (Anthropic, OpenAI) pushes FY27 AI revenue well under $115B and turns XPV into a live credit issue.
risks.signpost: Anthropic IPO delayed or priced well below the Series H mark; OpenAI stays private into late 2027; any convertible notes issued under the $42B facility in a 10-Q; management softening '$115B' to timing language on land/power/shell readiness.

risks.risk: Google moves TPU volume to MediaTek faster than Macquarie's 95% -> 80% -> 65% (2026-28) path.
risks.signpost: Alphabet or supply-chain reports of MediaTek winning next-gen TPU volume; Broadcom declining to quantify Google revenue for FY27; further sell-side FY28 EPS cuts.

risks.risk: The multiple compresses further on AI-capex digestion fears (the 12-20x range explains most of the outcome spread).
risks.signpost: 2027 hyperscaler capex growth guided below ~35%; a renewed 'pace the frontier' policy push; the stock closing below the $289.96 52-week low while estimates hold.

risks.risk: Gross-margin dilution and China: memory-heavy XPUs/racks and a SASAC substitution push.
risks.signpost: Gross margin guided below ~73% for Q1 FY27; formal or informal SASAC procurement guidance against Broadcom switches.

trade.position: 2 sh (~$699, 7.0% of the $10,000 book); size limited by the supervisor's 8% cap
trade.entry: Two tranches: half now, half after the Q4 FY26 report (expected 2026-12-10), or earlier on a close below ~$300 with the FY27/FY28 AI targets reaffirmed. The share ladder adds to 3 sh at ~$318 and trims to 1 sh at ~$360.
trade.exit_or_add: Exit on a close below $261 (thesis break, ~10% under the 52-week low, ~13.5x FY27 EPS) or on a cut to the $115B FY27 AI plan. Add, up to the 8% cap, after a clean Q4 print that reaffirms $115B/$230B, or on a drop to ~$300-318 with the roadmap intact. Trim toward 1 sh above ~$360 without new information; take profit at $522.

what_changes_our_mind: The Q4 FY26 print (~Dec 10) guides Q1 FY27 AI revenue below a run-rate consistent with $115B, or management stops reaffirming the $230B FY28 target.
Anthropic's IPO is pulled or priced sharply below its $965B private mark, or a 10-Q shows convertible notes issued under the $42B facility or a payment under the lease Backstop.

Distribution: mixture of lognormals, bear 25% (median $150, sigma 0.42), base 50% ($285, 0.35), bull 25% ($470, 0.42), giving a median ~$280 and effective vol ~75-85%, below the 112% trailing realized vol (inflated by a 5x run and short-report shocks) but far above large-cap base rates. The far-left tail is kept fatter than the mixture (P>=72 0.97, P>=115 0.92) because the stock was $61 a year ago. Research: ~14 round-1 queries plus 5 round-2 searches/fetches; no option data used.

agents.method_text: Blend of forward P/E (50%, $272 = FY2027 consensus EPS $4.93 x 55x), EV/sales on 2028E revenue (30%, $258 = $9.0B x 9x + ~$2.45B equity-adjusted net cash, / 323M diluted shares) and a DCF (20%, $158, now including net cash). Blended fair value ~$245, about 15% below the $288.70 close.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY2027 non-GAAP EPS $4.93 (Alpha Vantage consensus, 28 analysts, range $2.95-$7.01; up from $4.36 90 days ago) x 55x. That is ~39x my own FY2028 EPS extrapolation of ~$7.00 (+40%; there is no FY28 consensus), which is what the market will price in Sep 2027. Premium to electrical-equipment peers for 40%+ growth, well below today's ~77x NTM P/E. Unchanged from round 1; net cash is already reflected in EPS via interest income.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: 2028E revenue $9.0B (FY2027 consensus $6.79B +33%, my extrapolation) x 9x EV/sales = $81B EV, plus ~$2.45B equity-adjusted net cash ($2.67B cash at 6/30/26 less ~$0.2B financing obligations; the $2.475B of 0% 2030 converts are in the money at ~$194.97 conversion and their ~12.6M shares are already in the 323.3M diluted count, so they are treated as equity), / 323M diluted shares = ~$258.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Valued as of Sep 2027. Revenue $4.05B (2026) growing 60%/40%/30%/25%/20% to ~$17.7B in 2031. Terminal FCF margin 18%, WACC 10%, terminal growth 5%. Terminal value ~$67B discounted to ~$43B, plus ~$5.5B PV of interim FCF = ~$48.5B EV, plus ~$2.45B net cash = ~$51B equity / 323M shares = ~$158. Very sensitive: 15% margin, 11% WACC, 4% growth gives ~$100.

agents.reasoning: Round 2. Bloom Energy is at $288.70 after a +317% year on an AI on-site-power inflection: 2Q26 revenue $1.065B (+166%), non-GAAP GM 34.3%, EPS $0.78, OCF +$226M, FY26 guide raised to $3.9-4.2B / $2.55-2.85 EPS; FY2027 consensus $6.79B / $4.93 EPS (rising). The supervisor showed my round-1 ~$1.5B net cash was unsupported: cash was $2.67B at 6/30/26 and the $2.475B of 0% 2030 converts (issued Oct 2025, conversion ~$194.97) are in the money and already in the 323.3M diluted count, so equity-adjusted net cash is ~$2.45B. I accept that; it lifts EV/sales to ~$258 (+$3) and, because my round-1 DCF equity value had effectively omitted cash, lifts the DCF to ~$158 (+$8). P/E is unchanged. Blended fair value rises from $243 to ~$245. On Jupiter I verified: Oracle's Sep 24 notice went to developer Blue Owl as a lease-deferral right; Oracle and Blue Owl reaffirmed and Bloom says the 2.4 GW contract stands; the NM Supreme Court lifted its stay Sep 17, but NMED has not appointed a hearing officer and the permit deadline is Nov 23; Morgan Stanley (Overweight, $310) estimates >= $8B equipment backlog, more than half non-Oracle, and notes Jupiter is outside 2026 guidance. I folded the permit/pipeline risk into the bear case instead of giving it a separate scenario, because it is mainly a timing risk to 2027-28 revenue and not a backlog loss, and I trimmed the bear weight from 25% to 23% and raised the bear price to $135 (net cash). Scenario mean ~$305 (0.23x135 + 0.52x295 + 0.25x480). I move my median from $275 to ~$282, still below spot because my fundamental value ($245) is below spot and multiple compression from ~59x FY27 EPS absorbs most 2028 growth. Distribution: lognormal-ish around $282 with sigma ~0.75 (below the 112% realized vol but far above the large-cap ±25-35% base rate), with slightly fatter left tail at the lowest strikes. P(>= spot) ~0.485, P(>= $144) ~0.815, P(>= $577, 2x) ~0.165. Research used ~5 extra searches in round 2.

The change is therefore a nudge of about 0.5pt, not a settled disagreement that clearly matters.

agents.reasoning: Primary-document build. The Q3 2026 10-Q, release and transcript give actuals (room nights 345M +7%, gross bookings $54.5B +10%, adjusted revenue $9.79B, take rate -15 bp) and the Q4 guide (room nights 1-3%, adjusted revenue 0-2%, EBITDA about flat). The $900M FTC revenue reduction plus a $100M accrual is booked as a one-off and an equity adjustment. The record: annual first revenue guides were beaten in FY2024 (+3.4% vs mid) and FY2025 (+8.0%), but FY2026's first guide (low double digits) is now a ~3% miss, so I give no beat premium. Drivers: room nights from global travel demand (UN Tourism 2026 cut to +1-2%) plus a share-gain spread narrowed from ~4.5 pts to ~2 for AI and competition; ADR +3% (CFO); take rate down 10 bp/yr on flights mix; marketing flat as a share of GB; non-marketing opex +6.6% net of the $650M transformation run-rate. FY2027 revenue is $31.4B (consensus $31.5B, StockAnalysis 2026-11-13) and EPS ~$11.7 (consensus adjusted $12.23, ~4% below). Buybacks of ~$9B/yr cut shares 6.5%/yr. Valuation: P/E on horizon NTM EPS, exit 14.6x from the k = 0.8 shrink of 13.1x toward the 22.5x two-peer median, giving a research target (12m) of $184.82 (+17%). The downside (P10, $123) and upside (P90, $243) move room nights, take rate and marketing and ±3 turns of multiple; the left tail is fatter, consistent with 39% realized volatility. The room-night spread is the biggest judgment call (±7-10%), flagged for Kilian. Research was limited: numeric Q2/Q3 2026 quarter guides and a 2027 UN Tourism forecast were not found, and the SEC refused direct curl (filings read via WebFetch and the cached companyfacts).

agents.reasoning: Facts: Q3 2026 beat its own guide on every line (room nights +7%, adjusted revenue +9%, adj. EBITDA +9%; GAAP revenue -1% after a $900M FTC revenue reduction; src 1,3). But the CFO guided Q4 to room nights +1-3% and adjusted revenue +0-2%, citing October Middle East and European disruption (src 3). Industry lane: Expedia guided Q4 bookings down from +11% to +3-5% and fell 12%, with its CFO naming the same geopolitical headwinds (src 10,11,12). Airbnb accelerated (src 13), which shows that share in alternative accommodations is contested. UN Tourism cut 2026 arrivals growth to 1-2% (src 14,15). U.S. hotel ADR/RevPAR were firm in late October (src 25), and CoStar raised its 2026-27 outlook (src 16). AI agents: Google's partner list runs through the OTAs (src 18), but Meta Muse direct-booking fears hit the group in September (src 19,24). BKNG says LLM referrals are <1% of room nights (CFO, src 3). Build: four quarterly drivers. Room nights +2.5% in Q4 (inside the guide, below the record-adjusted 297.7M) and +5% in 2027-28. GB per room night +1-3%. Take rate -10 bp in 2027 on flight mix. GAAP margin +30 bp a year from transformation savings net of investment. FY2027 revenue $31.0B (1.5% below the $31.5B consensus) and GAAP EPS $11.67 (4.6% below the $12.23 adjusted consensus, src 9): moderately conservative per rule 0c. Value: one P/E leg; the exit 14.3x comes from the k = 0.8 shrink of the own 13.1x toward the 2-peer median of 22.5x, less 0.3x for regulation. Research target (12m) $180.89 (+14.8%). Downside P10 $116 (volume, take and margin cuts plus de-rating to ~11x) and upside P90 $234 give a fatter left tail, consistent with 39% realized vol and AI-disintermediation risk. agents.reasoning: Skeptic lane. Q3 FY2026 (10-Q/release 2026-11-03) beat its guide (room nights +6.7% vs 3-5%) but the CFO guided Q4 room nights to +1-3%, adjusted revenue +0-2% and adjusted EBITDA flat on investments, and cited end-of-quarter moderation and October disruptions (corrected transcript, Steenbergen). Reported revenue fell 1% because of a $900M FTC revenue reduction plus a $100M accrual for Priceline's B2B supply to deceptive third-party sites (Reuters/Techlicious; SF City Attorney suit), not yet paid. Litigation stack: EU hotel parity collective action (18,135 hotels, several billion euros, hearings 2027), Dutch consumer claims EUR 965M (jurisdiction upheld 2026-10-28), Spain EUR 413M fine under appeal. AI: Google moved agentic hotel booking into AI Mode in the US (Skift 2026-08-27) with Booking as a partner; LLM referrals are <1% of room nights (CFO). Sell-side mostly Buy but cutting (Wells Fargo EW $190; Feb 2026 cuts up to 23% on AI fears); Morgan Stanley sees AI as a channel and online travel +7% a year. Build: quarterly drivers (room nights, $/room night, take rate, marketing % bookings, fixed costs) calibrated to the supplements; FY2027 revenue $30,987M (-1.6% vs MarketScreener consensus $31,505M), EBIT $10,642M (-4.7% vs $11,162M), EPS ~$11.5 (-3% vs $11.85); NTM EPS at the horizon ~$12.2 vs consensus ~$13.5 (-10%: we have no share gains, continued take-rate dilution and +5% fixed costs). Valued at 14.2x (k-rule on a 2-peer median, less 0.75 turn AI risk) minus probability-weighted litigation. Downside/upside move the drivers and the multiple to genuine 1-in-10 cases; left tail fatter. Sources: 12 of 23 in lane; of the 16 non-company-filing/transcript sources, 12 (75%) are lane kinds (litigation, regulatory, critical press, target cuts, AI-threat trade press). Research limits: Nasdaq/Zacks consensus API not reachable (blocked), Twelve Data estimates need a higher plan; FY2027 consensus taken from MarketScreener.

memo.title: BKNG: low-conviction Long sized for portfolio fit. Trough multiple and buybacks against an unresolved AI-agent overhang
memo.call_reason: Low-conviction, portfolio-fit Long. The target ($179.61) is above the $163.31 price, but the supervisor rated sizing conviction low (0.52), below the medium minimum. The owner took it anyway on 2026-10-01 as a deliberate exception, replacing Microchip, because it lifted the book's forward Sharpe the most (0.594 to 0.66) and correlates only about 0.10 with AVGO.
memo.one_liner: Booking trades at about 13.7x NTM consensus, at its 2022 trough, while buybacks shrink the share count 6-8% a year. That supports a $179.61 12-month target and a $194 research target (12m). The stock-specific edge is thin (an idiosyncratic de-rating has beaten SPY only half the time), so this is a capped 6-share position held mainly because it diversifies a book otherwise driven by AI semis and power.

thesis.point: 1. The valuation already prices a lot of damage.
thesis.evidence: At $163.31 BKNG is about 13.7x NTM consensus (FY2027 EPS $12.37, 33 analysts, flat over 90 days). The supervisor rebuilt realized-forward P/E history: the ex-COVID median is about 19x, with troughs of about 15x (2011-12), 16.7x (2018) and 11.3-13.8x (2022). The FCF yield is about 7.8% on LTM FCF of $9.54B. A flat multiple plus EPS growth alone gets to about $180 by Sep 2027.

thesis.point: 2. Buybacks turn mid-single-digit volume growth into mid-teens EPS growth.
thesis.evidence: There were 751.4M shares on Jul 27, 2026. About 22M were retired in Q2, and $14.5B of authorization remains, so the count shrinks 6-8% a year. Q2 FCF was $3.6B (+16% y/y). FY2026 consensus EPS of $10.45 is +14.6% on FY2025's split-adjusted $9.12.

thesis.point: 3. The AI-agent fear is running ahead of the numbers.
thesis.evidence: The CEO says AI-generated traffic is 'significantly below 1%' of room nights. In Q2 room nights grew +5% and marketing was 4.7% of gross bookings, with no sign yet of lost share or rising marketing intensity. Booking is a hotel partner in Google's agentic AI Mode and has an ad deal with OpenAI. The Sep 23 sell-off came from Expedia's Meta Muse deal, which is a headline and not a number in Booking's results.

memo.variant_view: There is no real variant view against the Street, and our target is below it. Our $179.61 target sits under every one of the 35 analyst targets (weighted median $234.34, low $188), because we do not assume the market closes the AI discount within 12 months: the forecast median ($178-180) is below our own $194 research target (12m). Our view differs mainly from the options market. The options-only distribution centres at $165.64 with P(gain) 0.513, against our blended P(gain) of 0.591 and expected value of $190.51. The research adds roughly 8pp of upside probability from the trough multiple and the buyback math. That gap is modest and the supervisor treats it as thin edge, so the case for owning BKNG here rests as much on what it does for the book as on beating consensus.

valuation.methods: Supervisor's reconciled research target (12m) is $194 (agents $187-198, mean $194.4). It blends two methods. P/E (weight 0.6): NTM EPS at Sep 2027 of about $13.3 (FY2027 consensus $12.37 less 2%, FY2028 about +12.5-13%) x 14.5x = $193. FCF yield (weight 0.4): FY2027 FCF of about $10.45B over about 700M average diluted shares = about $14.9 per share at a 7.6% yield = $196. It then deducts about $1-2 for expected legal costs. The 12-month target is $179.61, the median of the blended distribution, which puts 0.67 weight on the options market and 0.33 on research. The expected value is $190.51 and P(gain) is 0.591.

catalysts.why_it_moves: The overhang sets the multiple, not yet the earnings. A Booking deal with Meta or OpenAI would remove the 'shut out' fear. A new rival deal or adoption data would extend the de-rating.
catalysts.watch: Partner announcements, agent booking volumes, AI referral share to booking.com month by month

catalysts.event: SHCA's third and final expansion of the Amsterdam hotel price-parity collective action (to about 18,000 hotels from 10,783)

catalysts.watch: Size of the filing and any damages figure claimed; the court's expert phase on market definition

catalysts.event: FTC decision on whether to sue Priceline over fees, disclosures and billing (staff recommended a complaint in July 2026), or a settlement
catalysts.why_it_moves: It is a headline risk. The Hopper base rate ($35M) suggests a small cost, but a complaint would add to sentiment while the stock is already de-rated.
catalysts.watch: FTC complaint filing or consent order; required changes to Priceline's fee practices

catalysts.event: Strait of Hormuz traffic normalisation (Kalshi: about 17% by Jan 1, 32% by Apr 1, 48% by Jul 1, 2027)
catalysts.why_it_moves: A reopening revives long-haul and Middle East travel and makes the H1 2027 comparison easy. Continued closure keeps that tailwind out.
catalysts.watch: Kalshi curve, Q4 guide commentary on Middle East room nights, oil price

catalysts.event: Q4/FY2026 results and first FY2027 outlook (FY2025 was reported Feb 18, 2026)
catalysts.why_it_moves: FY2027 guidance tests the $12.37 consensus that the whole valuation rests on, and shows the payoff from the transformation savings and the buyback pace
catalysts.watch: FY2027 room-night and EPS growth guide, marketing-intensity outlook, buyback authorization

risks.risk: AI agents start routing demand around Booking. Room-night growth falls to 0-2% and marketing intensity rises (the $118-122 bear case, 20-25% probability).
risks.signpost: Marketing above about 5% of gross bookings, room nights below the +3% low end of guidance, a Muse/Expedia volume disclosure, or Booking left out of the Meta and OpenAI agent platforms

risks.risk: The multiple stays at the trough. Idiosyncratic BKNG drawdowns with SPY near its high have beaten SPY only 11 of 22 times (the 2019 Google-scare analogue returned -0.1% against SPY's +8%).
risks.signpost: A clean Q3 print that fails to re-rate the stock; continued target cuts (Truist cut to $216 on Sep 30)

risks.risk: Travel demand shock: Hormuz stays shut through mid-2027, oil spikes, or a consumer slowdown hits.
risks.signpost: Kalshi Hormuz odds falling further; a Q4 room-night guide below +3%; weaker hotel RevPAR prints

risks.signpost: FTC files suit, or the SHCA claim states a damages figure in the billions

trade.position: 6 sh (~$980, 9.8% of the $10,000 book). This is a low-conviction exception sized at the supervisor's 10% cap, which is the binding limit. Loss at the stop is about $260, or 2.6% of the book.
trade.entry: Supervisor plan: two tranches. Buy 3 shares now near $163 and 3 after the Q3 2026 print (most likely Nov 3-5), provided the print does not show the AI tell (marketing above 4.7% of gross bookings with room nights below guidance).
trade.exit_or_add: Exit on a close below $120, the thesis break: about 9.7x FY2027 EPS, which needs a fundamental break. Also exit if the Q3 or Q4 print shows marketing intensity rising with room nights of 0-2%. Exit or swap if a re-solve shows the Sharpe lift is gone, for example if a medium-conviction name now adds more to the book or BKNG's correlation to holdings rises, because portfolio fit is the main reason we own it. Take profit at $232.69, near the Street median. Do not add beyond 6 shares while conviction is low and the 10% cap binds. Adding needs conviction raised to medium, for example after a Booking agent-distribution deal or a clean Q3 print with stable marketing intensity.

what_changes_our_mind: Q3 2026 (about Nov 3-5): marketing above 4.7% of gross bookings together with room nights below the +3-5% guide. That would be the first sign that AI agents are hitting the earnings and not only the multiple. We would exit.

Booking announces an agent-distribution deal with Meta Muse or OpenAI, or discloses agent-driven bookings growing through its own rails. That would remove the 'shut out' fear and would justify raising conviction to medium and completing or adding to the position.

Book re-solve: if BKNG no longer gives the biggest Sharpe lift (for example a medium-conviction candidate beats 0.66, or its correlation to AVGO and the rest of the book rises well above about 0.10), the portfolio-fit reason for this exception is gone and we would rotate out.

tax_assumptions._tax_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: taxable account; ~$20,000 internship wages in 2026 plus realized gains; claimed as a dependent by a parent living in CA; full-time student under 24 living in CT. Assumed (not confirmed): domicile stays CA (a student living away at school keeps the parents' domicile, FTB Pub 1031), CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode so CT does not tax investment income; kiddie tax applies (earned income not more than half of his support). tax_assumptions._other_unearned_note: Dividends etc. this year (rough: GOOGL + META dividends). Counts toward the kiddie-tax threshold.
tax_assumptions._kiddie_note: Unearned income above $2,700 (2 x $1,350, Rev. Proc. 2025-32) is taxed at the parent's rate, federal (Form 8615) and CA (FTB 3800). Applies to a full-time student 19-23 whose earned income is not more than half of his own support.
tax_assumptions._parent_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: parent in NYC, 37% federal bracket. Parent's NY/NYC rates do not apply to Kilian's gains (no NY kiddie tax under Form 8615).
tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. Net losses offset gains; up to $3,000 deducts at the own short-term rate. Bracket mode (mode 'brackets') still holds the CA schedule and is not updated.
tax_assumptions._short_term_all_note: Kilian 2026-10-28 card 'Assume short-term on all' (thread 'Fix AMAT target vs sell mismatch'): every holding is assumed sold within the year at the short-term rate, so a trim only pays the same tax H years sooner; band per year = q tau (1 - (1+d)^-H) / H + spread / T. Overrides lot_aware_horizon; false restores it.
tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. Long-term lots keep the T-year rule (years_until_you_would_otherwise_sell, future_rate_on_deferred_gains, Claude defaults 2026-09-28). false restores the T-year rule for every lot.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: horizon NTM adjusted EPS ~$9.0 (our build: FY28 $8.54, FY29 $8.86) x 16.5x; peer median 22.6x shrunk to CRDO's 15.2x with k=0.8

inputs_detail.value: actual 1.26-1.67; Q2 FY27 1.40 falling to 1.09 (Q4 FY28) and 1.05 (Q4 FY29)
inputs_detail.derivation: Actual quarters = (reported revenue - estimated optical) / ai_capex: 1.26, 1.28, 1.67, 1.54, 1.48 (Q1 FY26-Q1 FY27), i.e. capture already fell from its Q3 FY26 peak as capex grew faster than cable revenue. Forecast: Q2 FY27 1.40 (copper ~$474M, consistent with inventory up $62M q/q to $313M and $213M non-cancelable supply commitments [1][2]); then ~-4.5%/quarter to 1.09 by Q4 FY28 as (a) 1.6T AEC competition arrives: Marvell demonstrated 800G/1.6T AECs at SC26 [16] and settled its patent challenges with Credo [15]; MaxLinear's CEO Kishore Seendripu (competitor, not a Credo statement) targets 20-30% of 1.6T cables [19]; Cisco sought quotes for a proprietary 1.6T cable program [20]; (b) the CEO Bill Brennan said 1.6T AEC comes in 'in a much bigger way' in FY28 [13], which offsets part of the share loss; then -1%/quarter in FY29 as share settles. Other evidence-based builds: consensus FY28 revenue $3.88B [18] (copper capture held ~1.25 through FY28, +~$0.4B revenue); share held at ~93-99% (no competitor ramp) = upside case; share falling to ~70% in 1.6T = downside case.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Consensus-like path (capture ~1.25 held) adds ~$0.4B FY28 revenue and ~+$15/share; a fast share loss is the downside case.

inputs_detail.derivation: Optical revenue is not disclosed. FY26 base estimated at $63M (8/12/18/25 by quarter) and Q1 FY27 $35M (record optical DSP plus first PIC revenue per Bill Brennan, CEO [14]); flag: low confidence, it only splits the reported total. Forecast optical revenue = capture x capex: Q2 FY27 0.18 (~$61M), Q3 0.45 (~$170M), Q4 0.70 (~$291M) = FY27 ~$556M, 7% below the CEO's 'more than $600 million' [13] because three new product lines (ZeroFlap, PICs, 1.6T DSP) all have to ramp in 2H, and the record on multi-product new ramps is untested (first PIC revenue only in Q1). FY28 0.66-0.62 ($1.26B) and FY29 0.62-0.66 ($1.44B): exit run-rate held roughly flat as a share of capex while optics peers (LITE, COHR, MRVL post-Lumentum) compete. Other builds: management's >$600M (+$45M FY27); each of three lines >$100M [13] is a floor (~$300M+) = downside.
inputs_detail.variant_view: At management's >$600M FY27 and the same exit share, FY28 optics would be ~$1.36B (+$0.1B), ~+$4/share.

inputs_detail.derivation: Actual quarters: (non-GAAP operating income - estimated optical revenue x 20%) / copper revenue = 0.44, 0.48, 0.51, 0.51, 0.50. Forecast 0.51 in Q2 FY27 (Q2 guide midpoint implies 48.7% total: 530 x 68% - 102.5 opex), 0.53 in 2H FY27 (operating leverage: Daniel Fleming, CFO, guided FY27 non-GAAP opex +55% y/y = ~$420M on >85% revenue growth [13]); 0.52 in FY28 and 0.50 in FY29 as AEC pricing meets Marvell/MaxLinear competition [15][16][19]. Alternative: company-implied ~51% total FY27 operating margin (68% GM - 16.8% opex) = +~1pt.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Company-implied FY27 total margin ~51% (+1-2pt) [13].

agents.reasoning: Primary-document build. Q1 FY27 (Ex 99.1, 10-Q): revenue $479.0M, non-GAAP op margin 48.2%, cash $764M after the $1.25B DustPhotonics deal ($770M cash, $169M shares, $310M earnout), customers A/B 43%/28%, inventory $313M, $213M supply commitments. Q1 call (speakers named): CFO Daniel Fleming guides Q2 $525-535M, FY27 growth >85%, opex +55%, GM ~flat, ~200M shares; CEO Bill Brennan says >$600M optical in FY27 and 1.6T AEC 'much bigger' in FY28. Guidance record: 7/7 quarterly revenue beats, but the beat fell from +12-20% to +1.6-1.9% in the last two quarters, so we sit at the top of the Q2 range rather than the record-adjusted $596M. Since mid-August the stock fell >50%: AEC competition (Marvell 1.6T AECs at SC26, patent settlement 11-17; MaxLinear's CEO targets 20-30% of 1.6T; Cisco's 1.6T cable quotes), a sector multiple compression (peers down 25-45% in a month; TD Cowen and Stifel cut targets on multiples, not demand), and concentration. Drivers: AI capex from the standing file (base) x a copper capture that falls ~25% by FY28 (share loss) and an optical capture that ramps from ~0.1 to ~0.65 $M per $B. Result: FY27 $2,494M (in line with consensus), FY28 $3,531M (-9% vs $3.88B consensus), FY28 EPS $8.54 (-12%). Valuation: P/E 16.5x (peer median 22.6x shrunk with k=0.8 to CRDO's 15.2x) and a 3.0% FCF yield (departure from the 1.9% default, carded in gap_note: peers' trailing yields embed +50-98% growth that CRDO will not have at the horizon). Downside (P10 $70) moves capex, share, optics, margins and multiple together; upside (P90 $288) is share retained plus optics beat. Research limits: Twelve Data estimates unavailable on this plan; StockAnalysis/MarketBeat pages fetched were cached from 2025 and not used; peer consensus snapshot is 2026-10-23 (flagged). Not driver-linked: none.

agents.method_text: Blend of forward P/E (24x Sep-2027 NTM non-GAAP EPS ~$10.4 = $250, 50%), a 5-year DCF at 12% WACC on a lower FY28 FCF of $1.45B ($197, 30%) and EV/NTM sales of 11x on ~$4.2B ($234, 20%). The result is about $231, roughly 9% above the $210.97 close (down from $244 in round 1 after cutting the net-cash, FCF-conversion and concentration assumptions).

agents.reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's findings changed five things. (1) Tax: the P/E leg runs on adjusted EPS, so it takes the company-stated 26.0% non-GAAP rate (src 29; Q3 adjusted 25.3%) instead of GAAP history 23.5% (about -3%). (2) Exit multiple on one date and one vintage: peers at 2026-11-24 closes and 2026-11-25 Zacks consensus give a whole-company median of 14.55x (MTZ 13.0x, PRIM 11.95x, MYRG 16.1x, PWR 30.2x), not 17.1x at 2026-11-02 prices; STRL moves to segment-only; own 10.2x; k=0.8 -> 11.0x (was 11.3x). EV/EBITDA: 12.35x peer median, own 8.2x -> 8.2x. (3) Supplier finance: 204.4 of the 524.0 program (the excess over the FY26 year-end balance scaled by revenue) is treated as debt. (4) FTTH share: the 9M arithmetic (Comms +17% YTD = ~+701 with FTTH +50%, src 4) does not fit 31%: solving it gives FY26 FTTH ~1,650 and FY27 ~2,320 (~38%); FY28 -15% (-348, the same dollar cut as round 1) keeps FY28 Comms at +4.5%, inside 'mid-single-digit', and FY29 +8% (CEO: accelerating). I keep FTTH below the supervisor's 44% because DCI, copper and M&O also grew in 9M. (5) DMV moratoria (Loudoun pause adopted 2026-11-18, Maryland county pauses; src 30, 31): new legislative applications are held, by-right and under-construction work continues, so I haircut Building Systems 3% in FY28 and 5% in FY29 on top of the labor cap (FY28 +14.5%, below 'high teens or better'). Q4 FY27 is now built just above the guide (1,715) from Q3 momentum; it moves value only through net debt. Result: adjusted EPS ~17.15 / 18.96 / 22.13 (within 1% of pre-print consensus for FY28-29), research target (12m) $235.93 (was $252.17): P/E 228.35 (0.75), EV/EBITDA 258.69 (0.25). Scenarios keep the playbook's drivers (FTTH, DCI, copper/BEAD, Building Systems capture, margin, multiple): P10 $116.84, P90 $362.51. Where I differ from the supervisor's set (273.65 on 13.0x): I reprice the exit at today's price because the peers' own prices and consensus moved too, and the k rule is about the current gap. Research limited to ~6 new queries.

(1) Margins restated on the company's segment adjusted EBITDA basis (round 1 mixed EBITA and EBITDA): Comms 12.3/12.5/12.9%, BS 20.5/19.5/19.0%; engine EBIT = that less segment depreciation. memo.title: Dycom: no buy today. Research target (12m) $294.37 says cheap, but the blended 12-month target $231.80 (+4.9%) clears no hurdle; revisit at or under ~$206 or on the late-November Q3 FY27 print
memo.call_reason: The published 12-month target $231.80 is only +4.9% above $221.05, below DY's 12.3% beta-adjusted required return (binding: below_beta_return, so the book buys 0 shares), and rubric conviction is low; the price is above its Entry below level of about $206.42.
memo.one_liner: Kilian's driver build, with the middle trim to the Communications backlog path he chose on 2026-11-02 at 7:26 p.m. ET, values Dycom at a research target (12m) of $294.37 (+33%) on only 13.2x NTM EPS, and insiders bought in September, but the options market (12-month median $208.08, P(gain) 46%) weighs 67% of the published target and sees a carrier-capex slowdown after AT&T's 10-21 capex cut and MasTec's Communications slump. We do not buy today; we buy at or under about $206, or re-underwrite after the late-November Q3 FY27 print shows whether Communications backlog is still growing.

thesis.point: The driver build (approved set plus Kilian's middle backlog trim) gives a research target (12m) of $294.37, +33% from $221.05, on a multiple well below peers.
thesis.evidence: Horizon NTM P/E 13.2x (own 12.13x today vs 18.65x whole-company peer median of MTZ, PWR, PRIM, MYRG) weighted 0.7 ($288.63) and LTM EV/EBITDA 10.2x on pro-forma own EBITDA weighted 0.3 ($307.76); the five independent forecasts, made before the trim, span $299.55-$315.37 (the trim takes -2.7% off the untrimmed $302.46). Build EPS FY27 ~18.3-18.5 vs Zacks 15.98 and StockAnalysis 17.06.

thesis.point: Demand is slowing, not breaking: Communications backlog is flat while carrier capex is trimmed, and BEAD and long-haul land mostly after the 12-month horizon.
thesis.evidence: DY NTM Communications backlog 5,376 (Q1 FY27) -> 5,362 (Q2 FY27), flat; the path now in the set (Kilian's middle trim, 2026-11-02 7:26 p.m. ET) needs 5,420 in Q3 and 5,580 in Q4 (was 5,450 / 5,650), then +1.75% a quarter in FY28 and +1.5% in FY29. AT&T cut 2027-28 capital investment to $22-23B a year from $23-24B but kept >60M fiber locations by 2030; Verizon held 2026 capex at $16-16.5B. MasTec Communications backlog fell 7.5% q/q (flat y/y) with customer deferrals. All 56 BEAD final proposals are approved; >270,000 route miles, ~58% buried, construction 'in earnest' in FY28.

thesis.point: Insiders bought near current levels and the company keeps beating its own guide, which supports the base case through the Q3 print.
thesis.evidence: Open-market purchases: CEO 850 shares at $296.76 (09-09), directors 700 at $286.92 (09-01) and 350 at $280.62 (09-23). Q3 FY27 guide adj. EPS $4.33-4.79; the build carries ~5.2, Street 4.33 (whisper 4.55, 80% range 4.24-4.88), after six straight EPS beats of the guide midpoint.

memo.variant_view: Two consensus views bracket us. Sell-side analysts (11, Strong Buy, median $525, mean $520.91, range $375-625, as of 10-09) are stale, set mostly May-September before the 61% fall from $566.47, and get zero weight in the target. The options market's 12-month distribution is the other pole: median $208.08 (below spot), 15th-85th range $111.42-$312.30, P(gain) 46%, with 1-year implied volatility ~60%. Our research leg (median $268.97, P(gain) 63.5%) is more constructive because the build follows DY's beat record and puts BEAD, long-haul and data-center work into the multiple; the published blend (67% market, 33% research) lands at $231.80. So the variant view is real on value (research target (12m) $294.37 vs options median $208) but not strong enough to clear the hurdle at today's price: the market is pricing a carrier capex slowdown (AT&T's 10-21 cut, MasTec's deferrals) that our path reflects only in part even after the middle trim Kilian chose on the supervisor's recommendation (four of five forecasters and the supervisor had called the original approved path full). Events past the 12-month horizon cut both ways and are weighed through the multiple: FTTH programs mature around 2030-32 (p 0.45, about -$12/sh), BEAD and long-haul extend Communications past the FTTH peak (p 0.5, about +$10/sh), a data-center construction turn in CY2028-29 (p 0.25, about -$10/sh), and carrier consolidation pricing (p 0.3, about -$6/sh); keeping ~29% of DY's discount to peers (exit k=0.8) is how the visible FTTH end date is priced.

tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. Net losses offset gains; up to $3,000 deducts at the own short-term rate. Bracket mode (mode 'brackets') still holds the CA schedule and is not updated.

agents.method_text: 60% P/E plus 40% SOTP. The P/E leg is 21x core on CY2028E EPS of $17.0 (= $357), plus about $15/share of after-tax net financial assets, for $372. The SOTP leg is $348. The blend is about $362, against $361 on 2026-10-02.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: At Oct 2027 the market prices CY2028 EPS. Consensus CY2028 EPS is $17.89 (MarketScreener); I trim about 5% for 2027-capex D&A and use $17.0. The core multiple is 21x: inside the 10-peer range of 8.6-33.7x, about 7% above the peer median of 19.6x and below the mega-cap median of 24.4x. That gives $357, plus about $15/share of after-tax net financial assets (cash net of debt, SpaceX, non-marketable book) that consensus EPS does not capture. Total about $372.

inputs_detail.derivation: [citation gate 2026-10-06: $15.10 is not visible at the cited Stock Analysis page (2027+ EPS shown as 'Pro') and 24/7 Wall St names no vendor: not_found. Verified figure: $14.95 (Yahoo, 53 analysts; MarketScreener)]

$17.89 x 0.95. I haircut about 5% for depreciation on 2027 capex. The standing view's Big-4 base is +47% in 2027 ($733B to $1,080B). Applied to Alphabet's $200B 2026 midpoint, that gives about $295B, which the CFO calls a 'significant' increase. At the call's 60% servers / 40% DC mix, that adds about $35-40B a year of run-rate D&A from 2028. I cannot verify how much of it consensus already carries. Equivalent to +12.6% on the $15.10 CY2027 consensus.

Peer CY2027 P/E: median 19.6x, range 8.6-33.7x across 10 names; mega-cap four median 24.4x. GOOGL today is 23.0x all-in, or (347.68-15)/15.10 = 22.0x core. I take 21x, a modest premium to the median that I argue persists through the horizon. GOOGL's CY2027 EPS growth is +27% against a peer median of +15%. Visibility comes from contract, not forecast: $513.9B of Cloud backlog, just over half recognisable within 24 months (10-Q). Margins are top-quartile (Services 41.8%, Cloud 35.6%). I stay below today's 22x because FCF is negative (Q2 -$5.9B), buybacks are zero (10-Q), and capex rises significantly in 2027. [citation gate 2026-10-06: the 19.6x median rests on S&P Global adjusted (ex-SBC) EPS via Stock Analysis, an aggregator basis inconsistent with GOOGL's GAAP consensus. On MarketScreener EPS checked against 10-K GAAP EPS, at Oct 6 closes, the median of this set's comparable names is 21.7x (META 21.7x, MSFT 24.5x, AMZN 24.4x, ORCL 17.9x, CRM 23.0x, RDDT 21.1x, ADBE 11.1x, NOW 59.6x)]

methods.inputs: Services: 2027E OI $175B x (1-18%) x 20 = $2.87T. Cloud: 2027E revenue $150B x 7 = $1.05T. Other Bets/Waymo: $0.15T. Alphabet-level AI costs: -$23.2B x 0.82 x 20 = -$0.38T. Net financial assets: $0.24T, i.e. cash net of debt $40B + other equity $7B + SpaceX $94.1B x 0.85 + non-marketable $131.5B x 0.85. Total $3.93T / 12.30B = $319 today; rolled forward 9% to $348.

agents.reasoning: Delta refresh of my 2026-10-02 file. I re-checked filings first. EDGAR shows no 8-K, 10-Q or proxy since Aug 10; the only new filing is an Oct 2 Form 4. So I re-opened and confirmed every reported figure that feeds my fair value at source: the Q2 8-K, the 10-Q, the Q2 call transcript, and the June 5 and Aug 10 8-Ks. The only company releases are the Oct 6 Constellation PPA (890 MW of uprates, 20 years; a separate 2,700 MW, 15-year supply deal; first uprate 2028; cost undisclosed) and the Sep 30/Oct 1 Gemini 4 Argon preview (Fairwind-only, no GA date). Neither changes a 12-month number. Neither does the stock's move: +1.2% Oct 2-6, in line with QQQ's +1.3%. What did change is consensus. CY2027 EPS is now $15.10 (S&P Global; 24/7 Wall St shows $14.47 to $15.10 in 90 days), against $14.84 in my last file. MarketScreener carries CY2028 at $17.89. I also built the 10-peer comp set my prior file lacked, on one CY2027 basis. Its median is 19.6x P/E and 11.9x EV/EBITDA; GOOGL is at 23.0x all-in and 22.0x core. I now apply 21x core, down from 21.5x and anchored to that peer set, to CY2028E EPS of $17.0 (consensus less about 5% for 2027-capex D&A, sized from the standing capex view: Big-4 2027 base +47%), up from $16.5. With about $15/share of stakes, the P/E leg is $372. The SOTP is unchanged at $348. The blend is $362, against $361. The ladder uses median ≈ fair value $362 (+4%), a fat-tailed lognormal mixture (27% sigma at 70%, 40% at 30%, about 31% effective vs 32% realised), and P(≥ spot) of 0.55. The scenario mean is $368 (22/53/25 at $245/$368/$475), consistent with right skew. Thesis break stays $255. For one month, the Q3 print is about 97% inside the window, two-sided, centred at about $349. Lane: 9 of the 15 non-comp sources are primary (60%). The 30 data pages behind the comp table (3 per peer, required by the 2026-10-03 peer rule) are not counted. No option data was used.

agents.reasoning: Skeptic lane. Starting facts (filings): Q2-26 revenue $119.8B (+24%), operating income $40.8B, Cloud $24.8B (+82%) with $8.8B OI, Cloud backlog $513.9B [1][2]. What the consensus may be underweighting: (1) Earnings quality. H1-26 pretax income $216.2B includes $135.9B of equity-security gains (SpaceX IPO and other marks; $94.1B of SpaceX stock, mostly locked up [2][42]) [9][1], so trailing P/E of ~17x is misleading. On ex-gains consensus the stock is 23.2x CY27 [14]. (2) Cash. Q2 FCF -$5.9B, TTM $53.3B [1]. Consensus FCF is $8.4B in 2026 and -$36.7B in 2027 on capex of $201.7B and $301.0B [15], consistent with the standing AI-capex view (Alphabet 2027 consensus $285-357B) [40]. Purchase commitments jumped to $707B [3]. (3) Funding mix. Buybacks went from $13.2B in Q2-25 to zero [1]. Alphabet sold 58M Class A/C shares (net $20.5B) plus $10B to Berkshire, $19B of 6.25% mandatory convertibles, and set up a $40B ATM [4][5][6], plus $45B of bonds in Feb/Aug [7][8][39]. (4) Credit is pricing more risk. On like-for-like tenors, new-issue spreads widened from Feb to Aug: 10y T+63 -> T+85, 40y T+95 -> T+130, despite unchanged AA+/Aa2 ratings [7][8]. The Feb sterling deal included a 2126 century bond at gilts +120bp [41]. That is a mild, not alarming, signal. (5) Concentration and circularity. Anthropic reportedly accounts for over 40% of the backlog [31], and Google backstops financing of Anthropic's TPU purchases [32]. These are press reports (The Information, via Silicon UK), used here only to size bear-case probability, not as valuation inputs. (6) Sentiment is crowded: 0 sells and 4 holds out of 55 analysts; insiders sold ~$8.7M and bought $0 over 3 months [37]. Visible Form 4s are routine 10b5-1 or vesting [11][12][13], so this is not a red flag. Alt-data and markets: StatCounter puts Google at 89.94% of worldwide search in Sep-26 [35]. On Kalshi (via Octagon, Oct 2, week of Oct 5), 'Above 20.5%' Google share of OpenRouter text-model requests traded ~75% and 'Above 19.9%' 97%, with 30,430 contracts on the latter [36]. That reads as a solid but not dominant AI-model position. Privacy litigation remains a recurring cost (shareholder proponents cite a $425.7M privacy jury verdict [38]; PriceRunner $2.1B damages and the $5.2B EU Android payment in Q2-Q3 [3]). What weakens the bear case: the ad tech remedy decision rejected the AdX divestiture and imposed a 6-year behavioral decree [27][28][29][30], removing the largest structural legal tail. The balance sheet remains AA+. Operating momentum is real. Valuation: P/E (21.8x, between the all-peer median 19.8x and the US median 23.5x) on haircut NTM EPS gives $360. EV/EBITDA at the peer median (10.5x) gives $320. Blended fair value is $346, about 0.5% below spot. Scenarios: 257/348/440 at 25/50/25 (mean ~$348). The ladder is a lognormal mixture around those (sigma 0.22/0.17/0.17), giving a log-sd of ~0.27 and median ~$348. This is somewhat tighter than the 32% realized vol, because the realized figure includes the Mar-May 2026 re-rating (weekly close $274 in late March to a $408.61 high in May) [43], and wider than base-rate large-cap moves only in the left tail. Research limits: Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage estimate and statistics endpoints were plan-restricted, so consensus comes from MarketScreener and StockAnalysis. Seeking Alpha, Axios and some trade press were not fetchable.

memo.title: GOOGL: Long, small. 25% core EPS growth at 22x with the Anthropic/SpaceX stakes as a free option; target $371.53 (+8.4%)
memo.call_reason: The published target ($371.53) is above the $342.75 close, P(gain) is 0.59 and sizing conviction is medium, so this is a small, staged long. It is not a special situation.
memo.one_liner: Alphabet trades at about 21x forward core EPS while FY2027 consensus EPS grows about 25% with revisions running 8 up to 1 down, Cloud grows 82% on a $514B backlog, and roughly $13-15/sh of SpaceX/Anthropic stakes carry a November IPO option. The edge is modest (+8% to target against 36% implied vol), so we buy 2 shares in two tranches around the Q3 print and keep the stop at $256.52.

thesis.point: Earnings compound at a multiple that already prices in the capex debate.
thesis.evidence: FY2027 consensus core EPS is about $14.92 (+25%), with 8 upward and 1 downward revision in 30 days. NTM core EPS of about $16.2-16.9 at the horizon, at about 22x, gives $356-372 before stakes. The ~$257B 2027 capex consensus is already in that multiple.

thesis.point: Cloud is now a second profit engine, not an option.
thesis.evidence: Q2 2026 Cloud revenue grew about 82% with a $514B backlog, and TPU system sales to third parties begin in 2027. Backlog conversion is what supports FY2027 numbers while Search decelerates.

thesis.point: The equity stakes and base rates add a right tail at little cost.
thesis.evidence: SpaceX is about $82B (551M shares at $148.68, $14.1B locked until Q3 2027) and Anthropic is carried at $124.3B on a $47.6B cost. A reported November IPO at about $2T would add roughly $5-11/sh after tax. Separately, 9 of 10 prior 15% drawdowns were higher a year later; the one exception required EPS to fall 19%.

memo.variant_view: There is no strong variant view; this is a modest long. We sit between two consensuses. Our $371.53 target is well below the sell side (49 analysts, mean $425.45, median $425, range $310-515, Strong Buy), because we apply about 22x NTM core EPS and haircut for 2027 capex, negative FCF and the $84.75B equity program, which the Street's ~$425 largely looks through. We are slightly above the options market: its distribution centers on $358.96 with P(gain) 0.554 and a 15th percentile of $247.69, against our $371.53, P(gain) 0.593 and $256.52. Our small premium to the options market comes from the fact-checked EPS revision trend and the stake/IPO optionality. The difference is about 3.5% of price, which is not enough to call it a mispricing.

valuation.methods: Supervisor-reconciled research target (12m) of $367 (range across five agents $360-375). The main method is NTM core P/E: about 22x on NTM core EPS of about $16.2-16.9 at the Sept 2027 horizon gives $356-372. Added to that are about $13-15/sh of after-tax stake value (SpaceX corrected to about $82B; Anthropic at its $124.3B carrying value) plus about $4-5/sh of probability-weighted Anthropic IPO uplift. A rolled-forward SOTP (about $370) is the cross-check. DCF cross-checks at $313-340 reflect the ~$257B 2027 capex consensus and are weighted about 20%. The published target of $371.53 is the median of the blended options/forecaster distribution, weighted 67% market and 33% forecasters; the expected value is $391.56 (+14.2%).

catalysts.watch: Search & other growth against Q2's +17% (single digits would signal a thesis break), paid-click trends, Cloud growth and the $514B backlog, any early 2027 capex framing against the ~$257B consensus, FCF after Q2's -$5.9B, ATM usage beyond sell-to-cover, and the GAAP SpaceX mark-to-market loss (excluded from core EPS).

Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. tax_assumptions._short_term_all_note: Kilian 2026-10-28 card 'Assume short-term on all' (thread 'Fix AMAT target vs sell mismatch'): every holding is assumed sold within the year at the short-term rate, so a trim only pays the same tax H years sooner; band per year = q tau (1 - (1+d)^-H) / H + spread / T. Overrides lot_aware_horizon; false restores it.
tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. results.supervisor_summary: Research target (12m) $525.83 per current pre-split share. Meta has agreed not to issue Class C shares while the Delaware Class C suits are pending (trial set for April 19, 2027), which also holds back the planned ~$60B at-the-market sale; the model now books no ATM sales by the horizon and funds that gap with debt. The operating build is unchanged: ad revenue grows with the social ad market at a constant Meta share (WARC +14.6% in 2027, +10.6% in 2028; Omdia +12% in 2029), capex follows the post-print analyst estimates ($241B in 2027, $250B in 2028 and 2029), and D&A comes from the depreciation engine checked against construction-in-progress balances ($44B / $72B / $104B in 2027-29), so FoA margins fall from 38.5% to about 27% by 2029. Net interest comes from a net debt roll (net debt rising to ~$245B by end-2028). Legal items stay as before (New Mexico $25B penalty at 40%, $19.9B of accruals) and Reality Labs is valued once at -$53B.

agents.reasoning: Per-share figures are per CURRENT pre-split share (today's Class A share plus the Class C share it gets in the Jan-2027 dividend; 8-K 2026-10-21); EV is unchanged by the dividend. Evidence, mostly primary: Q3-26 release, 10-Q and call; Q2-26 call; nine prior releases for the guidance record. The core is strong: revenue +26% (impressions +10%, price +14%), Q4 guide $73-76B (+22-27%), and Meta beat the top of its range in 6 of 8 quarters. The debate is cost: FY26 expenses $175-179B (incl. $12.3B legal), capex $135-145B, $454.5B of non-cancelable commitments ($121.4B due 2027), management 'investing aggressively' in 2027, and RL loss ~$15B. Driver build: FY27 revenue $312B (at consensus) from impressions +9% and price +10% plus new AI revenue; FoA margin 51.6% FY25 -> 37.8% FY27 -> 34.5% FY28 as D&A rises with capex that follows the AI capex file ($192B, $236B; above street). FY27 EPS ~$32 (~5% below consensus $33.9). Valuation: SOTP $750 (FoA 16.5x NTM EBIT, RL -$25B), P/E 20x $691, EV/EBITDA 10x $681 -> research target (12m) $715.83, +11% vs $642.62. Scenarios: bear $409 (25%), base $716 (50%), bull $1,019 (25%). Ladder: 75% this scenario mix (within-scenario vol 17-18%) plus 25% a market-anchored lognormal (median $650, sigma 33%, about the stock's 43% realized vol trimmed for non-earnings periods), since price is the best single forecast. That gives a median of ~$697 and P(>= $643) = 0.59. Not driver-linked: the RL venture value (-$25B), the litigation and investment adjustments, and RL revenue. Research limits: the Q3 call transcript was reached at a content_files URL; no option data was used.

agents.reasoning: Per-share figures are per CURRENT pre-split share (today's Class A share plus the Class C share it receives on 2027-01-19); EV is unchanged by the dividend. Industry lane: the rest of the ad chain says demand is still strong but slowing. WARC's Q3-26 outlook has social ad spend +21.3% in 2026 and +14.6% in 2027, total +11.9% then +8.4% [13]; IAB US social +16.5% in 2026 [14]; Google Search +17%, YouTube +13%, Amazon ads +26%, Reddit ads +64%, Pinterest +18%, Snap ads only +9% in Q2-26 [16-20]; eMarketer puts Meta's 2026 ad revenue at ~$242B [30]. Meta's own impressions growth fell from +19% (Q1) to +10% (Q3) while price per ad rose to +14% [6][5][1]; an agency newsletter reports large CPM rises [31] (lead only, low weight). On the cost side the supply chain says Meta's bill keeps rising: CoreWeave $21B through 2032 [21], Nebius $12B from early 2027 [22], DRAM contract prices still rising [23], neocloud rental pricing up >50% YTD (MS proprietary index, used only as direction) [25], $454.5B of non-cancelable commitments and $355.7B of leases not yet commenced [2]. So the driver build has FY2027 revenue +17.7% (impressions +8%, price +9%), 2.4% under consensus, and FoA margin falling to 37.4% as D&A rises to $47B; FY2027 EPS ~$31 vs $33.92 consensus. Capex follows the AI-capex file base ($141B in 2026, $192B in 2027) [24]. Guidance record: five straight quarterly revenue guides at or above the range (median +3.4% vs midpoint), expense guides inside, capex guides overshot in 2024-25. Valuation: SOTP (FoA 16x EV/EBIT, RL separately at -$94B), P/E 19x and EV/EBITDA 10.5x give a research target (12m) of $691 after -$19.9B accrued legal and -$10.5B probability-weighted litigation. Ladder: bear $455 / base $680 / bull $920 at 25/50/25 with 25% within-scenario vol (total ~35% log vol vs 43% realized); the centre (~$670 median) sits between the price and the research target because the price is the better one-year predictor. No option data used. Research limited: Q3-26 peer results (Alphabet, Snap, Pinterest, Reddit) are not out yet; X/Twitter not used; no prediction market found on a Meta event that matters (Kalshi lists only headcount contracts). In-lane sources: 19 of 31.

thesis_triggers.event: At ~$125 the EV is ~$7.06B (53.2M x $125 + $406.1M net debt at the 2026-10-01 close), ~11.6x the ~$610M median FY28E RemainCo EBITDA (estimate: median of the agents' $635M/$600M/$581M/$625M/$610M) and ~15x FY27E (7,056 / our FY27 continuing 469.8 = 15.0x), in the lower part of the refreshed peer range (7.8x-18.6x consensus NTM EV/EBITDA on 2026-10-23; CARR 11.1x). That fits only DC growth or the $4B CY27-29 capacity agreement breaking (deferral or loss of the customer that was ~11% of consolidated FY26 sales per the 10-K, ~30% of DC sales if all DC (estimate), share loss, chiller-light designs) or an AI-capex down-cycle, not ordinary ~70% volatility (estimate: 1-year daily log-return volatility of Twelve Data closes to 2026-10-05 = 71%). Four of five agents are at $125 and agent_3 at $120. Reviewed 2026-11-03 (Q2 FY27): kept at $125. The print raised DC and CHVAC sales guides, record DC orders >$1B and a $400M award (slides 4/7 [src 76]), so the break's condition (DC growth stalling or the capacity agreement breaking) has not happened; the stock closing at it on 11-03 is price, not the fundamental trigger. Net debt is now 406.1 (was ~280) at the close, which moves EV at $125 up ~$0.13B (126 x 1/1e3), immaterial to the multiple read. Call pass 2026-11-04: stock -21.4% on the day (close 98.56; intraday low 91.42, Twelve Data) (implied move 20.8%, so ~1.15x, under the 2x trigger); the call reaffirmed the raised sales guide and gave the H2 margin cadence, so the fundamental condition still has not occurred. CORRECTION 2026-11-04 4:55pm ET (Kilian: timing): the 11-04 open 115.5 was already -7.9% below the 11-03 close 125.45 and the low 91.42 came in the session (Twelve Data daily bars); the session split from minute bars (adhoc/move_attrib.py: after-hours 11-03 +0.9%, pre-market -14.0%, open-11am -10.0%) is our own unpublished calculation, not a cited figure, so the timing read (print taken flat, fall after the Texas results) is a judgment alongside DC peers with no print (daily closes 11-03 -> 11-04, Twelve Data: VRT 235.97 -> 205.55 = -12.9%, NVT 129.26 -> 112.82 = -12.7%, VST 139.59 -> 120.29 = -13.8%; MOD 125.45 -> 98.56 = -21.4%). So the move is mostly the midterms/Texas, about -8 to -9% beyond peers (higher DC beta and/or a re-read of the margin miss, not separable); the 1.15x-implied test is the wrong frame (the straddle priced the print, not the election). No escalation either way: policy news is priced in dc_mor.

methods.inputs: NTM (Oct27-Sep28) EBITDA $700M (avg FY28E $635M / FY29E $765M, corporate -$80M) x 16.5x = EV $11.55B; less ~$120M net debt at Oct-2027; / 54.3M diluted shares

FY26 Commercial HVAC sales / adj. EBITDA

inputs_detail.value: DC +60% to +80%; Commercial HVAC +5% to +10% (reaffirmed Jul 29)
~$445M (DC $1.83B x ~19% = $348M; HVAC $1.04B x 16.5% = $172M; corporate -$80M; rounded up ~$5M)
inputs_detail.derivation: DC growth +65%, in the low half of the 60-80% guide because Q1 was supply-constrained. DC margin: 14.8% in Q1 (Ex.99.1); management expects the DC margin back at 19-20% in Q2 (CFO Mick Lucareli, Q1 FY27 call (company transcript): "When we look at going into Q2, we would expect, right now, a lift to be back between 19% and 20%, really driven by a significant lift in the volume recovering." src 38); I assume ~19% for the year (judgment). That is deliberately BELOW the explicit Q1-slide guide of DC 'full-year earnings growth in excess of 85%' (>= $397M, which needs ~23% margins in Q2-Q4 after Q1's $51.7M). HVAC margin 16.5% (16.7% in FY26). Corporate -$80M: Q1 FY27 adjusted corporate & eliminations was -$23.0M (vs -$15.5M a year earlier), ~-$92M annualised, against -$62.6M in FY26. I take a bit less than the run-rate because TSA fees from PT offset some of it. Q1 RemainCo EBITDA was $70.3M ($51.7M + $41.6M - $23.0M), so Q2-Q4 need ~$375M.

Management's Jan-2026 target is DC +50-70% a year for two years. I use +45%, below the range, for supply/execution risk and a possible capex digestion; that matches the capex note's base case of 2027 customer AI capex +50%. DC margin 20% (judgment; FY26 reported 19.4%). HVAC +6%. Corporate -$82M, up from -$80M on inflation, per the Q1 run-rate.
DC growth decelerates to +20% as AI capex growth slows (the capex note's base case has 2028 customer capex +22%).

Peer set of 10 (supervisor's core 8: VRT, NVT, AAON, TT, JCI, CARR, LII, SPXC, plus ETN for its Boyd liquid-cooling business and CSWI for HVAC/R). I dropped HUBB as electrical-only. All forward EV/EBITDA figures use one formula, TTM EV/EBITDA / (1 + 3Y revenue CAGR), on TTM EV/EBITDA derived from filings and Oct-5 closes, with stockanalysis consensus revenue CAGRs; I dropped my round-1 +3pt margin allowance as arbitrary. That gives a median of 20.73x (range 11.3-29.46x). The EPS-CAGR divisor gives 19.74x and the average divisor 20.23x, so I treat ~20x as the reference. 16.5x is inside the range, ~18% below ~20x. The discount rests on structural features that persist through Oct-2027: (a) concentration, with one technology customer ~11% of consolidated FY26 sales per the 10-K, ~30% of DC sales if all of it is Data Centers (estimate: 0.11 x $3,181.1M FY26 sales / $1,108.2M DC sales = ~32%; the 10-K places the customer only in the Climate Solutions segment); (b) about 30% of NTM EBITDA is commercial HVAC, whose peers LII/CARR/SPXC sit at 11.3-17.9x (derived); (c) DC EBITDA margins of ~19-20% vs VRT's ~22% (TTM GAAP EBITDA $2,561.8M / revenue $11,479.6M to 2026-06-30, 10-Q XBRL); (d) the NTM window at Oct-2027 includes DC growth decelerating to ~+20% in FY29. [Citation audit 2026-10-06: peer multiples re-derived from filings (EV from 10-Q debt/cash/shares and Oct-5 closes; TTM GAAP EBITDA) and consensus growth/EPS; aggregator multiples no longer used. The chosen multiple is unchanged.]

agents.reasoning: I valued only the remaining Climate Solutions company from recast segment data in Modine's filings: FY26 Data Centers $1.11B sales / $214.7M EBITDA, Commercial HVAC $974M / $162.4M. FY27 guidance is DC +60-80% and HVAC +5-10%. The Q1 slides also promise DC 'full-year earnings growth in excess of 85%', and the Jan-2026 deck targets DC +50-70% a year for two years. Round 2 changes after re-checking the supervisor's points in the filings. (1) Corporate cost: the Q1 FY27 release shows adjusted corporate & eliminations of -$23.0M for the quarter (vs -$15.5M a year earlier), so I raise it from -$55M to -$80M a year. That cuts FY27E RemainCo EBITDA to ~$445M (Q1 actual $70.3M) and FY28E to ~$635M. (2) Net debt: I confirmed $432.9M at Jun 30 less the ~$156M distribution = ~$277M, i.e. ~$280M, as in round 1. (3) Comps: I dropped HUBB and the +3pt margin allowance and recomputed all 10 peers on TTM/(1+3Y revenue CAGR): median 20.5x, or ~19x reconciled with the EPS-divisor result. 16.5x is now a ~13% discount, justified by 10-K concentration (one customer ~11% of consolidated sales; ~30% of DC if all DC, an estimate), the HVAC mix and DC margins below VRT. (4) Calendar: the Nov 18 Analyst & Investor Day is confirmed and sits outside the 1-month window. The Q2 date is still unannounced but very likely ~Oct 26-29. On NTM Oct-2027 EBITDA of $700M at 16.5x and EPS of $8.54 at 24x, fair value is ~$208 (+14%), down from $215; most of the upside is earnings growth, not re-rating. I am still explicitly below management's DC earnings guide because Q1 margins make the >85% promise require ~23% margins for the rest of the year. Scenarios: bear $110 (25%), base $205 (50%), bull $305 (25%). The ladder is a lognormal mixture around those (sds ~0.30/0.22/0.20) with tails fattened toward the 71% realized vol: median ~$202, P(>=183) 0.605. memo.title: MOD: stay long but small (3 sh): a sector sell-off has taken the stock to $135, ~8% above our $125 thesis break, 12 days before the Nov 3 Q2 print, the expected first standalone guide
memo.call_reason: The published target of $161.51 is 19.5% above the $135.17 close and the research target (12m) is $200, but supervisor confidence is low and the review trims to the Sharpe-optimal size (4 to 3 sh) [1][2][3][9].
memo.one_liner: Modine is now a pure data-center and commercial HVAC cooling company that guides data-center sales +60-80% this year and has a $4B 2027-29 capacity agreement, yet it trades at $135.17, down 26% from the $182.91 research price of Oct 5, and the latest 9.75% drop came with no company news [3][9][10][17][18][19]. We keep a small long (target $161.51, research target (12m) $200) into the Nov 3 print and Nov 18 Investor Day, with a $125 thesis break and an $89.26 stop [1][3][13][14].

thesis.point: Data-center growth is guided and partly contracted, not just hoped for.
thesis.evidence: FY26 Data Centers sales were $1,108.2M with $214.7M adj. EBITDA (19.4%); the Q1 FY27 slides guide DC sales +60-80% and DC earnings growth >85% for FY27; the 10-K expects more than $4B of DC cooling sales to one customer in CY2027-29 (~$1.3B/yr); management's medium-term DC target is 50-70%/yr.

thesis.point: Margin recovery is the near-term lever, and the Nov 3 print tests it.
thesis.evidence: Q1 FY27 DC margin fell to 14.8% on $348.6M sales because of supply shortages; hitting the >85% DC earnings guide needs ~23% DC margins in Q2-Q4. No continuing-ops guide has been issued since the Oct 1 spin; the Q1 release said the outlook would be updated after the spin closed, and the supervisor expects it with the Q2 results due after the close on Nov 3.

thesis.point: The price already discounts a lot: at $135.17 the EV is ~$7.5B, ~13.4-13.9x NTM RemainCo EBITDA vs a 20.2x filing-derived peer median.
thesis.evidence: 53,196,918 shares x $135.17 + $265.3M pro forma net debt at June 30 (8-K/A Ex.99.1 of Oct 7: $43.4M current + $276.0M long-term debt - $54.1M cash; derived) = ~$7.46B EV over ~$535-555M NTM EBITDA (supervisor estimate). The Oct 22 drop (-9.75%, from $149.78) came with no Modine filing or release; Vertiv fell ~8% and GE Vernova ~11% the same day after Meta's Q3 release, which narrowed 2026 capex upward to $135-145B but showed -$2.12B Q3 free cash flow.

memo.variant_view: We sit between the Street and the options market. Analysts (9, Strong Buy) have a median target of $301 (low $260) on StockAnalysis, and our recency-weighted median of the individual targets is $293.67 (as of Oct 20); several were set before the Oct 1 spin and on premium multiples; our research target (12m) of $200 uses 17x EBITDA, a ~16% discount to peers justified by ~11% single-customer concentration and below-peer DC margins [1][3][18][22]. The options market's own 12-month median is $134.66, roughly today's price (it gives a 44% chance of closing above the Oct 21 mark of $149.78 and ~50% above today's $135.17); our research is more constructive because DC growth is guided and contracted [1][17][19]. The published target $161.51 weights the options market 67% and research 33% [1]. The variant is modest: we are not calling the Street's $290s, only that the stock is pricing an AI-capex down-cycle that the latest hyperscaler data (Meta raising the low end of 2026 capex) does not show [1][11].

inputs_detail.derivation: Annual base-case totals from the standing file (sources 21). FY(N) ~ CY(N-1) (MRVL fiscal year ends late Jan). Quarter shape: geometric within-year shape from the neighbouring annual growth rates, rescaled to each year's total (shape only, totals are the file's). CY2025 = 1,225 x (Big-4 2025 ~$410B / Big-4 2026 base 733) = 685 (derived, low confidence; only sets the base-year capture, not any forecast quarter). Build: DC = customer AI capex (standing file base, CY2026-28) x MRVL capture; capture rises from 0.75% to ~0.97% on the custom ramp the CEO described (custom more than doubles in FY2028) and flattens in FY2029 for ASIC competition. That gives FY2028 $19.2B and EPS ~$7.28, 2-4% under consensus and the outlook (moderately conservative base). Year 3 (FY2029) margin ~41% non-GAAP is above MRVL's FY2026 35%, an upcycle level; the horizon multiple (19.2x, from the k=0.8 shrink of a 23.7x peer median at current closes toward MRVL's 18.2x) partly prices that. Deal: valued LITE on consensus FY Jun-2028 EPS at 17x with $1B synergies phased in; on those inputs MRVL holders give up ~$8/share if it closes, x 0.65 probability, plus a 12% chance of the $3.2B regulatory fee: about -$5.8/share. (d) Deal: LITE valued on its own horizon earnings (Zacks, -15% haircut) at its exit-rule multiple, against 456.4M new MRVL shares at my standalone $176.64: V -$9.1B if it closes, p 0.55 = -$5.41/share. agents.reasoning: Base rates first: MRVL's five earlier 45%+ drawdowns from a 12-month high since 2007 (2008-10, 2012-10, 2015-10, 2022-06, 2025-03; Twelve Data monthly closes) were followed by +37% to +97% 12-month returns (median ~+59%), but the 2000-01 bust shows a -50% stock can halve again, and this drawdown has a fundamental trigger (an all-stock $115B deal giving away 33% of the company) plus a macro one (midterm-driven AI sell-off, NVIDIA CEO exit, Google shifting custom work to MediaTek). Stock-financed acquirers earned -25% five-year excess returns (Loughran-Vijh 1997) and merger arbs price ~50% closing odds, so I book a small probability-weighted dilution (-$2.8/share). Kalshi-style 2027 recession odds are 21%. ARM: the 2026 US price change landed in Q2'26 ('partial-quarter impact', Q2'26 letter, source 4) and Q3'26 UCAN grew +11.0% with flat members, so ARM ~+11% until the change laps: Q4'26 +11.0%, Q1'27 +9.5%, Q2'27 +7.5% (partial lap). After the lap ARM growth = ads + plan mix only: Netflix ads ~$2.7B in 2026 (source 14) growing to ~$4.2B in 2027 adds ~2.5-3 pts in UCAN where ads are concentrated, so H2'27 +4.5%. Netflix's US price steps came in Jan 2025 and spring 2026 (sources 6, 4), ~15 months apart, so we place the next one in early 2028: Q1'28 +5.5%, Q2-Q3'28 +7.0%, Q4'28 +6.5% (ads maturing). Other evidence-based builds: (a) Antenna's no-net-adds reading taken at face value as members -2% a year: UCAN FY2027 growth ~4.5% instead of ~6.4%; (b) a second US price change in H2 2027 (Netflix's 15-month cadence from spring 2026): FY2027 UCAN ~+8%; (c) Spotify's Q3'26 ARPU +7.5% cc on price increases with 6M net adds (source 21) shows subscription price power still works in a mature market. The upside and downside cases move this driver by +2.5 / -3.5 pts.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Antenna's member losses taken literally (-2%/yr) cut FY2027 UCAN to ~+4.5% and the research target (12m) by ~4%; a 2027 US price step lifts it ~+5%.

Members: APAC/India view hours +24% and India revenue +18% (source 1), and the ad tier launches in 15 more countries from March 2027 (9 EMEA + Colombia, Peru, New Zealand first; source 14), so members grow ~5-6% in 2027. Path: Q4'26 +12.0% (some F/X tailwind left), 2027 +10.5% / +10.0% / +9.5% / +9.0% (decelerating as the 2026 price changes lap), 2028 +8.5% and +8.0% in Q4 (ad-tier countries in the base). Other evidence-based builds: (a) hold the Q3'26 F/X-neutral +10.9% through 2027: FY2027 International ~+11% instead of ~+9.7%; (b) EMEA's slower F/X-neutral 9% across all regions as markets mature (Greenlight/Hub on churn, source 24): ~+8.5%.
