agents.reasoning: Industry lane. The chain says Netflix's demand is flat in the US and still growing abroad: Antenna (via Reuters) shows no US net adds through September 2026, Apptopia shows non-openers up 16.6% y/y, H1 view hours rose only 2%, and YouTube holds 2x Netflix's TV time in Nielsen's Gauge. Pricing still works (Q3 UCAN +11% on the spring price change; Spotify's +7.5% cc ARPU shows the subscription model holds), but the US price step laps in Q2 2027. Competitors: Disney's streaming profit doubled (11.5% margin) and Paramount will merge HBO Max with Paramount+ (~200M subs), both raising content-rights pressure; YouTube's own ad growth slowed to 9%, so the CTV ad pool is not booming for anyone, and Netflix cut its 2026 ad outlook 10% to $2.7B. Build: two-region quarterly revenue (UCAN growth 11% -> ~4.5% in H2 2027 -> ~7% in 2028 with a next price step; International ~10% -> 8.5%), content amortization +6.5%/+6%, non-content costs down ~0.3 pt on the headcount cut. FY2027 revenue $55.4B (+8.3%) is below the 'sustained double-digit' aim; FY2027 EPS $3.73 matches the $3.74 consensus because our margin is higher, and FY2028 EPS $4.27 is 3.7% below the $4.43 consensus. Value: P/E 16.59x (whole-company peers DIS/SONY/SPOT median 17.66x shrunk to NFLX's 16.33x, k = 0.8) on NTM EPS ~$4.09 gives the research target (12m). Downside (P10) and upside (P90) move the regional growth drivers, costs and the multiple; the left tail is wider, matching the -46% year. Outside ad forecasts (WARC Feb 2026, Motley Fool Sept 2026) were overtaken by the Oct 20 cut and are reconciled, not used as the path. Research was limited by blocked consensus pages (no revenue consensus) and paywalled trade press (Puck, MediaPost).

agents.reasoning: Skeptic lane. The downside evidence is broad and current. Revenue growth has slowed four quarters running (Q1'26 16.2%, Q2 13.4%, Q3 11.8%, Q4 guide 11.5%). The FY26 range ended below its first midpoint. Ad revenue was cut 10% ($3.0B -> $2.7B). Bloomberg and Wells Fargo show viewing per member falling (Wells: about -8% per household in H1), and Antenna shows US subscriber losses through September. YouTube has twice Netflix's US TV time (Nielsen, August). HSBC, Wells Fargo, Needham and Wolfe downgraded, a Seeking Alpha Sell followed, and hedge-fund holders fell (146 -> 121). Insider sales (Hastings, Neumann, March 2026) are routine option exercises and carry little signal. Credit is not a risk: net debt is 6.9B on about 16B of EBITDA, the July 2026 10-year priced at 5.25%, and the revolver covenant is 3x EBITDA/interest, well clear. Weighed honestly, the business is still growing about 11% with a 31.5% margin and buying back about 5% of its shares a year, so the risk is a de-rating and estimate cuts, not distress. Model: four regional drivers built from price (the March-2026 US rise laps in Q2'27), members (flat to +1% in the US) and the 2027 ad-tier launches, with no currency gain carried forward. FY27 revenue comes to 55.4B (+8.5%), 2.1% below the Street's 56.6B. Content-amortization leverage is limited (cost ratio -0.3 points), so the EBIT margin is 32.4% in FY27 and 33.1% in FY28. EPS is about $3.59 and $4.14, 4% and 7% below Zacks (3.74 and 4.43). Value: NTM GAAP EPS at the horizon x 16.75x (peer median 18.56x shrunk to NFLX's 16.33x with k = 0.8). Downside and upside move the drivers (revenue levels -6%/+3.5%, cost ratios +2.5/-1.5 points) and the multiple (-4.0/+4.5 turns); the downside sits further from base, a fatter left tail. Research was limited: Twelve Data's estimate, insider and price-target endpoints require a paid plan; SEC folder indexes refused plain requests, so filings were read through WebFetch; Puck, NST and MarketBeat pages could not be read.

The fall followed three things: revenue growth slowing each quarter (16% -> 13% -> 12% -> ~11.5% guided for Q4), the cut to the 2026 ad target ($3.0B -> $2.7B), and evidence of weaker engagement. Lane work (alternative data) tested whether the engagement worry is real. It is, but it shows up mostly in volume, not yet in churn. Apptopia (via Bloomberg/A.V. Club) has US subscribers not opening the app up 16.6% y/y in Q3. Nielsen's Gauge (TheWrap, Tubefilter) puts Netflix at 7.7% of US TV against YouTube's record 15.8%. The Entertainment Strategy Guy and Hub Intel Substack show returning shows losing audiences and per-user viewing falling. Stocktwits retail sentiment is extremely bearish. On the other side, Antenna data still shows strong Premium uptake among cord-cutters, and the company says price rises in the US, Mexico and Spain went as expected. My read: pricing still works but member growth is saturating, so the base case decelerates memberships (+4.6% in 2026, +3.5%, +2.8%) and keeps ARM at +3-3.5%, below the 2026 pace. Ads come from company statements (250M+ monthly active ad viewers, 15 new markets in 2027), not the stale Omdia path, which I reconciled. Guidance record: quarterly revenue beats have shrunk to about zero in 2026 and margin beats came from expense timing, so Q4 sits just under the guide. Content cost (+7.5%/+6.5%) and opex give 33.0%/34.1% margins. EPS ends 2-3% under consensus. Valuation follows the playbook: P/E on our own GAAP EPS with the k = 0.8 shrink toward a thin 3-name whole-company peer median (17.66x), giving 16.59x and $69.32 (+16%). That is mostly buyback-driven EPS growth at a flat multiple. Downside (P10, $42.24) has the engagement slide turning into churn, an ad slip, a content push and a de-rating to ~13.6x. Upside (P90, $102.86) has ads and pricing working and a partial return of the premium. Engine-sized judgment calls over 5% are listed in gap_note for Kilian. Research used about 25 searches and fetches; X/Twitter, Reddit and several data-vendor pages (Apptopia, MediaPost/Antenna, Puck, eMarketer, MarketBeat) blocked fetching, so I relied on reachable relays of them and flagged each relay. No option prices were consulted.

agents.method_text: P/E 16.82x (peer median 18.92x shrunk toward NFLX's own 16.33x, k = 0.8) on the driver model's own NTM GAAP EPS at 2027-11-17 (~$4.27: FY2028 revenue $60.6B, EBIT margin 34.5%, ~3.96B shares) = $71.90.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Base-rate cross-check only: median 12-month return after a -40%+ year in six analog episodes (NFLX 2004-10, 2011-11, 2022-05; META 2022-10; PYPL 2022-05; DIS 2022-12) is +63% (range -27% to +223%) [15][16]; $59.68 x 1.63 = $97. Not weighted: the sample is small and picked from famous rebounds; the two maturity de-ratings (PYPL -27%, DIS +4%) fit today's setup (earnings still growing ~20%, revenue growth slowing) better.

agents.reasoning: Lane: base rates, history, events. (1) What happened: revenue growth slowed four quarters running (16.2% to 11.8%, Q4 guide 11.5%), the 2026 ad goal was cut to ~$2.7B, H1 view hours grew 2% and Netflix's US TV share fell from 8.8% to 7.7% while YouTube hit 15.8% [1][6][18][19]; the stock fell 46% in a year to a 52-week low. Earnings still grow ~20% and FCF (~$12B) all goes to buybacks. (2) Guidance record: first annual revenue guides were beaten by +1.5% (FY2024) and +3.9% (FY2025), margins by 2.7 and 1.5pts, but FY2026 lands inside its first range and on its 31.5% margin guide, and quarterly beats have shrunk to ~0.1-0.8%: the beat habit has ended, so we do not add one [4][7][8][9]. (3) Build: regional y/y growth (members, price, ads) fading by ~1pt a year per the growth-persistence evidence [23] to +9.4% in 2027 and +8.4% in 2028 (1-2.5% under consensus [13]); cost of revenues +7.5%/+7%, opex +6% on a base cleared of deal and layoff costs, giving 33.5% / 34.5% margins (consensus 33.3% / 35.1%). (4) Value: P/E 16.82x on our NTM EPS ~$4.27 (3.97B shares at the horizon; consensus NTM ~$4.35) = $71.90. NFLX's own 2022 trough was ~15.6x trailing [10][15], so the exit multiple already sits at the low end of its history. (5) Distribution: after -40%+ years the six analogs returned a median +63% but the two maturity de-ratings (PYPL -27%, DIS +4%) are the closer fit [15][16]; Kalshi prices a 2027 recession at 20% [17]. Downside (P10) $43.24 cuts growth 3pts and the multiple to ~11.8x; upside (P90) $104.37 adds 2pts of growth and re-rates to ~21.8x. The left tail is fatter. Not driver-linked: none (one P/E leg). Research limits: Zacks, MarketBeat, chartmill and Northeast Times pages were blocked; consensus revenue came from MarketScreener, EPS from Nasdaq/Zacks.

memo.title: NFLX: small two-step long in a de-rated cash compounder at ~18x 2027 EPS; the Oct 20 print and the January 2027 guide settle the engagement debate
memo.call_reason: The published 12-month target of $75.49 is 8.5% above the $69.58 close and the research target (12m) of $80.00 is 15.0% above it, at medium conviction; size is capped by the supervisor at ~8% because the engagement debate is unresolved and earnings are three weeks out.
memo.one_liner: Netflix has de-rated to ~18x 2027 consensus EPS on an engagement scare that has not yet reached churn (2% vs a 4% industry average) or pricing, while recurring FCF of ~$11.3-11.7B and a ~3-4% annual share shrink keep compounding per-share value. We buy 11 shares in two tranches around the Oct 20 print, target $75.49 / research target (12m) $80, take profit $97.77, stop at the $51 thesis break.

thesis.point: 1. Per-share cash compounding is intact and is being bought back cheaply.
thesis.evidence: Recurring 2026 FCF is ~$11.3-11.7B (the $11B pre-fee guide incl. the ~$700M Brazil deposit, vs $12.5B including the after-tax WBD fee), implying ~$13.0-13.5B in 2027. Net debt is only $5.24B (A2/A), and Q2 buybacks retired 52.9M shares, shrinking the 4.164B count ~3-4% a year.

thesis.point: 2. Monetisation shows no damage from the engagement debate yet.
thesis.evidence: Antenna July churn is 2% vs a 4% average for major services; the 2026 upfront nearly doubled ad commitments and the ad tier passed 250M monthly active viewers, with ads ~$3B in 2026. The fall season (~40% of annual gross adds) is the next test.

thesis.point: 3. The multiple already discounts a lot; the bar for the print is low.
thesis.evidence: At $69.58 the stock trades ~18x 2027 consensus EPS of $3.82 with 2028 at $4.56, near Wells Fargo's 15x bear multiple ($57 PT) after Wells Fargo and HSBC downgrades in September. Our research target (12m) of $80 needs only ~19x NTM EPS of ~$4.25 and a 4.5% FCF yield, not a return to the old 30x+.

memo.variant_view: We sit between the two consensus views. The options market's distribution (result.json market_only) is centred at $70.19 with P(gain) 0.51, i.e. it prices no edge; we have $75.49 and P(gain) 0.58 because the forecasters see churn, ad growth and buybacks absorbing the engagement drag. The sell-side is far more bullish (weighted median PT $95, Deutsche Bank upgrade to Buy at $95 on 9/29, Wells Fargo $57 underweight); we stay well below it because peer de-ratings of quality large caps (DIS, PYPL, NKE, ADBE) have a median ~-6% follow-through over the next 12 months, so we do not underwrite a re-rating before the January 2027 guide. The real variant view is modest: the market is treating an engagement metric (Nielsen 7.8% share vs YouTube 14.2%; Wells Fargo ~-4% y/y hours per member in H2'26) as if it were already a revenue problem.

valuation.methods: Supervisor research target (12m) $80 (five forecasters $77-83, mean $80.3) = 60/40 blend of (a) P/E: NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of 0.25x$3.82 + 0.75x$4.56 = $4.38, less ~3% engagement haircut = $4.25, at 19x = ~$81; and (b) FCF: NTM FCF ~$14.5B at a 4.5% yield, less $5.24B net debt, over ~4.08B diluted shares = ~$77.7. The published 12-month target ($75.49, the median of the blended market/forecaster distribution) sits below the research target (12m) because the options market centres near spot; take profit $97.77 is the 75th percentile, stop $51 is the thesis break (~13.4x 2027 EPS, ~6.6% FCF yield).

catalysts.event: Paramount Skydance closes its WBD acquisition (all regulatory conditions met in Aug; 12-state AG settlement Sep 21)

catalysts.watch: Streaming bundle/pricing announcements, content-spend guidance and leverage of the combined company.

catalysts.watch: Netflix share of TV time vs the July 7.8% and YouTube's lead; any restatement of history under the new method.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results and Q4 guide (letter 1:01pm PT, video interview 1:45pm PT)
catalysts.why_it_moves: First print since the September downgrades; the Q4 guide and any 2027 framing set the growth path the multiple hangs on. Q2's slight beat with a lower outlook sent the stock down after hours.
catalysts.watch: Revenue vs $12.86B guide, 33.2% operating margin, EPS $0.82; Q4 guide vs the $51.2B / 31.5% FY26 plan; engagement and ad-revenue commentary; Q3 buyback pace and FCF vs the ~$12.5B FY guide; early 2027 growth/margin framing (~10% growth, 33-34% margin needed).

catalysts.event: Antenna churn and sign-up reads through the fall acquisition season
catalysts.why_it_moves: Churn at 2% is the evidence that engagement loss has not reached monetisation; Sep-Dec is ~40% of annual gross adds, so a rise here would validate the bear case.
catalysts.watch: Netflix monthly churn above ~2.5%; gross adds vs prior years; ad-tier mix.

catalysts.event: NFL Thanksgiving Eve game on Netflix (Packers at Rams), first of its kind
catalysts.why_it_moves: Live-sports tentpoles drive sign-ups and ad inventory and counter the engagement narrative; a streaming failure would hurt.
catalysts.watch: Reported viewership, stream stability, ad sell-out.

catalysts.why_it_moves: A global live event at no extra cost; another engagement and sign-up spike for Q4.
catalysts.watch: Concurrent viewers; Q4 net-add commentary in January.

catalysts.event: NFL Christmas Day doubleheader exclusively on Netflix
catalysts.why_it_moves: Highest-profile ad inventory of the year; supports the ad-scaling leg of the thesis.
catalysts.watch: Viewership vs 2025 Christmas games; advertiser demand.

catalysts.event: Q4 2026 results and first full-year 2027 revenue, margin and FCF guidance
catalysts.why_it_moves: The main re-rating or de-rating event: ~10% 2027 growth with 33-34% margin supports the $80 research target (12m); high-single-digit growth or a flat margin is the bear path toward the $51 thesis break.
catalysts.watch: 2027 revenue growth vs ~10%, operating margin vs 33-34%, 2027 FCF vs ~$13.0-13.5B, buyback size, ad-revenue target.

catalysts.event: H2 2026 'What We Watched' engagement report
catalysts.why_it_moves: Direct test of Wells Fargo's ~-4% y/y hours-per-member call for H2'26.
catalysts.watch: Total hours and hours per member y/y; share of views from top titles.

risks.risk: Engagement erosion reaches churn and pricing power (YouTube and creators taking TV time).
risks.signpost: Antenna churn above ~2.5% for two consecutive months, Netflix share falling further on the recalibrated Gauge, or a weaker take-rate on the next price increase.

risks.risk: The January 2027 guide shows high-single-digit growth and a stalled margin, cutting 2027/28 EPS.
risks.signpost: A Q4 guide on Oct 20 below the implied $51.2B FY26 plan, or 2027 framing under ~10% growth / ~33% margin.

risks.risk: The de-rating persists even if fundamentals hold (peer base rate: median ~-6% follow-through in 12 months).
risks.signpost: Stock fails to rally on a clean Oct 20 print and stays below ~$63 into January.

risks.risk: A large debt-funded acquisition (Lionsgate interest was reported and denied in June) diverts buyback capacity.
risks.signpost: Formal offer reports, new bond issuance beyond refinancing, or a slower Q3/Q4 buyback pace.

what_changes_our_mind: Antenna churn rising above ~2.5% through the fall season, or the H2'26 engagement report showing hours per member falling faster than -4% y/y alongside slowing ad growth.
A Q4 guide on Oct 20 or a January 2027 guide pointing to <10% 2027 revenue growth or margin below ~33%, which would cut EPS rather than just the multiple.
On the upside: a January guide of ~10%+ growth with a 34%+ margin and a stable share on the recalibrated Nielsen Gauge would justify adding toward the research target (12m) of $80.

tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. It is (1) the CEO vacancy after Huang's 2026-11-12 resignation and the Megaspeed export probe, class action and governance overhang (src 7, 8, 11, 12); (2) a financing loop: $109.7B of equity stakes in customers/labs, guarantees up to $105B, $102B cloud/lease commitments, DSO up to ~64 days on extended terms, and a July CDS spike to a record 82bp (src 1, 5, 7, 13, 14); Kress now says support will be 'less' (src 8), which removes some ACIE demand; (3) the cycle: FY2028 demand rests on customer capex +50% in CY2027 with no 2027 dollar guides yet. Build: customer AI capex (standing file base, reconciled to Q3 actuals: Big-4 2026 ~730B vs 733B) x capture, which rises with Vera Rubin content per GW then fades; plus Edge; GM per Kress's Q4 bottom and 72-73% recovery but to ~70.7% in FY2029 (mid-cycle year 3); opex from the run-rate. Result: FY2028 $680.2B (8% under guide, 6% under the post-print $723.9B consensus), FY2029 $797B (12% under the $903B consensus), EPS ~$15.6 / ~$18.3. The market already prices much of this at 9.9x NTM; the default k = 0.8 shrink to a peer median of 21.6x gives 11.6x, so the research target sits above spot even on a below-consensus FY2029. The left tail is fatter (P10 -47% from base vs P90 +53%), from a capex -20% / capture -3pt / GM -2.5pt / 9x case. Sources: 11 of the 19 non-filing sources are in lane (sell-side downgrades, litigation, DOJ probe, credit/CDS and circular-financing journalism, call statements on financing and receivables); the 7 older releases plus the 10-K/10-Q/8-K are the basic-fact guidance record the brief allows. agents.reasoning: Base rates first. NVDA's own 12-month forward returns since 2002: median +40%, P(down) 22%, P(<-40%) 7%; in setups like today (prior year +10-45%, at a 52-week high, n=25) median +29%. That record is survivorship-biased for a $5.7T leader; the top-dog base rate (Arnott/Wu: largest companies trail their sector by ~4%/yr) and a ~7% market return pull the centre to roughly +5-12%. Round-2 corrections from the supervisor, all accepted: (1) my horizon NTM EPS used a window shifted one quarter forward; on the same Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29 window as today's 19.3-19.7x it is ~$16.7 after a 5% haircut (also FY29 growth trimmed to +15% given consensus 2027 capex growth of only ~+22%, src 27); (2) my fair value used 18x while my base scenario used 15x; I now use one multiple, 16x, in both; (3) FCF conversion of 85% is not supported (Q2 FY27 FCF 36-39% of NI, H1 ~70%), now 75%, with ~$1/share true net cash; (4) the 10Y at 5.24-5.28% is verified at Treasury (src 26) but it is the highest since 2007, not 2002; (5) the Fed-odds source was misattributed; the Dec-9 meeting-specific Kalshi contract shows ~70% for a 25bp hike (search-result snapshot; direct fetch 429) and DeFi Rate 72%, so the macro headwind stands; (6) I dropped the 'historical 17-20x floor' argument. On compression: it has been estimate-driven (FY28 EPS +24% in 90 days while the price rose), so it is real but has not hurt holders; I assume 3.5 more turns (to 16x), while a flat year needs ~14.2x on my EPS, a de-rating that likely needs an EPS break. Fair value $255 (P/E $267, FCF $230, mid-cycle $260) is below my round-1 $296. Scenarios: bear $150 (25%), base $267 (50%), bull $342 (25%, lowered from $370 to an 18x multiple). The ladder is a three-lognormal mixture (sigmas 0.25/0.20/0.18) plus a 5% wide tail component: mean ~$263, median ~$262, P(up) ~61%, P(<$166) ~17%. The ladder sits slightly above the blended fair value because the FCF leg is a deliberately rate-harsh cross-check. Research limits: Kalshi returned 429 and Polymarket's December page was the 2025 market, so Fed odds rest on the Kalshi search snapshot and the DeFi Rate aggregator; the Moody's capex note returned 403. Peer forward EV/EBITDA is estimated from trailing figures and peer growth is 3-year CAGR.

memo.title: NVDA: long a decade-low 19.5x NTM multiple; target $268.93, stop $174.61, add only if late-Oct capex guides clear our base case
memo.call_reason: Published 12-month target $268.93 is 12.6% above the $238.90 close, P(gain) is 0.63 and the conviction rubric reads medium, but the expected excess return barely covers ~38% volatility, so the position stays small and staged.
memo.one_liner: NVDA trades at ~19.5x NTM EPS, a decade low and below AVGO/TSM, with FY28 guided to ~+70% revenue; even after assuming the multiple compresses to 16x we get a $263 research target (12m) and a $268.93 target. The risk is a 2027-28 hyperscaler capex digestion, so we hold 1 share and add only if the Oct 27-30 capex guides and the ~Nov 17-18 Q3 FY27 print confirm demand.

thesis.point: The valuation already prices heavy de-rating: the stock is flat in a year only at ~13.9x Oct-2027 NTM EPS.
thesis.evidence: $238.90 is ~19.5x NTM consensus EPS of $12.00-12.25 (Q3 FY27-Q2 FY28; stockanalysis fwd P/E 19.34x), vs AVGO 20.49x and TSM 20.65x. Consistent Oct-2027 NTM EPS of $17.1 means a flat year needs ~13.9x, a further ~29% de-rating. All five agents assume compression to 16-17x and still reach research targets (12m) of $250-296.

thesis.point: Earnings visibility through FY28 is unusually high and supply-constrained.
thesis.evidence: Q2 FY27 revenue $96.2B (+106% y/y), Data Center $89.0B (+117%), non-GAAP GM 75.0%. The Q3 guide is $108.0B ±2% at 74.0% GM. Management's preliminary FY28 view is ~+70% revenue at 72-73% GM after a 71-72% Q4 trough. $279B of supply and capacity commitments back the ramp.

thesis.point: Customer capex keeps being revised up, and backlogs fund the 2027 ramp.
thesis.evidence: Big-4 2026 capex guides rose from ~$655B to $732.5B during the year, and none was cut. 2027 Big-4 consensus is $934.5B (IO Fund) to $1,029B (S&P), against our base case of $1,080B. Backlogs: MSFT commercial RPO $678B, Google Cloud $513.9B, AWS $496B. Year-ahead consensus drift was +25% to +62% in each of 2024-26.

memo.variant_view: There is no strong variant view against the options market. Our $268.93 target and 0.63 P(gain) sit close to the options-only distribution (target $263.75, P(gain) 0.61, 15th percentile $173.36). Against the sell side we are more cautious: the 50-analyst median target is $315 (range $210-515, Strong Buy), ~17% above ours. The gap is the multiple, not EPS: we assume 16x on Oct-2027 NTM EPS because FY29 growth should slow to low-to-mid teens. Our customer-capex work adds a second gap. At base capture, base-case 2027 capex implies FY28 revenue of ~$647B, 6% below the $687B consensus, and NVIDIA's supply cap (~$700-750B) limits FY28 upside. So we are below the Street on both multiple and FY28 revenue, and in line with options. [sources 9, 11, 12]

valuation.methods: Supervisor research target (12m) $263 is a blend of two legs. P/E (60%): consistent Oct-2027 NTM EPS (Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29) of $17.1 = H2 FY28 consensus $8.90 + H1 FY29 ~$8.5 (FY29 +13-15%, ~2% memory-cost haircut), x 16x = $274. FCF yield (40%): $17.1 x 23.9B shares x 72% conversion = $12.3/share at a 5.0% yield = $246, + ~$1 net cash = $247. Agent research targets (12m) $250/$255/$260/$270/$296 (median $260). agent_4 is high on 17x and a 4.5% yield. 16x is ~22% below the AVGO/TSM 20.57x anchor. The published target $268.93 is the median of the blended options-plus-agents distribution. Thesis break $160.

tax_assumptions._ignore_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: ignore taxes for now (he has money set aside for the liability). Set false to use the tax facts below.
tax_assumptions._future_note: Combined rate you'd expect on today's embedded gains when you'd otherwise sell (15% federal + ~6% state once working). Drives the sell cost and the gain-harvest suggestion.
tax_assumptions._tax_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: taxable account; ~$20,000 internship wages in 2026 plus realized gains; claimed as a dependent by a parent living in CA; full-time student under 24 living in CT. Assumed (not confirmed): domicile stays CA (a student living away at school keeps the parents' domicile, FTB Pub 1031), CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode so CT does not tax investment income; kiddie tax applies (earned income not more than half of his support). Federal 2026 figures from IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32; CA brackets are 2025 (FTB Tax News Oct 2025), 2026's not published yet.
tax_assumptions._other_unearned_note: Dividends etc. this year (rough: GOOGL + META dividends). Counts toward the kiddie-tax threshold.
tax_assumptions._kiddie_note: Unearned income above $2,700 (2 x $1,350, Rev. Proc. 2025-32) is taxed at the parent's rate, federal (Form 8615) and CA (FTB 3800). Applies to a full-time student 19-23 whose earned income is not more than half of his own support.
tax_assumptions._parent_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: parent in NYC, 37% federal bracket. Parent's NY/NYC rates do not apply to Kilian's gains (no NY kiddie tax under Form 8615).
tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. Net losses offset gains; up to $3,000 deducts at the own short-term rate. Bracket mode (mode 'brackets') still holds the CA schedule and is not updated.
tax_assumptions._short_term_all_note: Kilian 2026-10-28 card 'Assume short-term on all' (thread 'Fix AMAT target vs sell mismatch'): every holding is assumed sold within the year at the short-term rate, so a trim only pays the same tax H years sooner; band per year = q tau (1 - (1+d)^-H) / H + spread / T. Overrides lot_aware_horizon; false restores it.
tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. Long-term lots keep the T-year rule (years_until_you_would_otherwise_sell, future_rate_on_deferred_gains, Claude defaults 2026-09-28). false restores the T-year rule for every lot.

agents.reasoning: Round 2 (supervisor fact-checks plus a direct read of the AT&T Q3 call transcript, 10-Q R63/R17 and FCC auction notes). Evidence: Q3 2026 revenue $32.3B (+5.3%), adj. EBITDA $12.5B (+5.4%), adj. EPS $0.65, FCF ~$5.0B; 379k postpaid phone adds, churn 0.92%; postpaid phone ARPU +4% from new/refreshed plans and back-book pricing with promotions unchanged (call); fiber ARPU -4% with Q4 similar and "relatively stable ARPU" over 2026-28 (CFO). GAAP EPS $0.12-0.13 carries a $2.6B Mexico impairment and an ~$800M separation charge whose cash lands mainly in 2027. Guides: 2026 EPS ~$2.40, AC EBITDA mid-to-high single digits, consolidated EBITDA 5%+ in 2028, FCF $18B+/$19B+/$21B+, capital investment $22-23B in 2027-28, $24B+ buybacks, 2.5x leverage in 2029. Price moves: Oct 9 (-10.8%) = SpaceX buying Grain's 800 MHz licences (no ex-dividend effect: ex-date Oct 12); Oct 21 (-6.4%) = results day (phone-add miss, capex/working-capital framing), a small earnings-path change; Oct 23 (-8.0%) = Bloomberg report of SpaceX seeking 80,000+ sites, a multiple effect. What changed from round 1: Forged Fiber stake $4,058M x 0.9 (R63) instead of $2.58B; separation cash no longer double-counted in net debt (horizon $147.9B, now linked to driver FCF); wireless ARPU +1.5%/+0.8% (was +0.6%/+0.4%); fiber ARPU -1.0%/+0.5% (was +0.7%/+1.6%); AC EBITDA +6.0%/+6.0%; interest +$0.1B; upper C-band -$5B x 0.35; P/E 8.1x and FCF yield 12.3% held at today's levels (were 8.5x / 12.0%); EPS, FCF/share and horizon net debt are now computed from the drivers through driver_build.set. Peers: Kilian's 12 incumbents on CY2027E, after leases: EV/EBITDA median 5.52x (5.98x ex-DT), P/E 10.55x; AT&T 5.78x / 7.98x on that basis. Result: research target (12m) $23.88 (EV/EBITDA $23.43, P/E $24.37, FCF $24.26); bear $15.15 (price war, 5.3x), bull $29.23 (6.9x). Guidance record: EPS first guides met or beaten 3 of 3 (median +2.7%), FCF floors 3 of 3 (+3.75%); we sit just below the 2027 FCF floor ($18.9B) and the 2028 EBITDA 5% (4.7% ex-Mexico) because of Legacy and fiber ARPU, and above the 2028 EPS floor on buybacks. Ladder: 60% the scenario mixture (lognormal, 15% within-scenario vol), 40% a neutral 28%-vol distribution centred near spot, because the October de-rating came from SpaceX headlines that may continue and momentum is negative; median ~$22.8, P(>= $21) 0.605. All value legs are driver-linked; the dividend and peer-median cross-checks carry zero weight.

Facts fixed: fiber stake now +4,058 x 0.9 as an equity adjustment (R63; round 1 had ~$1.7B in net debt); net debt at the horizon re-derived at 145.4B (Q4 FCF ~6B, 68% of FY27 FCF by Oct-23, three dividends, ~$7B/yr buybacks, NCI/preferred, Mexico x0.9); FCF per share on horizon shares (6,385M); postpaid phone base on reported year-end counts (73.4815M); home-internet FY26 average time-weighted for the Lumen subscribers (14.06M), which lowers fiber ARPU to the -4% the company reports. Model deepened: a sixth driver, the AC EBITDA margin, now sets segment EBIT, and the P/E and FCF legs read EPS and FCF computed from the drivers; Legacy is a plain run-off segment (driven revenue 81%). Industry follow-ups (8 searches/fetches): Verizon steering to the top of its 750k-1M phone-add guide with no free phones (TIKR), Comcast blaming fiber's $30-40 gig pricing for its losses, SpaceX's own plan of rooftop small cells rather than macro towers (Wireless Estimator), and FCC rules forcing the upper C-band auction to close by July 2027 (Light Reading). memo.title: AT&T (T) Long: SpaceX de-rating priced in, cash path intact - target $22.65, research target (12m) $23.16 plus a 5.3% yield
memo.call_reason: The published target ($22.65) is above the $20.93 price and conviction is medium (rubric), with a 5.3% dividend on top and a stop at $16.54 that sits on the $16.5 thesis-break level.
memo.one_liner: AT&T lost ~16% in October on SpaceX headlines (Grain 800 MHz licences, a reported 80,000-site push) while Q3 beat and 2026 EPS was raised; our horizon multiples keep that de-rating and still value the shares at a research target (12m) of $23.16 (+10.6%) on the earnings path alone. We buy 167 shares at or below the page's Entry below (~$21.60), ahead of this week's peer prints and the Oct-29 FCC vote, stop $16.54, take-profit $27.52.

thesis.point: Earnings power is rising, not falling: EPS growth from lower D&A and ~5% a year of buybacks carries value even at today's de-rated multiples.
thesis.evidence: Q3 2026 revenue $32.3B (+5.3%), adjusted EBITDA $12.5B (+5.4%), adjusted EPS $0.65; 2026 EPS guide raised to ~$2.40, mainly on lower depreciation from held-for-sale accounting for Mexico. Our driver build gives adjusted EPS $2.66 (2027) and $2.91 (2028) vs Zacks consensus $2.54 / $2.86; at 8.3x (AT&T's own NTM P/E today) the P/E leg alone is $24.01.

thesis.point: The October drawdown is a multiple event, and we keep it in the target rather than betting on a rebound.
thesis.evidence: Closes fell 24.87 -> 22.18 (-10.8%) on Oct-9 (SpaceX buys Grain's 800 MHz licences), 23.42 -> 21.91 (-6.4%) on results day Oct-21, and 22.74 -> 20.93 (-8.0%) on Oct-23 (Bloomberg: SpaceX seeks 80,000+ sites). The horizon EV/EBITDA stays at the post-news 6.1x (~$2.8/sh of de-rating retained; 6.1x = 5.69x on the peer basis vs an 11-incumbent median of 5.98x ex-DT). SpaceX targets next-generation service by end-2027, so most fourth-carrier cash-flow damage falls after our 2027-10-23 horizon.

thesis.point: Cash returns and asset sales put a floor under the equity.
thesis.evidence: $0.2775 quarterly dividend (5.3% yield at $20.93), $24B+ of buybacks guided for 2026-28, Mexico sale for ~$2.0B cash at closing (Q1 2027) and a 50% fiber JV stake carried at $4,058M (taken at x0.9 = +$3.65B). At the $16.5 thesis break the stock would yield 6.7% and ~15% FCF-to-common at ~5.2x EBITDA on the peer basis, a level consistent only with a broken cash path.

memo.variant_view: We sit between the Street and the options market. Sell-side (24 analysts, Buy) has a median target of $28.00 (mean $27.80, range $20-34), roughly 21% above our research target (12m) of $23.16: we keep the post-SpaceX 6.1x EV/EBITDA and model FCF of $18.5B / $19.9B for 2027-28, below both management's $19B+ / $21B+ floors and consensus ($19.24B / $20.97B), because Legacy EBITDA turns negative after 2027 and wireless ARPU growth fades to +0.75% in 2028. The options market is more bearish than we are: its standalone 12-month median is $21.35 with P(gain) 52.7%, vs our published 60.2%. Our variant view is therefore narrow and specific: EPS (above consensus on lower D&A and buybacks) carries value at a de-rated multiple, so we do not need the SpaceX fear to fade to make money; a move back toward the pre-October ~6.8x would add ~$2.8/sh on top. This is not a large mispricing call; most of the expected return is the dividend plus a modest earnings-path gain.

valuation.methods: Research target (12m) $23.16 = model-engine base horizon value (23.1576) of the supervisor's reconciled driver set (wireless and fiber subs x ARPU, Advanced Connectivity margin, capital investment ~$23.4B/22.8B/22.7B): EV/EBITDA 6.1x on NTM EBITDA ~$50.4B = $22.55 (weight 0.5), P/E 8.3x on driver-linked NTM EPS $2.86 = $24.01 (0.35), 12.3% FCF yield on $2.82/share = $23.19 (0.15); net debt at horizon $144.3B, NCI $18.0B, preferred $2.95B, fiber stake +$3.65B, expected upper C-band spend -$2.0B (-$5B x 0.4), 6,387M shares. No DCF leg (not in the DCF policy for this sector). The five forecasters' values span $22.24-24.39. The published target $22.65 is the median of the final distribution, which blends the options market (weight 0.67, median $21.35) with the research ladder (0.33); expected value $23.42 (+11.9%), P(gain) 60.2%. Bear values $15.15-16.68 (price war, cable-like ~5.2-5.3x), bull values $27.51-29.23 (re-rating toward ~6.8-7.0x).

catalysts.event: Verizon Q3 2026 results (out today)
catalysts.why_it_moves: First big read on wireless pricing after the SpaceX news; Verizon has been buying share. It reported 406k postpaid phone net adds (vs 44k a year ago, and above AT&T's 379k), raised its 2026 phone-add guide to 1.1-1.2M and cut promotional acquisition cost 41% y/y.
catalysts.watch: Whether share gains came from price (bad for T) or lower subsidies (good for industry pricing); any call comment on SpaceX or satellite; T's reaction vs VZ today.

catalysts.event: FOMC rate decisions
catalysts.why_it_moves: A 5.3%-yield, 3.1x-levered stock trades partly as a bond proxy; the forecasters flagged a ~5% 10-year yield and few cuts priced as a cap on yield-stock multiples.
catalysts.watch: 10-year Treasury yield after each decision; a dovish turn helps the multiple, a hawkish one hurts it.

catalysts.event: T-Mobile Q3 2026 results (call 4:30 p.m. ET)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Second wireless read-across in three days and T-Mobile's SpaceX commentary (it is SpaceX's existing direct-to-cell partner); TMUS fell more than T on the SpaceX headlines.
catalysts.watch: Postpaid phone adds and churn, promotional intensity, any statement on SpaceX site access or wholesale talks.

catalysts.event: FCC October open meeting: NPRM to modernize Supplemental Coverage from Space rules (+482 MHz for satellite-to-device)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Widening satellite access to terrestrial bands lowers the barrier for Starlink Mobile; AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile have lobbied to keep carrier consent and to exclude 2.5/3.45 GHz. Agenda items are tentative until the meeting.
catalysts.watch: Whether the adopted NPRM keeps carrier consent and which bands are proposed; it is a proposal, not a final rule.

catalysts.event: Charter Q3 2026 results
catalysts.why_it_moves: Broadband and cable-MVNO read-across: cable losses to fiber support AT&T fiber adds, but cable has called fiber pricing 'irrational' and AT&T fiber ARPU fell 4% in Q3.
catalysts.watch: Charter broadband net losses, mobile line adds, pricing response to fiber overbuild.

catalysts.event: Any signed SpaceX cell-site access deal (Bloomberg-reported talks for 80,000+ sites)
catalysts.why_it_moves: A signed deal is the step that turns a satellite service into a terrestrial fourth carrier; each SpaceX headline this month cost T 8-11% in a day.
catalysts.watch: Tower-company announcements, site counts and lease terms; any SpaceX US pricing; any wholesale or partner deal with an incumbent instead (would be +).

catalysts.event: Quarterly dividend declaration (last year on 2025-12-15; record date ~mid-Jan 2027)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Confirms the $0.2775 payout that underpins the 5.3% yield; a hold is expected, any change would be a major signal.
catalysts.watch: Amount held at $0.2775; any new buyback authorization alongside.

catalysts.event: AT&T Q4 2026 results and 2027 outlook (first print under the new CFO from 2027-01-01; last year's Q4 print was 2026-01-28)
catalysts.why_it_moves: The single biggest scheduled event: management promised more color on the 2027 FCF bridge to $19B+; we model $18.5B, so a firm bridge is upside and a soft one confirms our below-floor view.
catalysts.watch: 2027 FCF guide vs $19B+, capital investment $22-23B, buyback pace vs $24B+ 2026-28, Q4 postpaid phone adds vs Q3's 379k, fiber ARPU (guided ~-4% in Q4), separation cash.

catalysts.event: Mexico wireless sale closes (~$2.0B cash at closing)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Cash to net debt and leases leave the balance sheet; small but supports the deleveraging story.
catalysts.watch: Closing announcement and proceeds vs ~$2.0B.

catalysts.event: FCC review and closing of SpaceX's purchase of Grain's 800 MHz licences (expected H1 2027)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Approval with terrestrial flexibility would firm up the fourth-carrier case; conditions or delay would ease it.
catalysts.watch: FCC conditions on terrestrial use, carrier petitions, closing date.

catalysts.event: AT&T Q1 2027 results (Q1 2026 was reported 2026-04-22)
catalysts.why_it_moves: First quarter of 2027 pricing and the Legacy decline; tests whether ARPU growth holds once 2026 price actions lap.
catalysts.watch: Postpaid phone ARPU growth vs our +1.6% for 2027, churn vs 0.92%, Q1 FCF seasonality.

catalysts.event: FCC Auction 115 (upper C-band, 160 MHz) bidding
catalysts.why_it_moves: We carry -$5B x 0.4 = -$2.0B (-$0.31/sh); heavy AT&T bidding at 3.13x leverage would hit net debt before the horizon and could slow buybacks.
catalysts.watch: Qualified-bidder list, AT&T commentary on participation, SpaceX as a bidder.

catalysts.event: Composite Fiber 37 JV with GIP/CPP closes (50% stake)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Crystallises the fiber stake we carry at +$3.65B and brings proceeds for debt reduction.
catalysts.watch: Proceeds (undisclosed so far) and any payments AT&T owes the JV for network access.

risks.risk: SpaceX becomes a priced, national fourth carrier (Grain 800 MHz + EchoStar spectrum + leased terrestrial sites); supervisor probability 0.35 over 2028-2031, and the market can price it well before then (bear values $15.15-16.68).
risks.signpost: A signed site-lease deal for tens of thousands of towers; FCC approval of the Grain licences with terrestrial rights; a US price list for Starlink Mobile; Polymarket odds of a US carrier by end-2027 rising from 34.5% (thin market).

risks.risk: Free cash flow misses the floors and buybacks slow: we already sit below management ($18.5B vs $19B+ in 2027), and the 2025 tax-law cash benefit runs off after 2027.
risks.signpost: Q4 print guides 2027 FCF below $19B or capital investment above $23B; buyback pace below the ~$24B+ 2026-28 plan.

risks.risk: Wireless price competition: Verizon is taking share (406k Q3 phone adds, guide raised to 1.1-1.2M) while AT&T adds slowed to 379k; fiber ARPU is already -4% y/y.
risks.signpost: AT&T postpaid phone adds below ~300k a quarter, churn above 1.0%, postpaid phone ARPU growth falling from +4% toward +1%, rising promotions on the Q4 call.

risks.risk: Balance sheet: 3.13x leverage with the 2.5x target pushed to 2029, a Fitch BBB+ Negative Outlook, $9.5B of debt due within a year and possible ~$5B upper C-band spend.
risks.signpost: A Fitch downgrade, AT&T qualifying to bid heavily in Auction 115, refinancing at materially higher coupons.

trade.entry: Buy at or below the Price Targets page's Entry below (~$21.60 at the 2026-10-23 run; spot $20.93 is under it), in one order for the full 167 shares as the page's next-share table shows (no tranche pacing under the book's rules). trade.exit_or_add: Exit at the $16.54 stop (15th percentile, just above the $16.5 thesis break) or on a signed national-scale SpaceX site deal combined with a 2027 FCF guide below $19B. Take profit at $27.52 (+31.5%; 43.6% modelled chance of touching it vs 35.2% for the stop). No room to add above the 15% ceiling. The supervisor's own sizing view was more cautious (4-6% in two tranches); the book's joint mean-variance sizing takes it to the 15% name cap. Material SpaceX site-deal news before the order fills holds the buy for re-research. [Updated 2026-11-24: the one upside exit is now $24.67, where the 12-month expected value no longer beats the 4% cash sleeve and the model sells every share; any other take-profit figure in this memo is superseded.]
trade.take_profit_note: expected value: the price where the 12-month expected return (research fixed in dollars, options leg moving with the price) falls to the 4% cash rate (full exit) (as of 2026-11-24)

what_changes_our_mind: A signed SpaceX terrestrial site deal at national scale (tens of thousands of towers) or FCC approval of the Grain licences with full terrestrial flexibility before mid-2027: move to No position.
The late-January Q4 print guides 2027 FCF below $19B, slows the $24B+ buyback plan, or shows postpaid phone adds below ~300k with ARPU growth fading: exit.

Upside case: SpaceX talks end in a wholesale/partner deal with incumbents and AT&T holds +4% phone ARPU with adds back above 400k; the multiple can revert toward ~6.8x (~+$2.8/sh), so we would hold through the take-profit review rather than trim.

(2) Net debt now includes supplier finance $393.1M (10-Q, in accounts payable): 3,383.3. (3) NCI at market (-488: 9M NCI earnings $20.0M annualised x 18.3x) and the asbestos plan balance (-275 = $545M plan - $270M QSF, 10-K) as adjustments; the supervisor's extra -197.5 x 0.4 court estimate is not in the 10-K and is left out. Where I disagree: the supervisor says 'Q4 incrementals north of 25%' is not in the transcript; the TradingKey transcript (source 4) has the CEO saying 'our incremental leverage in the fourth quarter, we're projecting to be north of our target range' (target 25%+) - I re-cite it to source 4 and keep it, while taking the FY 'low 20s' cut into the Americas path (+30bp FY27, ~23.8% reported incrementals). Guidance record: every first annual EPS guide FY23-26 beaten (median +5.8%); FY26 incremental target missed. The net effect of the fixes is small (443.6 -> 442.9): removing the haircut, the lower tax and the share count lift the P/E leg, supplier finance/NCI/asbestos and the lower EV/EBITDA multiple take it back. Downside (P10) = data-center order pause + margin -200bp + de-rate to the peer median; upside (P90) = faster burn, 25%+ incrementals, multiple held. sec.gov refuses scripted access without a contact email, so filings were read with WebFetch. agents.reasoning: Cause of today's drop (verified): BLS released September CPI at 08:30 ET 2026-10-14 (+0.6% m/m, +3.7% y/y; core +0.3% m/m, +2.6% y/y); Reuters reported an AI-infrastructure rout; the IPPs fell together (VST -6.7%, CEG -5.6%, TLN -6.2%, NRG -5.9%) while SPY fell ~1.2% and XLU ~0.4%; EDGAR shows no Vistra 8-K since 2026-10-05. So the move is sector-wide (AI-power factor) triggered by a market-wide macro print, not company news, and does not change fair value. PJM thesis-break flag: open, not tripped; I read PJM's ER26-1556 answer myself: a 'limited extension' through 2029/30, with the 2030/31+ path to be set after an end-2026 stakeholder evaluation; no filing to extend or lower the cap. Round-2 changes after the supervisor's review: Cogentrix's $3.8B now fully in the horizon bridge (net debt incl. preferred $22.96B, built from FCFbG guidance and the call's capital-allocation plan); FY2028 EBITDA cut from $9.0B (thin FMP consensus) to $8.5B; FY2027 raised to the sourced $8.1B (unsourced $0.2B haircut dropped); multiple 10.0x -> 9.5x (below VST's ~9.9x today, 1.1x under the IPP median); P/E leg dropped; shares from the 335.6M cover count; SBC counted once as dilution; Cogentrix ~$0.7B tax NPV added (x0.9). memo.title: VST: small, staged long into the Q4 catalyst cluster; ~9% to a $150.54 target on 2027 EBITDA roll-forward, not re-rating
memo.call_reason: Target $150.54 is above the $138.02 price with medium conviction and no special situation, but the edge is thin (P(gain) 0.57) so size is capped at 5 shares and entry is staged around the Q3 guide.
memo.one_liner: At ~9x pro-forma 2027 EBITDA of ~$8.15B, VST is priced for the contracted nuclear/PJM book with no credit for ERCOT recovery; formalizing the 2027 guide and a cap-level PJM auction should carry it to ~$151 research target (12m). The Street at ~$219 is paying for an 11x re-rating we don't underwrite, and the stock sits only ~$33 above the $105 thesis-break level at 45-49% vol, so we buy small and add on the print.

thesis.point: 2027 EBITDA of ~$8.1B is largely locked: the low end of the $7.4-7.8B opportunity plus ~$0.7B from Cogentrix and the Meta premium, with 2027 ~94% hedged.
thesis.evidence: CFO on the Q2 call: 2027 'trending towards the lower end' and Cogentrix plus Meta 'add roughly $700 million'; hedges 100%/94%/72% for 2026/27/28. EIA's September STEO held 2027 ERCOT generation at ~527 TWh and raised 2027 ERCOT North to $34.30/MWh, so the August load-growth cut did not extend.

thesis.point: At ~$138 the stock trades at ~9x forward EBITDA, only ~1.8 turns above the 7.25x plain gas-fleet M&A mark, so the contracted nuclear (Meta 2.6 GW PJM, AWS 1.2 GW Comanche Peak) and PJM capacity at the $325 cap are cheaply valued.
thesis.evidence: Cogentrix bought at 7.25x 2027 EBITDA; PJM 2028/29 BRA cleared at the $325/MW-day cap (10,924 MW for Vistra) and the collar extends through 2029/30; ~$23.5B net debt plus preferred and ~337M diluted shares give ~$105 at 7.2x.

thesis.point: Insiders and the balance sheet are supportive: the CEO bought in the open market after the drawdown, and the preferred is being refinanced into cheaper junior notes rather than equity.
thesis.evidence: CEO Form 4 purchases Aug 24 and Aug 31-Sep 1, 2026; $1.5B 7.000%/7.250% junior subordinated notes (Sep 24) fund redemption of the 8.0% Series A and 7.0% Series B preferred at their resets. Offset: the CFO sold 20,000 shares at $151.03 under a 10b5-1 plan.

memo.variant_view: Versus the Street we are the bear: our $150.54 target is ~31% below the weighted analyst median of $218.97 (17 analysts, low $169 Mizuho, high $298). Street targets need ~11x EBITDA or ~$8.5B+ 2028 EBITDA, which requires ERCOT forwards to turn and new hyperscaler deals; with ~28% of 2028 unhedged into a curve still falling in late September, we don't underwrite that. Versus the options market we are only modestly more constructive: the market-implied median is $141.57 with P(gain) 0.52, against our $150.54 and 0.57; our edge is the belief that the Q3 guide formalizes ~$8.1B and that the EIA Texas load cut is already in the price. That is a small variant view, not a big one, and it is why the position is small.

valuation.methods: Supervisor blend, same as the five agents' mean ($150.9; range $145-156): (1) 9.0x ~$8.15B forward EBITDA = ~$73.4B EV, less ~$23.5B net debt plus preferred, over 337M diluted shares = ~$148 (50% weight); (2) ~$13.9/share FCF before growth at a 9% yield = ~$154 (30%); (3) ~13.5x ~$11.1 forward EPS = ~$150 (20%). Blend ~$151. The published 12-month target ($150.54) is the median of the combined options-market and agent distribution; expected value is $170.65 because of the fat right tail (q75 $206.50). Each 0.25x on the multiple is ~$6/share; the $8.1B vs $8.25B EBITDA dispute is ~$2.7/share.

catalysts.why_it_moves: Clearing prices near the cap would confirm scarcity value in PJM and data-center-paid capacity; a weak outcome or political cost-allocation fights would pressure the PJM story ahead of the BRA.
catalysts.watch: Procured MW vs the 6,831 MW target and the clearing price relative to $325 and $555/MW-day.

catalysts.event: Series A preferred first reset / earliest redemption date (8.0% rate ends); Series B reset in Dec 2026

catalysts.watch: Redemption notice/8-K for the full $1.0B Series A; no equity issuance.

catalysts.event: FOMC rate decision
catalysts.why_it_moves: IPP multiples compressed as the 10-year approached 5%; VST is a levered, high-multiple name, so a hawkish surprise hits it harder than the market.
catalysts.watch: Hike vs hold and the 10-year's reaction; a move back above 5% is a multiple headwind.

catalysts.why_it_moves: This is the event that formalizes (or breaks) the ~$8.1B 2027 base the whole valuation sits on, and gives the first read on 2028 hedging.
catalysts.watch: 2027 guide at or above ~$8.1B incl. ~$0.7B Cogentrix+Meta (below $7.4B low end is a thesis hit); 2028 hedge % and price; buyback pace; any new hyperscaler contract; whether guidance waits for the Cogentrix close.

catalysts.why_it_moves: Unlocks ~5.5 GW of gas and the Cogentrix share of the $0.7B EBITDA add; a slip delays the formal 2027 guide.
catalysts.watch: Closing 8-K; 5M shares issued to seller; $1.5B assumed debt.

catalysts.event: ERCOT files the Batch Zero Eligibility Verification and Community Impact Review reports (governor-ordered data-center audit); energization of new 75 MW+ loads paused until then
catalysts.why_it_moves: Determines how much of the Texas large-load queue is real, which drives the ERCOT load-growth narrative and the 2028 forward curve on VST's open volume.
catalysts.watch: Share of the ~128 GW studied load that survives; restart date for Batch Zero and energizations; any new PUCT rules for large loads or co-location.

catalysts.date: mid-Dec 2026 (agents cite 2026-12-15 close; PJM confirms December)
catalysts.event: PJM 2029/2030 Base Residual Auction under the $325 cap / $175 floor collar
catalysts.why_it_moves: Sets East capacity revenue for June 2029 onward; a fourth cap-level clear supports the out-year story (adds nothing to NTM EBITDA).
catalysts.watch: Clearing price vs $325 cap; reserve shortfall; any talk of extending the collar or more affordability intervention.

catalysts.event: Texas 90th Legislature convenes (session through late May 2027)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Bills on large-load limits, data-center cost allocation or co-location could cut the ERCOT demand story that underpins 2028+ pricing.
catalysts.watch: Filed bills on large-load interconnection, curtailment or co-location; committee hearings in Feb-Mar.

catalysts.event: Q4 2026 results: first 2028 outlook and updated hedge levels (~72% hedged as of Aug 2026)
catalysts.why_it_moves: The 2028 view tells us whether EBITDA grows past 2027 or rolls over as the open ~28% re-hedges at weaker ERCOT forwards; it sets the NTM base at our horizon.
catalysts.watch: 2028 opportunity range vs ~$8.1-8.2B; hedge % and realized prices; buyback authorization.

risks.risk: The Q3 guide lands below the $7.4B low end plus $0.7B, or the 2028 view comes in below 2027, as the ~28% open 2028 volume is re-hedged into weak ERCOT forwards.
risks.signpost: ERCOT 2027/2028 forwards keep falling week over week (they were down ~2.0%/1.7% in the week of Sep 21); management language shifts from 'lower end' to 'below the range'; continued downward EPS revisions.

risks.risk: Texas large-load demand disappoints: the Dec 10 audit culls much of the queue and the 2027 legislature restricts data-center interconnection, cementing the ~$30-34/MWh ERCOT curve.
risks.signpost: Audit reports show a large share of the 128 GW studied load ineligible; Batch Zero restart pushed to late 2027; another EIA STEO cut to Texas load growth (August already cut 2027 to 6% from 14%).

risks.risk: Sector de-rating: IPPs trade as a group on AI-power sentiment and rates; a hyperscaler capex pause or a 10-year above 5% compresses the multiple toward the 7.25x gas-fleet mark (~$105).
risks.signpost: CEG/NRG/TLN falling together with VST; hyperscaler capex guidance cuts; 10-year sustained above 5%.

risks.risk: PJM political intervention: extended or tighter price caps, data-center cost allocation or backstop design that caps East capacity value.
risks.signpost: White House/governor pressure for lower caps, a FERC order changing the collar beyond 2029/30, or the backstop procurement clearing far below cap.

trade.position: 5 sh (~$690, 6.9% of the $10,000 book); binding limit is the supervisor's 7% cap for overlap with the AI-power driver in META/GOOGL
trade.entry: Staged per the supervisor: buy ~3 sh now at ~$138, add the last ~2 sh after the Q3 call (calendars: Nov 5) only if the 2027 guide is at or above ~$8.1B incl. Cogentrix and Meta; hold the second tranche if the guide is below the $7.4B low end or Cogentrix has not closed.
trade.exit_or_add: Exit on a close below $104.94 (the ~$105 thesis break, ~7.2x EBITDA = gas-fleet M&A mark) or on a 2027 guide below $7.4B + $0.7B. Take profit at $206.50 (q75; ~11x, where the Street already is). Add the second tranche on a clean Q3 guide; consider going above the cap only with a new hyperscaler contract or a Dec 10 audit that clears most Batch Zero load. Expected loss at stop ~$165.

what_changes_our_mind: Q3 call guides 2027 below ~$7.9B including Cogentrix and Meta, or signals 2028 below 2027 (bearish: exit).
ERCOT 2028 forwards fall another ~10% into year-end or the Dec 10 audit/2027 legislature materially restricts large loads (bearish: cut).
A new hyperscaler contract (Comanche Peak expansion or a gas-backed PPA) plus a clean audit that reopens Batch Zero (bullish: lift target toward the Street and add above 7%).

invested_cash.meaning: dollar gain on stocks (price, dividends, realized and unrealized) / average dollars in stocks; SPY and equal weight = the same dollars on the same days in them instead

live_book.spy_basis: price plus distributions reinvested on the ex-date (dividends.json); no adjusted closes in the data
live_book.dividends_missing_note: names not in dividends.json are treated as paying nothing
live_book.note: 38 trading days of returns cannot show skill: daily stock returns swing by about 1-2%, so a gap of a few percent over a few weeks is well within luck. rough_se treats days as independent; read the gaps as what happened, not as evidence, until there are many months. Whole book: time-weighted, cash at the T-bill, vs fully invested SPY and equal weight. Invested cash: dollar-weighted on the stock sleeve, vs the same dollars in SPY and equal weight.
